PART II - PUBLIC LAND, TENURE, TOWNSITES & SETTLEMENT RIGHTS

2.1 Public-land entry is a legal relationship, not instant ownership

CANON LOCK - Homestead, Timber Culture, Desert Land and other dated public-land programs create different entry rights,
obligations, evidence and eventual title outcomes. Filing may grant a lawful claim/possession basis without patented title.
Actual residence, cultivation, improvement, tree survival or reclamation requirements must be evaluated from world history
and LegalRegime data.

2.2 Land-status mosaic

The world can contain unperfected claims, patented farms, railroad/company land, private speculative holdings, leases,
tax-sale interests, mortgages, estates, federal land, treaty/reservation land and disputed or unknown title simultaneously.
Property UI may expose only what the actor legitimately knows. Promotional maps and visually vacant terrain never override
the right-holder state.

2.3 Railroad/townsite land promotion and paper towns

Railroads and townsite companies may market land because settlement generates future traffic. They may plat a depot town,
advertise exaggerated prospects, grant favorable terms or organize land-seeker excursions. A promoted town may fail. Lots
and brochures create opportunities and expectations, not automatic households, businesses or institutions.



                                                    LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 027/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXIX / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                                                7



2.4 Farm tenure beyond owner-operation

By the late campaign, owner-operator, cash tenant, share tenant and part-owner/operator are all valid rural arrangements.
Share tenancy is a farming/operating relationship, not wage employment. Landlord, operator, equipment owner and crop
owner/share claimant may be different parties according to the lease.

2.5 Indigenous land chronology requires exact geography

The Black Hills and other Indigenous/federal geographies cannot be treated as ordinary vacant land. The 1868 treaty
context, 1874 gold expedition/rush, federal conflict and later taking/allotment policies are date- and place-specific. Dawes-
era allotment requires a separate research-backed authoring record for the affected reservation/community; no generic
OpenReservationLand event is permitted.

PART III - TRANSPORT CORRIDORS, RAILHEAD ECONOMIES & SERVICE CHANGE

3.1 Route value can be temporary

A stage, freight, mail or construction-front corridor can generate large but temporary traffic. The Bismarck-Deadwood route
and end-of-track towns are controlling examples: equipment, horses, employees, hotels, liveries and merchant demand can
rationally expand, then collapse or relocate when the rail network changes.

3.2 Crossings and service stages are distinct

CANON LOCK - A rail line reaching a river is not the same as an all-weather bridge connection. Ferry transfer, seasonal
ice crossing, temporary transfer track and permanent bridge must remain distinct route/service states where the geography
justifies them. Each changes capacity, delay, cost and reliability independently.

3.3 Rail bypass and supply-network opportunity

A bypass can redirect freight, hotel traffic, institutions and property demand without explicitly deleting the bypassed town.
Conversely, a settlement can profit from a distant boom as an outfitting/supply node even when the resource itself lies
elsewhere. Network position, not local resource labels, creates the opportunity.

3.4 Rail regulation and claims

The Interstate Commerce Act of 1887 changes published tariff/rate/classification evidence and the legality of specified
rebates/preferences while creating formal complaint/damages avenues. Carrier disputes over lost/damaged freight, livestock,
right-of-way or contract performance use ordinary claims and legal processes, not a generic service-quality penalty.

PART IV - ENVIRONMENTAL, BIOLOGICAL & INFRASTRUCTURE SHOCKS

4.1 Horse-power dependency and the 1872 epizootic

CANON LOCK - Draft capacity belongs to healthy usable animals, not wagons alone. A widespread equine outbreak may
leave freight assets, stages, farm machinery and fire equipment physically present but unable to operate. Replacement
horses, rest, veterinary care and prioritization become real scarcity decisions.

4.2 Weather shocks act through physical state

The Long Winter, 1881 Missouri flooding/ice jams, the 1888 blizzard, drought and other severe weather events remain
authoring anchors for route closure, livestock/feed stress, building damage, inventory shortage and worker exposure. The
event is not an outcome card; affected objects and networks determine consequence.

4.3 Fire, locust and compound failure

Locust/grasshopper outbreaks damage crops/forage geographically.  Prairie fire uses fuel, wind, ignition and suppres-
sion/backfire capacity. Town fire uses building material, spacing, ignition and response. Multiple weak seasons/events can
compound until a household/business/settlement chooses to leave without any forced ghost-town transition.

4.4 Water projects can succeed or fail

Wells, pumping windmills, artesian drilling, irrigation ditches and municipal/private waterworks are Project/Property/Utility
investments. Drilling can consume capital without useful yield. Successful access can expand viable settlement/ranching



                                                    LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 028/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXIX / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                                                8



geography and fire/sanitation capacity.

PART V - INFORMATION, COMMUNICATIONS, MAIL & MARKET KNOWLEDGE

5.1 Information latency is historical gameplay

CANON LOCK - True world state and actor knowledge remain separate. Mail, messenger, newspaper, railway mail, telegraph,
telephone, commercial reports, fairs and traveling salesmen differ in speed, cost, reach and reliability. Better communications
narrow delay and uncertainty; they do not grant omniscience or a universal management bonus.

5.2 Postal and express financial/logistics services

Postal money orders, telegraph money transfer where available, railway mail, private express and COD can support distant
trade before local banking and parcel-post systems mature. The payment instrument and the goods shipment are separate
obligations and can arrive at different times.

5.3 Mail order and the Sears anachronism guard

Montgomery Ward-era mail order is valid inside the campaign as a supplier-discovery/order channel. Heavy goods still
move by express/rail/wagon. Rural Free Delivery arrives late and changes mail access more than heavy-goods logistics.
Sears kit houses begin in 1908 and therefore must not appear during the normal 1870-1905 horizon; earlier freight of
lumber/components remains valid.

5.4 Weather and market information

Federal weather observations/forecasts and telegraphed commodity quotations create dated evidence. A person can receive
yesterday’s newspaper price, a faster telegraph price or no outside quote at all. Local price formation still depends on actual
local supply, buyers, transport and contracts.

5.5 Commercial credit information

R.G. Dun-style commercial reports and later formal bank reporting/examination allow distant counterparties to obtain evidence
about business standing. Such reports are dated, partial and potentially stale. They can support credit decisions without
giving the creditor direct access to the simulation truth.

PART VI - RURAL PRODUCTION, AGRICULTURAL SERVICES & MARKET INSTI-
TUTIONS

6.1 Mechanization creates service and consumable economies

Bonanza farms demonstrate that annualized staffing and peak harvest concurrency can differ enormously. Custom thresh-
ing/reaping outfits, implement dealers, repair shops and seasonal crews can serve many farms. Machinery creates demand
for draft animals, fuel where applicable, parts, twine, skilled operation, freight and maintenance rather than becoming a
one-time productivity unlock.

6.2 Fencing, water and winter resilience

Barbed wire, wells and windmills change actual stock control and watered acreage. Ranch survival through the 1886-87
winter depends on stocking, condition, shelter, hay/forage and weather. Investments reduce specific vulnerabilities rather
than raising a generic RanchResilience stat.

6.3 Grain grading, elevators, receipts and futures

CANON LOCK - Grain custody, ownership, grade, weight, storage receipt and sale remain separable. A warehouse/elevator
may own purchased grain while merely holding other grain for depositors. Warehouse receipts can represent claims and may
be transferable/pledgeable where law permits. Terminal-market/futures information can influence elevator bids and hedging
without replacing physical local commerce.

6.4 Dairy cooperation and testing

Cooperative creameries can aggregate milk and capital to justify separators and other processing equipment. Babcock-
era butterfat testing changes payment evidence and farmer incentives. The organization, equipment, member farms and



                                                    LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 029/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXIX / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                                                9



transactions remain separate economic entities/relationships.

6.5 Agricultural information and temporary markets

Experiment-station bulletins, agricultural fairs, stock shows, seed catalogs and machinery demonstrations are informa-
tion/commercial channels. Awards can become evidence about animals/products. Seed firms may serve broad territories
through catalog/mail/rail and should preserve variety/source suitability rather than a generic SeedQuality score.

6.6 Finite rural side-economies

Buffalo-bone collection is a controlling example of a temporary exhaustible rural trade. Physical resource availability supports
collectors, buyers and freight until the stock is depleted, after which the business must move, pivot or close.

PART VII - WHOLESALE COMMERCE, TRAVELING SALES & MERCHANT NET-
WORKS

7.1 Regional wholesaling is a real middle layer

CANON LOCK - Manufacturer -> regional jobber/wholesaler -> local merchant is an ordinary supply chain. Regional hubs
such as Omaha, Sioux City, Minneapolis/St. Paul and Chicago may differ by product, route, price and lead time. A merchant
is not assumed to buy every line directly from the original manufacturer.

7.2 Traveling salesmen and sample rooms

A wholesaler representative may physically travel a rail/stage circuit, stay at a hotel, store/display samples, visit merchants,
negotiate terms and take orders. The visit creates information and commitments. The actual goods arrive later through a
shipment. Hotels can therefore participate in business-to-business commerce rather than serving only overnight travelers.

7.3 Implement dealers and supplier lines

Implement/hardware dealers can carry multiple product lines and commercial capabilities. Manufacturer relationships
influence stock, credit, warranties/repairs, parts and replacement lead time. One business may combine implements,
hardware, lumber, grain buying or livestock trade when actual people/assets/premises support it.

7.4 Collection and trade-credit continuity

A remote supplier can use correspondence, local attorneys/agents and secured remedies to collect frontier debt. Default
can lead to workout, revised terms, demand for security, lawsuit or foreclosure rather than instant write-off or repossession.
Liberal credit can increase sales and bad-debt exposure simultaneously.

PART VIII - FINANCE, INSURANCE, INSOLVENCY & DISTRESSED ASSETS

8.1 Multiple credit institutions

Commercial banks, private lenders, merchant credit, building-and-loan associations, manufacturer notes and coopera-
tive/mutual arrangements can coexist. Financial instruments keep their own rights, collateral, payment schedules and creditor
identities rather than merging into one Debt object.

8.2 Secured personal-property finance

CANON LOCK - Chattel mortgages/security interests attach to identified movable property only when the dated legal regime
supports the instrument and requirements. Default does not transfer unrelated assets. Future-crop collateral must obey the
law in force; the 1889 Dakota example is a warning against assuming universal enforceability.

8.3 Insurance is balance-sheet risk transfer

Fire, hail and mutual insurance policies create premiums/assessments, reserves, coverage limits and claims. Physical loss
occurs first. Concentrated disasters can threaten the insurer itself. Insurance payment does not restore destroyed property or
crops.





                                                    LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 030/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXIX / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                                               10



8.4 Distress and insolvency have multiple pathways

Workout, private liquidation, mortgage/chattel foreclosure, judgment execution/sheriff sale, tax sale, assignment, estate
process and bankruptcy are distinct. The 1878-1898 federal bankruptcy gap is a material campaign condition; the 1898 Act
adds a later federal route but does not create modern Chapter 7/11 behavior.

8.5 Distressed assets remain ordinary market objects

Foreclosed farms, machinery, livestock, stores and industrial plants remain physical assets with condition, tenants, encum-
brances, redemption rights and carrying costs. Distress can create opportunity but does not guarantee a discount or clean
title.

PART IX - COOPERATIVES, INSTITUTIONS, UTILITIES & SETTLEMENT ORGANI-
ZATION

9.1 Cooperative/mutual capital formation

CANON LOCK - A cooperative or mutual is an ownership/governance pattern, not a bonus type. Members may pool capital
because they need a shared service such as cream processing, grain storage/marketing, insurance, housing finance or
telephone connectivity. The organization owns its assets/cash and contracts separately from the members.

9.2 County seats, capitals and institutional relocation

Courthouses, county seats and state-capital contests create real legal traffic, records access, construction, lodging, land
speculation and public debt. Institutions can relocate; supporting economic activity should move or decay through actual
journeys/businesses rather than a permanent AdministrativeCenter modifier.

9.3 Utilities may be public, private or mixed

Water, irrigation, electric light/power and telephone systems can be privately capitalized, cooperative, municipal or mixed
according to local law and finance. Incorporation/franchise only creates authority/organization; physical plant, connections
and capacity still have to be built and maintained.

9.4 Corporate and communal diversity

Territorial incorporation records should calibrate the variety of real organizations, including banks, elevators, utilities, insurers
and agricultural associations. Communal organizations such as Hutterite colonies must  fit the same general owner-
ship/governance framework without erasing Person/family identity.

9.5 Migration promotion and chain networks

Railroad, territorial, county and private immigration campaigns create advertising, correspondence and leads. Kinship,
religious/community and language networks can lower information, travel and initial-housing barriers. Ethnicity is never
converted into an economic-stat bonus.

    pre-1913                Express companies / COD              Heavy parcels and valuable shipments often use private express rather than ordinary mail. COD,

   1896 onward             Rural Free Delivery                RFD changes information/mail accessibility and household trip patterns but does not teleport
                                                                    merchandise. Local rollout is route-specific and late-period.

PART XI - ACCEPTANCE DOCTRINE, RESEARCH HOLDS & SUPERSESSION

11.1 Acceptance rules

 • A drought, panic, blizzard, epizootic, fire, flood or locust outbreak must first change physical/economic drivers; market
  outcomes follow from ordinary systems.

 • A farther-west scenario can receive rail earlier than an eastern one when actual corridor chronology supports it. No West
  = Later Rail rule is allowed.

 • A public-land filer can possess/use land without yet holding patent; sale, mortgage and inheritance rights depend on the
   actual interest and law.

 • A railhead business can be rational and profitable before becoming stranded by route change. The game must not protect
   the player from historically plausible network risk.

 • A mail-order purchase cannot enter inventory until payment/acceptance and physical fulfillment occur.

 • A town can have telegraph/telephone/weather-service access while many residents/businesses remain unconnected or
   receive information late.

 • A distant wholesaler can deny or extend credit based on incomplete third-party evidence without seeing true hidden player
   finances.

 • Stored grain can be physically inside an elevator while owned by a depositor; warehouse custody cannot silently become
    title.



                                                    LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 034/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXIX / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                                               14



 • A cooperative can own expensive equipment while members remain independent farms/households/businesses.

 • Foreclosure, tax sale, sheriff sale and bankruptcy cannot be collapsed into one DistressedSale state when surviving rights
    differ.

 • Sears kit houses cannot appear before 1908 in the normal 1870-1905 historical envelope.

11.2 Research/calibration holds

 • Exact homestead/Timber Culture/Desert Land/Dawes procedure by county, land district and date beyond the general legal
   structure.

 • Exact railroad-land sale terms, immigration-agent budgets, townsite lot prices and promotional conversion rates.

 • Quantitative probabilities/severity for the 1872 epizootic, grasshoppers, drought, prairie fire, flood, blizzard and cattle-winter
   events.

 • Exact Bismarck-Deadwood traffic by date, individual stage-company rates, schedules and asset rosters beyond the cited
   anchor evidence.

 • Artisan/utility/telephone/water adoption rates by settlement size and year; artesian drilling costs and failure distributions.

 • Express/COD tariffs, postal-money-order office coverage, RFD route effects and telephone subscription prices by
   date/place.

 • Warehouse charges, grain-grade discounts, inspection rules and actual hedging/futures use by Dakota elevators.

 • Cooperative creamery capital structures, patronage/distribution practice, Babcock adoption and separator prices by
    locality/year.

 • Building-and-loan dues/loan conventions, chattel-mortgage notice/perfection rules, tax-redemption periods and execution
   practice by jurisdiction.

 • Insurance premiums/reserves/assessment structures for fire, hail and mutual companies and how catastrophic concentra-
   tion affected failures.

 • Wholesale jobber/dealer catalogs, discounts, credit terms, manufacturer lines, sample-room rents and drummer circuits by
   hub/year.

 • Farm lease/share-contract templates, obligations for seed/equipment/fencing/repairs and exact tenancy prevalence below
   state level.

 • Indigenous land, allotment and agricultural-knowledge treatment requires community-, treaty- and reservation-specific
   research before detailed mechanics are locked.

 • Complete extraction of Dakota territorial incorporation records and Sanborn maps into quantitative generator datasets.

11.3 Supersession/deepening map

Revision XXIX deepens Revision XXV historical-envelope doctrine, Revision XXVI property/market/evidence doctrine, Revision
XXVII catchment/workforce doctrine and Revision XXVIII construction/project doctrine. Existing HistoricalRegime, Dated-
HistoricalEvent, LegalRegime, PropertyRight, Agreement, Finance, Insurance, Institution, Logistics, Information/Evidence,
Person/Household, Business/CommercialCapability and Project authorities remain active. This revision does not create a
parallel historical-events economy.

         REVISION XXVIII

     Construction, Contracting & Project Delivery Integration:
  Delivery Structures, Estimating, Resource Execution, Payment,
                  Change, Default & Claims

                                      Revision date: October 5, 2026

               Source baseline: Canonical Project Bible Revision XXVII - September 26, 2026

  New source integrated: Construction, Contracting & Project Delivery Research Passes I-III - October 2026

                                           Status: Active integration


 PRESERVATION GUARANTEE

  REVISION XXVIII preserves Canonical Project Bible Revision XXVII in full except where this integration
   explicitly adds, deepens, clarifies, corrects or supersedes prior wording. The complete Revision XXVII
  document follows unchanged as the preserved historical layer. Where a conflict exists, Revision XXVIII
   controls. Historical prices, wages, crew outputs, contract sums and legal procedures below remain dated
  evidence or calibration unless explicitly promoted to a Canon lock.

 PURPOSE

   Revision XXVIII consolidates the three construction research passes into durable gameplay doctrine. The
  research strongly validates the existing Project, Agreement, WorkPackage, Task, Property, Finance,
   Inventory, Evidence and LegalRegime foundations while deepening delivery structure, bottom-up
   estimating, crew/resource execution, working-capital risk, public procurement, defects, claims, liens, surety
  and recovery after default.

 REVISION XXVIII MASTER DOCTRINE

    - A construction contract promises obligations; it does not purchase guaranteed progress.

    - Construction delivery is compositional: owners may self-perform, hire separate trades, hire a prime
     contractor or use a mixed arrangement according to actual capability, agreement and period practice.

    - Project cost and duration arise from physical scope, materials, labor, methods, logistics, equipment, site
     conditions, information and dependencies rather than universal construction points or cost-per-area
     formulas.

    - Estimate, bid/proposal, Agreement, approved Baseline, Current Forecast and Actual outcome remain
     distinct historical/economic states.

    - Contract value, owner cash outlay, resource cost consumed and completed-asset value are not
     automatically the same number.

    - Crew productivity arises from task/method, worker capability, crew composition, tools, available work
     fronts and environment. Extra labor has task-specific diminishing returns.

    - Backlog is committed future capacity, not revenue. Profitable growth can create a liquidity crisis when
     payroll, materials and subcontractors must be financed before customer receipts arrive.

    - Payment to a prime contractor does not prove workers, subcontractors or suppliers beneath that contractor
    have been paid.





                                                     LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 039/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXVIII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                                 2




    - Change, delay, defect, acceptance, payment and responsibility remain separately auditable. Rework
    consumes new labor and materials.

    - Default, abandonment, fire or cancellation do not reset the site. Completed work, defects, materials,
     claims, debts, salvage and unfinished improvements persist.

    - Mechanic/material claims, liens, performance security and surety exist only through
     historically/date/jurisdiction-appropriate Agreement and LegalRegime rules; they are real
    contingent/encumbrance relationships, not abstract penalties.

    - Public/institutional procurement uses the same ordinary economic systems but may add
     plans/specifications, advertised bidding, responsible-bidder screening, security, progress certification,
     withholding/retention and formal acceptance.

 PART I - CONSTRUCTION DELIVERY, ESTIMATING &
 CONTRACT FORMATION

  1.1 Construction delivery is a relationship structure
  CANON LOCK - The same physical building may be delivered by owner/self-performed labor, directly
  contracted trades, a coordinating prime/general contractor or a mixed arrangement. The delivery structure
  changes responsibility, procurement, working-capital burden, coordination and counterparty risk; it is not a
  technology tier.

  A carpenter, mason, painter, plumber, builder or other specialist may operate independently or under a
   prime. A prime contractor coordinates obligations and capacity; the role does not erase the underlying trade
  businesses or Persons.

  1.2 Contractor is a commercial role, not a universal occupation
   Contractor/builder status is ordinarily a business/relationship/authority role layered over real trade,
   estimating, supervision, commercial and management capabilities. Do not require every contractor to have
  a unique Contractor occupation profile, and do not infer construction capability from the title alone.

  1.3 Estimate, proposal and agreement stay separate
  CANON LOCK - An internal Estimate is an actor's forecast. A Bid/Proposal is the commercial offer presented
   to a counterparty. An Agreement is the accepted obligation structure. Baseline preserves the authorized
  scope/budget/schedule; Current Forecast changes as information changes; Actual records what occurred.
  None should silently overwrite the previous state.

  1.4 Bottom-up estimating and uncertainty
   Construction estimates should derive from meaningful measurable scope: excavation/site work,
  masonry/foundation quantities, lumber/board measure, roofing, openings, plaster/finish area,
   fixtures/systems and comparable work packages. Floor area may help infer quantities but is not the
  economic truth.

  Estimate uncertainty should be explainable through categories such as quantity uncertainty, unit-cost/quote
   uncertainty, productivity uncertainty, schedule/dependency uncertainty and collection/payment
   uncertainty. Better expertise, inspection and records narrow justified uncertainty; they do not guarantee
   profit.

  1.5 Procurement responsibility is contractual
  The Agreement may assign labor, materials, tools, equipment, hauling, temporary works, specialist
   installations and other inputs to the owner, contractor, subcontractor or a mixture. Owner-supplied and
   contractor-supplied material are therefore different commercial arrangements even when the finished
   structure is identical.

 PART II - PHYSICAL EXECUTION, CREWS, METHODS &
 ENVIRONMENT

  2.1 Quantity/resource construction
  CANON LOCK - Authoritative construction progress comes from executed physical WorkPackages/Tasks and
  changed Building/site state, not from spending construction points. A summary completion percentage is
  allowed only as a read model.

  2.2 Active-work time versus elapsed project time
  Calendar duration may include waiting for finance, material delivery, a specialist, curing, weather,
   inspection, customer decisions or prerequisite work. Actual active-work intervals remain separate and
  continue to control objectives that measure overlapping work or crew continuity.

  2.3 Crew composition and diminishing returns
  A skilled trade lead can coordinate appropriate helpers on work that permits it. General labor can stage,
   carry, excavate and support skilled work, but specialist requirements remain real. Productivity depends on
   available work fronts, supervision, method, congestion and equipment; adding Persons does not scale
  output linearly.

  2.4 Construction methods change input grammar
  New or diffusing methods should alter required materials, tools, skills, task sequence and labor burden
   rather than grant abstract speed bonuses. Dimensional/plank framing, manufactured doors/windows, wire
   nails, Portland cement, tar paper and other period changes are availability/supportability inputs, not global
  unlock multipliers.

  2.5 Logistics is construction
  Lumber, stone, brick, hardware, windows, fixtures and equipment must come from actual
   suppliers/producers and reach the project through physical logistics. Rail access can improve construction
  because it changes supplier choice, delivered cost, lead time and available components; it does not apply a
   generic ConstructionSpeed bonus.

  2.6 Weather acts on tasks and supply
  Do not use a universal winter construction shutdown. Frozen ground, low temperature, precipitation,
   storms, daylight and route condition affect the particular tasks/material methods they physically constrain.
   Interior work may continue while excavation or masonry is blocked. Severe weather can also interrupt
   delivery even when on-site work would otherwise be possible.

  2.7 Completed work becomes persistent property history
   Installed work changes the Building/improvement and remains after contractor departure, default or project
   suspension. Hidden or known construction quality, defects, repair burden and previous corrective work
  remain part of future diligence and condition history.

 PART III - PROJECT FINANCE, PAYMENT, WORKING
 CAPITAL & CAPACITY

  3.1 Four distinct economic views

   Measure                Meaning

    Contract / Agreement Value   Amount or pricing structure the counterparty agreed to pay, before or after authorized amendments.

     Project Cash Outlay          Cash actually paid by the owner/project entity for purchases, payroll, contractor bills, freight, fees
                             and other project expenses.

    Resource / Cost Attribution     Labor, owned materials, equipment use, donated/family work and other real resources consumed
                              even when no cash transaction occurs.

    Asset Basis / Value             Historical/carrying/market valuation of the resulting improvement under the applicable
                                    property/valuation system; not automatically equal to any one figure above.

  3.2 Progress billing follows the Agreement
   Physical progress does not directly create cash. A contract may use deposits/advances, payment for
   delivered materials, milestone/progress certificates, completion balances, withholding/retention or another
   historically supported structure. Billable/certified amount, invoice/claim, receivable, cash received,
   retained/withheld amount and disputed amount may all differ.

  3.3 Contractor cash remains ordinary business cash
  CANON LOCK - Do not create a magical project wallet merely to prevent poor treasury decisions. Contractor
  cash is ordinary business cash unless a real agreement, escrow, trust, security or restricted-fund
   relationship says otherwise. Project accounting may allocate costs and commitments without creating a
  second money authority.

  3.4 Profitability is not liquidity
  A contract can be profitable while the contractor cannot finance payroll, materials, freight or subcontractors
   until the next receipt. Supplier credit, customer advances, lines of credit, owner capital and payment terms
  can bridge the gap. Expansion and simultaneous projects can increase working-capital stress faster than
  reported profit.

  3.5 Backlog means committed capacity
  Backlog should be understood through future commitments of specific Persons/capabilities, supervisor
   attention, equipment, project windows, materials and liquidity rather than a flat BacklogScore. A contractor
  can be capable but unavailable for the required schedule.

  3.6 Downstream payment remains independent
  CANON LOCK - Owner payment to a prime contractor does not automatically settle the prime's suppliers,
   subcontractors or workers. Each obligation settles only through its own authoritative transaction/claim path.
   This preserves historically plausible lien and nonpayment exposure.

 PART IV - CHANGE, DELAY, DEFECT, ACCEPTANCE &
 RESPONSIBILITY

  4.1 Changes append history
  Owner changes, discovered conditions, design changes, substitutions and corrective work can create
  Change Orders/Amendments that record changed scope, price, schedule and risk. The original baseline
  remains visible. Authorized extras are not silently absorbed into the original estimate.

  4.2 Delay is causal
  Late completion does not by itself prove breach. Contractor scheduling failure, supplier failure,
  owner-caused change, owner failure to furnish required access/input, weather, route disruption, labor
   scarcity and other causes can have different contractual consequences. Time extensions, daily damages or
   other remedies apply only where the Agreement/LegalRegime supports them.

  4.3 Physical completion, usability, occupancy, acceptance and settlement are
  separate
  CANON LOCK - A building may be physically usable or occupied while defects remain, acceptance is
  disputed or final payment is outstanding. Conversely, contractual acceptance does not prove that every
  downstream supplier has been paid.

  4.4 Defect truth and responsibility are separate
  A physical defect can arise from workmanship, wrong/defective material, design/specification error,
  unauthorized substitution, site condition, environmental damage or an unresolved cause. Evidence and
   later investigation determine what actors know and who is responsible; the game should not instantly
  expose omniscient fault attribution.

  4.5 Rework consumes new resources
   Corrective work creates real Tasks/WorkPackages, consumes additional labor/material/equipment and
  changes schedule. Original inputs are not refunded. Financial responsibility for rework follows causation,
   contract terms, negotiation and dated law.

  4.6 Negotiated resolution before full legal escalation
  Disagreements may resolve through negotiation, architect/superintendent interpretation, agreed
   referee/expert, settlement, arbitration or court/legal process when supported. The game should preserve
   time, cost, uncertainty and enforceable outcome without requiring a courtroom simulator.

 PART V - DEFAULT, LIENS, SURETY, ABANDONMENT &
 RECOVERY

  5.1 Default changes relationships; it does not erase physical history
  A Project can be suspended, abandoned, underfunded, damaged, disputed or continued under a
  replacement contractor. Agreement termination does not require Project deletion. Completed work, site
   materials, defects, temporary works, salvage and outstanding obligations remain.

  5.2 Replacement execution uses the remaining real problem
  A replacement contractor should inspect and price the actual remaining work, acceptable completed work,
   defective work, on-site materials and stabilization needs. Do not convert the unfinished project into an
   abstract remaining percentage that ignores physical state.

  5.3 Construction liens/claims are real encumbrances where law permits
  CANON LOCK - Dated Dakota/South Dakota law supports construction claims by labor/material suppliers.
  The LegalRegime determines who may claim, what property/improvement interest can be reached,
   notice/timing requirements, withholding rights and enforcement. A lien/claim is not a reputation debuff and
  must interact with title, sale, refinancing and diligence.

  5.4 Surety/security transfers specified contingent risk
  Performance bonds and other security do not make failure impossible. The contractor can still default and
  work can still stop. Security creates a third-party or pledged obligation that may respond after specified
   default/notice conditions, subject to coverage limits and defenses. It should be modeled as contingent
  exposure, not instant project completion.

  5.5 Default does not confiscate unrelated property
  Owner rights to project-site materials, equipment or other assets after default depend on the Agreement,
   security arrangement and law. Do not automatically transfer a contractor's unrelated wagons, shop assets
   or cash because one project failed.

  5.6 Fire and risk of loss follow real state and agreement
   Fire or other casualty destroys/damages actual work, materials and equipment first. Contract terms,
  ownership, legal regime and insurance determine who bears the economic loss and whether rebuilding is
   required. Insurance creates a claim/possible later payment; it does not restore the destroyed work.

  5.7 Distress can become ordinary market opportunity
  Incomplete or encumbered projects can feed normal property, lending, acquisition and restructuring
  systems. A distressed developer, creditor or replacement contractor may sell rights/assets or negotiate a
  recovery rather than triggering a special construction-failure screen.

 PART VI - PUBLIC / INSTITUTIONAL PROCUREMENT

  6.1 Same systems, greater formality
   Public and institutional construction remains ordinary Agreement/Project execution but can impose
   historically valid additional procedure: prepared plans/specifications, public notice/advertising, sealed or
  formal proposals, responsible-bidder selection, cost ceilings/appropriations, performance security,
   superintendent/architect certification, progress payment limits, withholding/retention and final acceptance.

  6.2 Public work creates a real risk/reward tradeoff
  Large public contracts can provide scale, visibility and credible counterparties while imposing tighter
   pricing, qualification, security, inspection and slower cash conversion. Do not model government work as a
   generic revenue bonus.

  6.3 Qualification is evidence and financeability
  A customer may reasonably consider relevant accepted work, references, specialist Persons,
  equipment/assets, geography, present commitments, liquidity/credit and ability to furnish required security.
   This deepens existing contractor qualification doctrine without creating a ContractorLevel gate.

 PART VIII - ACCEPTANCE DOCTRINE, RESEARCH HOLDS
 & SUPERSESSION

  8.1 Acceptance rules
    - Two visually identical buildings may have different costs, schedules and risk because delivery structure,
    source responsibility and actual supply chains differ.

    - A low bid can win a project and later produce a loss, liquidity crisis, breach or abandonment without
    automatic repricing.

    - A project can be physically advanced while billable amount or cash received remains low or zero under the
    Agreement.

    - A building can be occupied while final acceptance, defects and financial settlement remain unresolved.

    - Payment to the prime cannot automatically clear unpaid downstream obligations.

    - Default preserves the partially completed site and allows replacement execution through the remaining
     physical work.

    - A performance bond changes contingent financial exposure but cannot prevent delay, physical failure or
     contractor insolvency.

    - Construction claims/liens, risk of loss and public-procurement procedure must query dated law/Agreement
    data rather than use one timeless global rule.

    - Scenario-specific crew minimums from THE CONTRACTOR remain scenario definitions and do not become
     universal construction crew requirements.

  8.2 Remaining research/calibration holds
  Keep open as data/calibration rather than Canon constants: detailed 1870-1905 local wage series by trade;
   project-type material quantity libraries; Dakota building-cost series by locality/year; exact productivity
   distributions by method/crew/weather; local supplier inventories and freight spreads; detailed historical lien
  notice/enforcement procedure by date; bond premium/underwriting practice; builders-risk coverage terms;
   public procurement thresholds by jurisdiction; and exact allocation of disputed design-versus-workmanship
   responsibility in specific legal regimes.

  8.3 Supersession/deepening map
    - Revision XVI physical staged construction and Construction & Contracting archetype are deepened by
     delivery-structure, bottom-up estimating, crew/capacity, working-capital and downstream-payment
     doctrine.

    - Revision XVII Project financial reporting, change-order and project-failure persistence are deepened by
     contract-value/cash/resource distinctions, replacement execution, defect responsibility and claims.

    - Revision XXIII Agreement/Obligation/Project lifecycle is deepened by construction-specific billing,
    acceptance, default, lien, surety and risk-of-loss behavior.

    - Revision XXII contractor qualification is deepened by explicit security/bonding feasibility and
    committed-capacity interpretation.

    - All preserved Property, Finance, LegalRegime, Insurance, Inventory, Logistics and Evidence authorities
    remain active and are reused rather than duplicated.

 END OF REVISION XXVIII INTEGRATION

  The complete Canonical Project Bible Revision XXVII follows unchanged as the preserved baseline and
  remains authoritative except where Revision XXVIII explicitly adds, deepens, corrects or supersedes it.

          LAND & LEDGERS
  CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE - REVISION
                   XXVII
  Town, Catchment & Workforce Integration: Economic Population, Market Territory,
            Family Labor, Business Density & Demand-Driven Generation

                                            Revision date: September 26, 2026
                      Source baseline: Canonical Project Bible Revision XXVI - September 26, 2026
                  New source integrated: Historical Research Findings - September 26, 2026
                                                     Status: Active integration

 PRESERVATION GUARANTEE
 REVISION XXVII preserves Canonical Project Bible Revision XXVI in full except where this integration explicitly adds,
 deepens, clarifies, corrects or supersedes prior wording. The complete Revision XXVI document follows this integration
 unchanged as the preserved historical layer. Where a conflict exists, Revision XXVII controls. Numeric catchment ranges,
 workforce percentages, staffing bands and business-prevalence observations from the new research remain
  calibration/authoring evidence unless this integration explicitly identifies a Canon lock.
 PURPOSE
 Revision XXVII integrates the September 26 Historical Research Findings on Dakota Territory town economics and
 workforce calibration. Its central correction is structural: the number of people sleeping inside a town is not the same thing
 as the population supporting that town economically. The revision therefore separates built-up residents, rural service
 population, effective market population, economic participation and wage employment; makes market territory and
 settlement role causal; strengthens family/seasonal labor doctrine; and rejects hidden population-to-business formulas.
 REVISION XXVII MASTER DOCTRINE
   - Town population is a residence count, not a direct proxy for customers, workers or viable businesses.
   - Built-up population, rural service population and effective market population are separate read models over actual
    Persons, Households, Farms, routes and market relationships.
   - Residents, economically active Persons, primary occupation and wage employees are separate measures.
   Employment must not be treated as synonymous with employees.
   - Market territory emerges from physical rural settlement, route access, competing centers, institutions, transient traffic
   and actual trade. No RuralPopulationMultiplier or BusinessCount = Population / X rule is allowed.
   - Settlement role can outweigh size. Agricultural service town, railhead, county/administrative center, mining node, river
    center and industrial node generate different demand even at similar resident population.
   - Business formation and survival follow actual demand and capability. One enterprise may expose several commercial
    capabilities and productive work may occur in houses, barns, yards, shared premises or mobile/route operations.
   - Most local enterprises should be able to remain owner-operated or very small. Staffing grows from task workload,
    seasonality and simultaneous demand rather than a fixed employee recipe.
   - Farm labor distinguishes operator, family enterprise labor, permanent hired labor, seasonal/casual labor and
    contract/service labor. Unpaid family work is economically real without becoming wage employment.
   - Labor demand is worker-time by task and season, with peak simultaneous headcount distinct from annualized FTE.




                                                LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 048/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXVII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                                    2


   - Farms are mixed enterprises; raising animals, processing products and retailing finished goods remain distinct
   economic stages.
   - Historical percentages, catchment brackets and staffing bands in the source are evidence-anchored authoring
    envelopes, not universal Canon constants.
 PART I - SETTLEMENT POPULATION, ECONOMIC POPULATION &
 MARKET TERRITORY
 1.1 Town population is not economic population

 CANON LOCK - The resident population attached to a settlement must not directly determine the number of viable
 businesses, the number of customers those businesses can reach or the size of the local workforce.

 A small town can be the commercial node for a much larger dispersed farming district. Rural households may travel into
 town for grain shipment, blacksmithing, lumber, implements, groceries, mail, banking, lodging, saloons, medical care and
 other services. Conversely, a badly placed or bypassed settlement can underperform despite a larger resident count.
 1.2 Three population views
 Settlement reporting should distinguish at least: Built-up population - Persons whose primary residence lies inside the
 settlement; Rural service population - rural Persons/Households economically connected to the settlement through
 reachable trade/service relationships; and Effective market population - the combined reachable market relevant to
  local commerce. These are read models over world state, not independent counters that can mutate the world.
 1.3 Person-side economic measures

 CANON LOCK - Residents, Economically Active Persons, Primary Occupation and Wage Employees are separate
 measures.

 A farmer or proprietor can be economically active without being anyone's employee. A spouse or older child can
 contribute economically meaningful family labor without conventional wages. A Person can have one primary livelihood
 while still performing secondary household, seasonal, civic or business tasks.
 1.4 Market territory is physical and competitive
 A settlement catchment is shaped by farms and households, roads and river crossings, travel time, wagon economics,
 railway access, nearby competing towns, county or institutional boundaries, terrain, ferries/bridges, production flows and
  existing commercial relationships. Do not implement a fixed radius or multiplier merely because two settlements have the
 same resident population.
 PART II - SETTLEMENT ROLE, BUSINESS ECOLOGY & DEMAND
 2.1 Demand-driven generation

 CANON LOCK - Do not generate businesses directly from town population. Generate viable opportunities from
  resident demand + surrounding rural demand + access + settlement role + competition + transient traffic + local
 production + date + actual unmet demand.

 Population is a useful prior and constraint, but not a cap or a business recipe. The causal chain is: physical rural
 settlement -> farms/households/output -> roads and travel reach -> settlement catchment -> town residents + transients +
  institutions -> actual demand -> businesses form, survive, expand or fail -> staffing emerges from workload.
 2.2 Institution-generated demand
 Courthouses, depots, mills, mines, military/federal facilities and other institutions create demand in their own right. A
 courthouse can support legal, clerical, lodging, restaurant, printing, transport and finance activity; a depot can support
  freight, drayage, hotel, livery, grain and warehousing; a mill can create transport, fuel, maintenance and labor demand.
  Institutional demand is causal rather than an abstract settlement bonus.





                                                LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 049/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXVII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                                    3


 2.3 Settlement role outranks a universal Town Level
  Agricultural service towns, rail junctions/railheads, administrative centers, mining towns, river centers and industrial nodes
 must not be cosmetic skins over one population template. Role and history alter who travels there, what is produced,
 which institutions exist and which capabilities can be supported.
 2.4 Business prevalence is a distribution, not a ratio
  Historical town rosters show high variance at small populations. Therefore rules such as one general store per 100
 residents, GeneralStores = Population / 150 or similar hidden formulas are expressly rejected. Use empirical distributions
 and actual demand drivers instead.
 2.5 Historical observations used as authoring anchors
 The new research documents very small settlements with substantial business rosters and also shows larger towns with
 fewer establishments of particular types. These records establish plausibility and variance, not mandatory templates.

   Observation                Resident population / date    Research use

   application                     population served (Feb. 1880)   multiplier

                                                                support

                                                                farming country

                                                                     resident population; rejects monotonic ratios

                                                   demand from transients
 PART III - BUSINESS ENTITY, COMMERCIAL CAPABILITIES,
 PREMISES & STAFFING
 3.1 One business may provide several services
 A Business is an ownership/accounting/governance entity. Its commercial capabilities can include general goods,
 groceries, hardware, implements, mail/post functions, credit, produce purchasing and other supported services according
  to actual Persons, stock, tools, premises, agreements and authority. Do not satisfy every demand category by spawning a
 separate firm.
 3.2 Business is not building
 A dedicated shop is not required when the work can genuinely occur in a house, barn, yard, mixed-use room, shared
 premises or mobile/route operation. The 1870 opening should therefore contain more productive enterprises than
  storefronts where the physical capability supports it. This deepens Revision XXVI premises doctrine.
 3.3 Small-enterprise structure
 Most ordinary local businesses can remain tiny. Owner-operated microenterprises and 2-6 Person establishments should
 be common; larger 6-20+ local establishments appear where throughput and industrial/service scale justify supervision,
  shifts, clerical work and specialization. These size descriptions are mental models, not hard tiers or unlocks.
 3.4 Staffing is workload-driven
  Staffing follows labor-hours/days, task collision, customer/service load and seasonal peaks. Historical manufacturing
 evidence in the source - roughly 3.4 workers per Dakota manufacturing establishment in 1880, 2.9 per flour/grist mill and
 about 7.4 per sawmill - is retained as dated calibration evidence, not a universal staffing formula.

 PART IV - FARM LABOR, HOUSEHOLD PRODUCTION & MIXED
 ENTERPRISE
 4.1 Five farm labor relationships

 CANON LOCK - Farm work must distinguish: (1) farm operator; (2) family enterprise labor; (3) permanent hired
 hand; (4) seasonal/casual hired labor; and (5) contract/service labor.

 Family enterprise labor is real economic work even when no conventional wage changes hands. Contract/service labor
 includes hired threshing crews, freight carriers, veterinarians, machine providers and comparable external services.
 Permanent employment is only one way labor enters a farm.
 4.2 Seasonal labor is worker-time, not employee slots
 A farm can average modest annual FTE while requiring many Persons at once during harvest, haying, threshing, fencing
 or other peaks. Labor demand should therefore be expressed by task, date/season, duration and simultaneous capacity,
 with FTE only as a reporting abstraction.
 4.3 Primary occupation does not capture all work
  Historical census occupation tables omit or understate much household and family labor. A Person without a recorded
 wage occupation may still perform poultry, dairy, garden, preserving, bookkeeping, childcare, repairs or other productive
 work. Demographic/workforce calibration must not erase that labor merely because it lacks a formal occupation label.
 4.4 Farms are mixed enterprises
 Do not create rigid Chicken Farmer, Wheat Farmer or Beef Farmer classes for ordinary farms. The farm's actual land,
 crops, livestock, equipment and task schedule determine current work. Raising livestock, processing meat/dairy/grain and
  retailing finished goods are separate economic stages that can be performed by different businesses or combined only
 where real capability exists.
 PART V - 1870 OPENING & LONGITUDINAL SETTLEMENT CHANGE
 5.1 1870 opening character
 The normal 55-95 Person 1870 settlement should remain sparse, dispersed and less rail-industrial than the 1880s
  directory examples. Authoring should lean toward wagon freight, stage/ferry/river connections, smithing, one or a few
 merchants where the route/catchment supports them, combined post functions, school/church/shared community space,
 home/yard carpentry and repair and small-scale teamster activity. Bank, grain elevator, lumber yard, newspaper and hotel
 are not automatic population-based fixtures.
 5.2 Generate the countryside first
 A stronger opening rule is to generate surrounding farms/households and their routes before inferring the settlement's
 market. Two 70-Person towns can have radically different economies if one serves dozens of farm households while the
 other is an isolated ferry/stage node with little nearby settlement.
 5.3 Transformation is physical
 As rail, population, finance, institutions and production grow, denser Main Street form should emerge through actual
 businesses, buildings, mixed-use conversion, traffic and investment rather than through a scripted Town Level change.
 PART VI - HISTORICAL ANCHORS, CALIBRATION ENVELOPES &
 NON-LOCKED NUMBERS
 6.1 De Smet high-end service-population anchor
 The source records a February 24, 1880 post-office application stating De Smet town population 50 and post-office
 population served 500, with rapid growth reported soon after. This is a documented proof that service population can
  greatly exceed resident population. It is not permission to apply a 10x multiplier to every town.





                                                LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 051/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXVII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                                    5


 6.2 Occupational context anchors
 The source records 1880 Dakota Territory occupational shares of 49.3% agriculture, 24.2% professional/personal
 services, 10.8% trade/transport and 15.7% manufacturing/mechanical/mining, while warning that territory-wide figures
 include mining, larger towns, transport and government and may understate agriculture in rural districts. It also records
 1890 South Dakota farmers plus agricultural laborers at about 64.0% of gainfully occupied males and 1900 South Dakota
  agricultural pursuits at 60.4% of gainful occupations. These are context anchors, not direct small-town generator
 percentages.
 6.3 Latest workforce-sector table remains calibration
 The source's latest settlement-plus-catchment sector percentages for 10/50/100/200/500/1,000/2,000 resident towns are
  explicitly BRIDGE ESTIMATES. They remain authoring/calibration envelopes with uncertainty, not Canon locks. Separate
 town-proper and rural-district workforce distributions are preferred to one blended population formula.
 6.4 Latest catchment table remains calibration
 The source's latest rural-service ranges - for example a 100-resident agricultural market village serving roughly 300-600
 surrounding rural Persons and a 200-resident farm-service town serving roughly 500-1,000 - are retained as provisional
 authoring envelopes for normal 1878-1890 agricultural settlements. They do not apply automatically to mining camps,
  division points, military posts or major river centers and must never be stored as multipliers or rigid radii.
 6.5 Research provenance boundaries
 Promotional directories and one-town records prove that a configuration could exist; they do not prove every same-size
 settlement had it. Derived arithmetic, bridge estimates and historical observations must retain source, geography, date,
 denominator and confidence under the existing Canon provenance doctrine.

 The new source explicitly leaves several items unresolved. Revision XXVII preserves them as research/calibration work
 rather than silently closing them.

 PART VIII - ACCEPTANCE DOCTRINE & SOURCE TRACEABILITY
 8.1 Acceptance rules
   - A 50-Person or 100-Person town can support more commerce than resident headcount suggests when a real rural
    catchment, transit flow or institution supplies the demand.
   - Increasing resident population alone cannot automatically add businesses, workers or customers.
   - A larger town may have fewer firms of a given type than a smaller town when market territory, role, competition or
    timing differ.
   - Family enterprise labor contributes real task time without creating wage payroll entries.
   - A farm can require several simultaneous seasonal workers even when its annualized FTE is much lower.




                                                LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 052/346 ====================

   - One business can satisfy several commercial capabilities when its people, stock, tools, rights and premises support
   them.
   - A Person can be a resident and economically active without being a wage employee.
   - No catchment multiplier, business-per-population ratio, Town Level or fixed staffing recipe may bypass the causal
   systems above.

         LAND & LEDGERS
  CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE - REVISION
                XXVI

    Ghost Town Playtest Integration: Open Entrepreneurship, Property Rights &
     Agency, Physical Commerce, Migration, Delegation, Valuation & Evidence

                                        Revision date: September 26, 2026

                   Source baseline: Canonical Project Bible Revision XXV - September 22, 2026

                                               Status: Active integration


 PRESERVATION GUARANTEE

 REVISION XXVI preserves the supplied baseline in full except where this integration explicitly adds, deepens,
  clarifies, corrects or supersedes prior wording. The complete baseline document follows this integration
 unchanged as the preserved historical layer. Where a conflict exists, this integration controls. Scenario-specific
 values remain scenario data or calibration unless this integration explicitly promotes them to a general rule.

 PURPOSE

 Revision XXVI consolidates every recorded finding from the September 22-26 Ghost Town playtest into durable
 design doctrine, scenario-specific corrections, calibration boundaries, research holds and explicit supersessions.
 The playtest exposed particularly strong needs around open starting choice, rural catchment economics, property
  rights, real business formation, perishable inventory, recruitment, property agency, delegated portfolio
 management and enterprise valuation. Intermediate in-session references to possible Revision XXVI/XXVII labels
 are superseded by this single consolidated Revision XXVI.

 REVISION XXVI MASTER DOCTRINE

  • Open-ended scenarios should let the player investigate credible opportunities before irreversible starting
    investment unless forced commitment is an intentional premise.

  • Vacancy, abandonment, deterioration and non-use never erase property rights. Property right, physical possession,
    legal basis and enforcement are separate states.

  • A business becomes operating through actual commerce supported by real people, premises, assets, inventory and
    counterparties - not through a setup button or a business-level flag.

  • One business may use several sites and one property may host several businesses or operations. Functional space
   and shared physical capacity remain real.

  • Perishable inventory, prepared food and long processes retain lot provenance, condition and calendar time. Quality
   and food-safety risk are separate.

  • Recruitment and migration arise through actual people, relationships, information channels, jobs, ownership
    opportunities and housing feasibility; applicant and migrant buttons do not conjure people.

  • Human capability presentation is Ordinary -> Great -> Excellent -> Mastered. Underlying capability remains
    continuous and confidence controls the width of what the player sees.

  • Procurement begins with real suppliers and real quoted goods. Landed cost, package terms, deposits, freight and
   payment terms precede retail pricing.

  • Delegated managers act through explicit authority and evidence. Competent rivals use the same systems as the
    player and receive no hidden economic bonuses or omniscience.

  • Enterprise evaluation distinguishes gross going-concern value from the estimated equity/sale proceeds attributable
    to the owner after business-specific liabilities. Business cash is displayed separately.

  • Maintainable operating profit, normalized for replacement labor and seasonality, is the primary ordinary valuation
    evidence; productive assets matter without being double-counted.

  • Property agency, commercial tenancy, chair/room/station leasing, post-sale supply agreements and related-party
    contracts are ordinary contractual relationships rather than special-case ownership shortcuts.




                                          LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 054/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXVI / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                2




  • Railroad promotion, freight adaptation, advertising and market discovery operate through real counterparties,
    capacity, information and incentives rather than success rolls or percentage bonuses.

  • Historical law and specific prices remain dated authoring data with provenance. Scenario-generated quotes and
    playthrough prices are calibration unless explicitly locked.

  • World and portfolio reporting is evidence, not omniscience. Important changes can surface through inspection,
    records or delegated monitoring without turning every state change into a blocking pop-up.
