 PART I - SCENARIO FRAMING, STARTING CHOICE & OBJECTIVES

 1.1 Scenario narration

  CANON LOCK - Every authored scenario should have brief opening narration that establishes premise
  and stakes, plus short route-agnostic completion narration that recognizes what changed without
  prescribing the strategy used.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-CAN-001

 1.2 Player-selected starting opportunity

 When a scenario is intended to support open economic strategy, it should not force the player into a specific
 industry merely because the scenario preselects a building or asset. The author may provide a constrained pool of
 credible starting opportunities, but the player chooses among them. Once selected, the choice becomes persistent
 world history; unchosen opportunities remain in the world and may be taken, altered or lost through NPC action.

 Where the scenario is explicitly structured around a pre-start choice, the campaign clock may remain paused until
 that choice is made. This is an authoring tool, not a universal rule that every campaign must pause at start.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-CAN-008

 1.3 Starting investment follows ordinary investigation

  CANON LOCK - Open entrepreneurship should permit ordinary available market research before scarce
  capital is committed unless forced commitment is deliberately part of the scenario premise.

 The player may investigate traffic, rural demand, existing suppliers, customer sourcing, property condition, title
 status, nearby production and competing businesses using whatever information channels are actually available.
 Investigation is allowed to kill a weak idea before money is spent; a failed investigation is a successful use of the
 system, not a content failure.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-CAN-009, GHOST-DES-019, GHOST-DEF-001

 1.4 Historical starting year is gameplay

 Scenario dates should be chosen for the economic regime they create. The Panic of 1873, railway capital
 conditions, settlement waves and infrastructure availability change actual opportunities, credit and counterparties.
 Starting in 1874 is therefore not a cosmetic reskin of 1880. Scenario authors should select dates intentionally and
 describe the resulting context through the existing HistoricalRegime and evidence doctrine.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-086

 1.5 Ghost Town objective correction

  SCENARIO LOCK - GHOST TOWN SCENARIO LOCK - By December 31, 1885, own 100% of three operating
  businesses with a cash-free, debt-adjusted estimated sale value of the owner interest of at least
  $1,000 each.

 The earlier $500-per-business revision is superseded. The separate December 31, 1876 objective requiring one
 $1,000 business remains unchanged. A business qualifies only if it is genuinely operating through commerce and
 the valuation uses transferable owner equity rather than gross financed assets or cash parked in the account.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-038, GHOST-DES-043, GHOST-DES-049, GHOST-DEF-002

 PART II - PROPERTY RIGHTS, USE, ENFORCEMENT & RESIDENCE

 2.1 Vacant is not ownerless

  CANON LOCK - Vacancy, abandonment, deterioration and non-use never by themselves establish that a
  parcel or building is unowned, free to claim or available for ordinary purchase.

 Property UI must show the ownership/control status the player legitimately knows, the player's current legal basis
  for possession or use and the feasible avenues known to exist. Unknown or disputed is an acceptable state.
 Visually empty does not become legally unowned.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-CAN-002, GHOST-CAN-003





                                          LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 056/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXVI / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                4



 2.2 Unauthorized use is physically possible

 Legal right and physical possibility are distinct. If access and physical requirements permit, a Person may occupy,
 store goods, improve property or conduct business without adequate premises rights. That action can create civil,
  financial, reputational and, where applicable, criminal exposure. Unauthorized occupation never silently creates
  title or a valid lease.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-CAN-004

 2.3 Legal rule is not instant enforcement

 Discovery, notice, awareness, travel, service, negotiation, litigation and enforcement consume ordinary world
 time. A legal rule can exist while an infringement continues because nobody knows, nobody has acted yet or the
 enforcement chain has not completed. The game must preserve the distinction among legality, detection,
 proceeding and consequence.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-CAN-005

 2.4 Good-faith and adverse possession states remain distinguishable

 Color of title, defective documentation, honest boundary error, disputed rights and knowing trespass are not one
 Unauthorized flag. They can carry different knowledge, bargaining, legal and reputational consequences. Property
 troubleshooting should therefore support record searches, owner/agent/executor contact, lease or sale
 negotiation, mortgage resolution, tax-sale paths, public-land entry where lawful, claim challenges, settlement or
 withdrawal.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-CAN-006, GHOST-CAN-007

 2.5 Property opportunity provenance

  CANON LOCK - Every market property opportunity must have a physical property, current right-holder
  or justified unknown status, a reason/channel by which it became known and a traceable path into the
  market.

 Do not fabricate generic cottages, storefronts or farms as ungrounded purchase cards. A broker, newspaper,
 owner, creditor, estate, tax proceeding, personal relationship or direct observation can introduce an opportunity.
 The current owner and sale/lease motivation may be partly unknown, but the world object and information source
 must exist.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DEF-011, GHOST-DES-096

 2.6 Primary residence is distinct from tonight's sleep location

 The player, like other Persons, can have a continuing Primary Residence/Home while temporarily sleeping
 elsewhere for travel, work or lodging. One hotel night does not rewrite residency. Where a legal regime such as
 homestead entry depends on actual residence, compliance uses real residence, presence, cultivation and
 abandonment history rather than a checkbox or merely leaving a bed on site.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-084, GHOST-DES-085

 2.7 Property change is information, not a mandatory pop-up

 NPC property purchases, transfers and encumbrance changes should appear when the player inspects the
 relevant records/property or when a delegated watcher reports them. They should not automatically interrupt
 play. This does not make the strategic camera omniscient: direct inspection, records and delegated observation
 can provide different levels of detail and confidence.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-096, GHOST-DES-097

 PART III - BUSINESS FORMATION, PREMISES & OWNERSHIP

 3.1 Universal Create Business workflow

  CANON LOCK - Creating a Business creates an economic/legal entity and its ownership/governance
  relationships; it does not make the business operational by itself.

 The ordinary workflow is Businesses -> Create Business -> choose business type -> assign owner/ownership
 structure -> establish premises if required -> assign assets/working capital/authority as needed. Premises choices
 can include no dedicated premises required, owned space, leased space or an acquired property. An already-used
 parcel is not automatically unavailable; the player assigns real functional space where compatible.





                                          LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 057/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXVI / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                5





  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-029, GHOST-DES-031, GHOST-TECH-004

 3.2 Operating status comes from actual commerce

 A business crosses into operating status when it can actually perform its economic activity and real commerce
 occurs: inventory or services are produced/provided, customer/supplier counterparties exist and transactions
 settle through ordinary systems. There is no universal Open Business button that bypasses capability or
 commerce.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-009

 3.3 Production and retail space may separate

 One business may span several sites when operations have materially different sanitation, nuisance, storage,
 access or customer-facing requirements. Slaughter, hide preservation, tanning, meat retail and food service are a
 controlling example. Conversely, one building can host several businesses or operations when actual rooms,
  floors, yards, storefronts and shared facilities support them.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-003, GHOST-DES-004, GHOST-DES-031

 3.4 Add operation versus add separate business

 Inside an existing business, Add Operation/Capability expands what the same ledger and ownership entity does.
 Add Separate Business Here creates a distinct business with its own cash, ownership, staff and agreements while
 preselecting the same property and requiring an actual space assignment. Enterprise may exist as an optional
 management umbrella/read model, but it is not another source of cash or ownership truth unless the businesses
 are formally reorganized.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-033

 3.5 Partnerships and partial ownership

 Formation and acquisition workflows may create sole ownership, partnerships/partial ownership and later
  historically appropriate corporate structures. Ownership percentage, capital contribution, profit/loss participation,
 creditor exposure and managing authority are separate facts. Internal economic sharing of a liability does not
 rewrite what the external creditor can legally claim.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-035

 3.6 Shared assets and multi-unit enterprises

 One business may contain multiple operating units under one ledger, such as freight and wagon repair. Shared
 workers, bays, animals, wagons, yards and buildings remain one physical resource pool. A wagon in repair cannot
 haul freight at the same time, and a worker reserved for one task is not simultaneously available elsewhere.
 Internal work consumes time and materials but does not create fake revenue to the same enterprise.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-071, GHOST-DES-072, GHOST-DES-073

 3.7 Parcel expansion and common building costs

 Unused yard area is not generic spare capacity. Planning must preserve real space for circulation, deliveries,
 future structures, utilities/privies/water, fire separation, storage and additions. In mixed commercial buildings,
 common heating/water, stairs, roof, exterior maintenance and common cleaning remain landlord/property costs
 unless a real agreement reallocates them.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-064, GHOST-DES-080

 PART IV - PHYSICAL PRODUCTION, PERISHABLES & PROCESSING

 4.1 Rural production can support town-facing enterprise

 Opportunity evaluation for a small settlement must include its wider rural catchment. Livestock buying, slaughter,
 aggregation, processing and trade can be viable because surrounding farms/ranches and travelers use the town
 even when permanent town population alone is tiny. The market is the actual network of reachable people and
 producers, not the municipal boundary.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-002, GHOST-DEF-001





                                          LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 058/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXVI / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                6



 4.2 Poultry is biological state, not a growth percentage

 Poultry growth preserves egg production, fertility, incubation/brooding, hatch events, sex, juvenile stages,
 mortality, retained females, surplus males and slaughter outcomes. Individual/source identity and known
 parentage remain available where economically material. Same-source birds can be treated conservatively as
 potentially related until evidence says otherwise; breeding decisions can therefore respond to actual lineage
 rather than a calendar timer.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-005, GHOST-DES-022, GHOST-DEF-003, GHOST-DEF-004

 4.3 Butchery and carcass allocation

 A butcher requires a real minimum workstation/tool set rather than ButcherTools=true. Slaughter produces a
 physical carcass and byproducts that can be allocated among fresh retail, wholesale, preservation, household use,
 tallow/fat use, hide processing and waste. Cheap livestock can still be a poor purchase when throughput is lower
 than carcass size and preservation/customer reach are insufficient.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-008, GHOST-DES-010, GHOST-DES-011, GHOST-DES-012

 4.4 Tanning and leatherworking are separate process/capability chains

 Tanning is a multi-stage, time-consuming process using actual tools, inputs and work-in-progress state. Producing
 usable leather does not automatically confer the separate leatherworking/saddlery capabilities required to cut,
 punch, stitch and finish goods.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-006, GHOST-DES-007, GHOST-CAN-013

 4.5 Perishable condition and food safety

  CANON LOCK - Perishable lot degradation and food-safety risk are separate causal states. Neither
  should be represented only by an expiry timer.

 Taste, texture, appearance and saleability can deteriorate before complete spoilage, but contamination or poor
 handling can also produce safety risk before obvious sensory failure. Mixing new and old stock cannot rejuvenate
 old product. Losses, discards and downgraded sales must remain visible in inventory and ledgers.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-CAN-010, GHOST-CAN-011, GHOST-TECH-002

 4.6 Preservation transforms; it does not reset

 Curing, smoking, salting, tanning and comparable transformations create persistent work-in-progress batches
 carrying source condition, handling history, process quality, ingredients, storage and elapsed calendar time.
 Successful preservation changes future deterioration; it does not erase earlier damage. Prepared foods such as
 boiled eggs are likewise physical batches with quantity, age and condition.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-CAN-012, GHOST-CAN-013, GHOST-DES-063

 4.7 Work-in-process can create real bridge-income pressure

 Long production chains do not create revenue before sale. Businesses such as butcher/tannery operations may be
 profitable in the long run while remaining cash-starved between livestock purchase, curing, leather production and
  final sale. That gap is an intended working-capital problem.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-015

 PART V - MARKETS, PROCUREMENT, PRICING & SERVICE CAPACITY

 5.1 Procurement is supplier-first

  CANON LOCK - The game must not generate purchasable stock as an anonymous product-price pair
  when a real supplier/channel should exist.

 A procurement option resolves supplier, exact product/grade, package and quantity, minimum order, bulk tier,
 supplier price, refundable container/deposit terms, freight/handling/other charges, landed consumable cost and
 payment terms. Refundable deposits consume cash but are not COGS unless lost.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-056, GHOST-DES-065





                                          LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 059/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXVI / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                7



 5.2 Supplier qualification and delegated opening purchases

 Where a supplier will provide one, a sample can be requested, transported and inspected. Quality becomes
 evidence from the actual sample/use rather than a hidden permanent supplier score. Delegated buyers may
 choose among acceptable suppliers, grades, package sizes and opening quantities within owner constraints using
 landed cost, quality evidence, expected demand, availability and working-capital burden.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-062, GHOST-DES-066, GHOST-DES-067

 5.3 Retail pricing follows landed cost

 Menu and retail pricing should be evaluated only after the actual procurement terms, serving yield and landed
 cost are known. UI may then show margin, cash burden and demand consequences of candidate prices; it should
 not reverse-engineer a fictional supplier price from the desired retail price.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-060

 5.4 Internal sourcing remains physical and contractual

 A wholly owned supplier does not create free goods. Internal requisitions draw from physical inventory after other
 obligations and production needs. Existing third-party agreements remain binding until legitimately renegotiated
 or ended. Inter-business transfers can be recorded for business-level economics, but internal transfer pricing
 cannot manufacture consolidated profit.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-061, GHOST-DEF-008

 5.5 Staffing follows observed workload

 Hospitality and service businesses should not use fixed recipes such as Saloon=2 bartenders. Start with the staff
 actually hired, then observe customer volume, service delay, cleaning/restocking, bookkeeping, manager overtime
 and concurrent tasks. Add labor when workload supports it. One Person may cover compatible duties when real
 time permits.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-050

 5.6 Physical capacity, patron density and congestion

 Premises capacity derives from actual tables, chairs, bar-standing positions, usable open floor and service points.
 Crowd effects primarily arise through occupied positions, queues, blocked circulation, table scarcity and wait time.
 Individual customers can prefer quiet, moderate or lively establishments while separately tolerating crowding and
 waiting. Preference response should be gradual, and expected crowd based on prior knowledge may differ from
 experienced crowd after arrival.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-054, GHOST-DES-058, GHOST-DES-059

 5.7 Business reporting is evidence

 The simulation can know true occupancy, workload and inventory internally, but the player learns through direct
 observation, records and employee/manager reports. Multiple competent observations can improve confidence
 without simply adding skill scores together. This evidence doctrine applies equally to management dashboards
 and property information.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-055

 5.8 Advertising is a real media market

 Newspapers and other paid media should have publication location, circulation/reach, issue frequency, readership
 geography, placement/size inventory, rates and repeat terms. Advertising creates awareness according to actual
 distribution and placement; it does not create better applicants or tenants. Effectiveness is observed through a
 chain such as insertion -> inquiry -> qualified inquiry -> visit -> hire/lease/sale rather than a hidden +20% bonus.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-076, GHOST-DES-079

 PART VI - LABOR, RECRUITMENT, CAPABILITY & CAREER

 6.1 Casual specialist/helper relationships

 Short-term helpers and specialists can be hired for bounded tasks without creating permanent employment.
 Standing delegation may authorize routine casual hires when a task genuinely benefits from extra labor or
 experience. Major or long-term employment can remain an escalation point.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-013, GHOST-DES-014





                                          LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 060/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXVI / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                8



 6.2 Hiring is a recruitment workflow

 Hire Worker should expose actual channels: contact a known Person, ask employees or associates for referrals,
 post handbills/notices, use local businesses/travel networks, send correspondence or buy newspaper advertising
 where available. These actions create awareness and possible inquiries from actual Persons over time. They do not
 spawn a candidate list on demand.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-051

 6.3 Referral and correspondence recruitment

 NPCs can be asked whether they genuinely know family, former coworkers, friends or business contacts who may
 be interested in a job, property, business or relocation. A relationship can produce a plausible lead or no lead.
 Letters take real travel time; recipients may reply, ignore, negotiate or travel to inspect. The player action remains
 manual unless delegated; separate passive word-of-mouth can spread awareness without a click.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-021, GHOST-DES-034, GHOST-DES-039, GHOST-DES-041

 6.4 Capability bands and candidate evidence

  CANON LOCK - Human player-facing capability bands are Ordinary -> Great -> Excellent -> Mastered.
  "Good" is not a human capability band, though it may remain a valid condition adjective for
  assets/buildings. All preserved seven-band human capability wording is superseded.

 Underlying capability remains continuous or sufficiently granular. Weak, novice or unproven workers are described
 through experience, mistakes, task fit and evidence rather than Bad/Poor labels. Candidate presentation is
 ordered Capability | Current Reading | Confidence | Evidence. High confidence displays one band, Moderate
 exactly two adjacent bands, Low exactly three adjacent bands and insufficient evidence displays Not enough
 information.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-CAN-014, GHOST-CAN-015, GHOST-DES-052, GHOST-TECH-005

 6.5 Capability advancement uses one system for player and NPCs

 Improvement arises from relevant task exposure, aptitude, frequency, variety, instruction/supervision, task
  difficulty and accumulated experience, with diminishing gains as capability becomes exceptional. The player is not
 given a separate RPG XP progression. Promotions or titles do not manufacture competence.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-091

 6.6 Player employment is a valid starting state

 A scenario may begin with the player as a wage employee such as a clerk, carpenter, teamster, farmhand,
 bartender or assistant. The NPC employer owns and controls the business; the player earns real wages, consumes
 real time, gains experience through ordinary work and can later accumulate capital for entrepreneurship. Starting
 self-knowledge of the player's own relevant capabilities may be high confidence where scenario design intends it.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-090

 6.7 Employees can carry personal relationships

 A brokerage or other relationship-heavy employee may leave, join a rival or become independent. Business-held
 exclusive agreements remain with the business unless legitimately transferred, while personal relationships and
 future opportunities can follow the Person. Non-compete protection is not assumed without a real agreement and
  historical/legal support.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-046

 PART VII - MIGRATION, SETTLEMENT & RURAL CATCHMENT

 7.1 Housing is feasibility, not sufficient cause

 Vacant housing alone does not create migration. People move for durable work, wages, business/land opportunity,
 kinship or another plausible pull, then housing determines whether and how the move can occur. Settlement
 strategy should therefore target viable households and their economic reasons for moving rather than only a raw
 headcount threshold.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-016, GHOST-DES-018, GHOST-DES-025





                                          LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 061/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXVI / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                9



 7.2 Business ownership can drive migration

 A skilled outsider may relocate because they can acquire/control a viable business, not only because the player
 offers wages. Genuine business sales, partial ownership and employee/manager financing can therefore become
 migration causes when the household can feasibly relocate.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-020

 7.3 Recruitment and housing can occur at distance

 A prospect can learn about a property through correspondence, receive descriptions and known terms, rent
 sight-unseen, request more information or travel to inspect before moving the household. Information travel and
 physical travel remain distinct.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-032

 7.4 A settlement does not require one dominant anchor

 Durable settlement can emerge from several ordinary businesses and opportunities rather than one mine, mill or
  railroad. A useful causal loop is work/business opportunity -> feasible housing -> household migration ->
 relationship/word-of-mouth spread -> more workers/customers/businesses -> more opportunity. One business
 serving only its owner is not yet a settlement anchor.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-017, GHOST-DES-037

 7.5 Abandoned extraction is evidence, not a binary resource truth

 A vanished placer or mining boom should lower confidence in an easy profitable restart but does not prove that no
 recoverable resource remains. Investigation must resolve actual geology/tailings, rights, process, cost and market
 conditions rather than reading AbandonedMine=false/true as a resource oracle.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-026

 PART VIII - PROPERTY AGENCY, RENTALS & COMMERCIAL TENANCY

 8.1 Property agency is a first-class contractual business

 A real-estate/land/property agent may represent privately owned property for sale or letting, collect rent, care for
 absentee property, coordinate taxes/records and arrange related transactions when authorized. An Agency
 Agreement grants authority and compensation. Exact commission rates remain market/scenario calibration unless
  specifically sourced and locked.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-027, GHOST-DES-028

 8.2 Listings are represented property, not owned inventory

 Agency UI should distinguish Active Listings/Managed Properties from Leads. A represented property remains
 owned by its actual right-holder. The agency gains only the authority granted in the agreement; it does not
 acquire inventory ownership by listing the parcel.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-030

 8.3 Related-party brokerage conflicts require disclosure

 When an agent represents a seller and the agent/player becomes the buyer or otherwise acts on both sides, the
  conflict must be exposed. A commission is not automatically earned on the agent's own acquisition; compensation
 requires the actual agreement and whatever disclosure/consent the historical/legal setting requires.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-036

 8.4 Rental holdings can be an operation inside a property business

 An agency business may also own rental property without creating a new business entity. Each property retains
 separate rent, debt, condition and maintenance history. Lead-routing policies - such as offering suitable company
 vacancies before third-party listings - are configurable management policy, not a universal hidden preference. Any
 playtest commission percentage or employee split remains scenario/company calibration.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-047, GHOST-DES-048





                                          LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 062/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXVI / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                               10



 8.5 Commercial space leasing supports independent businesses

 A landlord may lease a furnished room, station/chair or other functional commercial space to an independent
 operator who keeps customer revenue and pays rent. This is premises use, not disguised employment. A building
 can have occupied and vacant stations simultaneously. The same pattern can support barber, professional office
 or other historically plausible small-space uses.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-074, GHOST-DES-075

 8.6 Professional tenant recruitment is not hiring

 Commercial tenant recruitment follows advertise space -> awareness -> inquiry -> inspection/information ->
 lease negotiation -> relocation/decline. The tenant remains an independent business. Exact claims about how
 common individual barber-chair rental was in 1870s Dakota remain a research hold; the general space-use
 agreement is retained without universalizing that specific custom.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-077

 8.7 Commercial tenancy has operating evidence

 Landlord reporting should separate rent collection, tenant retention, tenant business health, customer traffic and
 space utilization. Full occupancy does not guarantee that tenants are economically healthy, and a strong tenant is
 not the same fact as a high landlord occupancy rate.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-078

 PART IX - DELEGATION, PORTFOLIO AUTONOMY & RIVAL
 ENTREPRENEURS

 9.1 Delegated authority can include credit

 Authority assignments may explicitly cover ordinary purchasing, hiring, contracts, business borrowing and, where
 the owner and lender permit, personal co-borrowing/guaranty. A manager title alone does not grant those powers.
 Authority to borrow for one business does not silently permit sale of the company or mortgage of unrelated
 personal/property assets.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-044

 9.2 Management optimization operates on evidence

 A freight or other manager can monitor real operating evidence such as loaded/empty mileage, asset-days, worker
 load, refused work, delays, route/customer margin, maintenance, queues and stockouts. Better management
 changes actual scheduling, pricing, purchasing, staffing and investment decisions; it does not apply an Efficiency
 +X% bonus.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-045

 9.3 Portfolio autonomy and owner attention

 The player may place businesses under standing delegated operation so routine purchasing, scheduling,
 maintenance, staffing and cash handling continue without owner clicks. Reports surface periodic state and
 material exceptions, with detail weighted toward current owner attention. Major ownership transfers,
 extraordinary debt, unrelated collateral and other owner-locked actions still escalate.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-057, GHOST-DES-068

 9.4 Standing portfolio policies are configurable

 Owners may issue persistent policies such as reinvest all rental cash after obligations, maintain a minimum
 reserve or prioritize particular lead types. These policies constrain delegated choices but are not global rules. The
 Ghost Town 100% rental reinvestment mandate is therefore an example of player policy, not the default behavior
 of every rental business.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-069

 9.5 Venture Manager / Business Development Agent

 A mature portfolio can employ a Person to investigate opportunities, inspect property, research markets, negotiate
 ordinary deals within authority, recruit specialists, arrange suppliers, prepare startup budgets, establish
 operations and hand them to a manager. The Person still requires time, information, capability, capital and
 granted authority. They cannot create enterprises from an abstract Opportunity score.





                                          LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 063/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXVI / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                               11





  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-089

 9.6 Strong rivals use the same rules

  CANON LOCK - When competition is too weak, prefer stronger actual rival behavior over player nerfs or
  hidden NPC bonuses.

 A strong rival can investigate more opportunities, preserve liquidity, negotiate finance, hire capable managers,
 acquire distressed companies, bid for strategic property, vertically integrate and react to evidence. Their edge
 comes from capability, capital, information, relationships and policy. Entrepreneur capital-structure preferences -
 debt-averse, conservative, liquidity-focused, growth-oriented or reckless - are real behavioral inputs rather than
 one generic aggression stat.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-053, GHOST-DES-089, GHOST-DES-093

 PART X - FREIGHT, RAIL STRATEGY & RELATED-PARTY COMMERCE

 10.1 Farm-route freight is first-class commerce

 A carrier can canvass farms, establish standing pickup relationships and combine compatible cargo into routes
 rather than waiting only for one-off jobs. Volume remains real, cargo remains physical and route economics must
 support the service.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-040

 10.2 Related-party exclusive service agreements

 Player-controlled or partly owned businesses may enter exclusive or preferred service contracts when ordinary
 governance approves them. Minority owners must be protected from value-stripping terms, and the agreement
 can include performance windows or fallback rights. Any specific playtest discount is a negotiated scenario term,
 not a universal related-party rate.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-042

 10.3 Internal repair and shared physical capacity

 Freight and wagon-repair operations can coexist in one enterprise, but shared wagons, workers, stables, yards and
 bays cannot be double-booked. Repairs to the enterprise's own wagons consume labor/materials and change asset
 condition without creating internal sales revenue. External repair customers create revenue.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-071, GHOST-DES-072, GHOST-DES-073

 10.4 Railroad promotion / civic lobbying

 A settlement may organize a railroad promotion committee and pursue a route, station, siding or freight stop
 through real persuasion, rights, traffic evidence, land, finance and public authority. Success depends on railway
 economics, engineering and strategy. Public bonds/subsidies and depot/shop commitments execute through real
  civic finance rather than a Lobby Railroad roll.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-082

 10.5 Rail-resilient freight strategy

 Wagon carriers can reason about territory as likely rail-displaced, rail-feeder or rail-insulated and deliberately
 develop non-rail collection/distribution routes to future depots. Rail arrival can destroy some long-haul corridors
 while increasing drayage, farm collection and secondary-node demand. It remains a strategic reconfiguration, not
 a generic penalty.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-083

 PART XI - FINANCE, ACQUISITIONS & ENTERPRISE VALUATION

 11.1 Financing structure is negotiable

 Property and business financing can negotiate price, cash down, maturity, amortization, payment timing, collateral
 scope, guaranty/co-borrowing and prepayment terms. Preserving startup working capital can rationally justify
 more total interest, but counterparties accept or reject terms based on actual risk, security, liquidity and
 alternatives.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-FIN-001





                                          LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 064/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXVI / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                               12



 11.2 Debt assumption is distinct from purchase price

 A buyer may assume secured debt, subject to the real lender/legal requirements, while a seller note or cash covers
 the remaining consideration. Ownership transfer, underlying lender claim, assumed liability and seller credit
 remain separate relationships. Debt continuity must survive sale, save/load and reporting.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-FIN-002, GHOST-DEF-010

 11.3 Enterprise evaluation shows two values

  CANON LOCK - Enterprise Evaluation must distinguish estimated gross going-concern/business sale
  value from estimated owner equity/sale proceeds after business-specific liabilities.

 A heavily financed business and a debt-free business with the same operating assets are not economically
 identical to the owner. Objective checks that intend to measure what the player has actually built should use the
 transferable value attributable to the required ownership interest after directly associated liabilities.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-043, GHOST-DES-081

 11.4 Business cash is separate from business value

 Cash held in the business account is economically owned but contributes zero to the Ghost Town business-value
 objective and should be displayed separately. Parking cash inside a weak business cannot satisfy a valuation
 milestone. Receivables/payables can be handled separately at closing according to the deal.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-087

 11.5 Maintainable operating profit is primary valuation evidence

 Ordinary operating valuation starts with maintainable operating profit, then adjusts for seasonality, consistency,
 margins, trend, customer concentration, repeat contracts, supplier stability, competition, operating history,
 records, reputation, management continuity, owner dependence, capital replacement needs, legal/licensing risk
 and premises security. Do not blindly annualize the best short period.

 Owner labor is normalized at replacement cost. If the owner works extensive unpaid hours, the transferable
 business profit is what remains after paying a competent replacement for the actual work. Employee count itself
 adds no value; capable staff can increase transferability while unnecessary payroll can reduce it.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-088

 11.6 Productive assets matter without double counting

 Machinery, tools, vehicles, fixtures and owned real estate affect sale value, replacement-capital needs and asset
  floors. Do not simply add original asset purchase price on top of an earnings value that already assumes those
 productive assets are included. Asset-heavy enterprises can lean more strongly on asset/equity evidence;
 service/agency businesses may lean more strongly on earnings and transferable clientele. Treatment of inventory
 at business sale remains an open design point: durable inventory may transfer at agreed current value while
 perishables need realizable value, age, condition and spoilage risk.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-092

 11.7 Seller motivation and distress are evidence

 Acquisition negotiation should model known evidence about seller age/plans, liquidity need, attachment,
 alternatives, creditor pressure and willingness to remain as employee/manager. Do not invent a retirement motive
 after the fact to justify a deal. Distressed businesses can be surfaced by owners, creditors, employees or brokers,
 but the player receives evidence about problems rather than an answer key; some businesses cannot be fixed
 economically.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-094, GHOST-DES-095

 11.8 Plain-language finance UI

 Underlying structures such as seller note, mortgage, lien, guaranty and assumed debt remain distinct. Default
 player-facing presentation should additionally state in ordinary language who lent the money, amount owed, rate,
 next payment, maturity, collateral and any guaranty/assumption exposure.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-UX-001





                                          LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 065/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXVI / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                               13


 PART XII - HISTORICAL LAW, CALIBRATION, RESEARCH HOLDS &
 OPEN QUESTIONS

 12.1 Historical legal gates can precede operation

 The Ghost Town research established a scenario-relevant Dakota liquor-law gate: the January 1873 regime
 requires a license and a $3,000 bond with at least two sufficient sureties before on-premises liquor sales. The bond
  is security/liability, not automatically a $3,000 cash deposit. Historical law should be represented through dated,
 sourced authoring records and actual compliance workflows rather than a generic SaloonUnlocked flag.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-LEGAL-001

 12.2 Exact playtest prices remain calibration

 Opening purchase prices, repair estimates, land values, poultry/livestock prices, exact tool/material prices,
 first-slaughter yields, local meat prices and horse/wagon prices used in Ghost Town remain scenario calibration
 unless later research explicitly promotes a particular value to a dated authoring anchor. They should persist
 consistently within the playthrough but not become universal Canon constants.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-CAL-001, GHOST-CAL-002, GHOST-CAL-003, GHOST-CAL-004, GHOST-CAL-005

 12.3 Generated local quotes are not archival facts

 Where historical supplier/commodity/freight/tax evidence constrains a fictional town but no exact local quote
 survives, the game may generate an authoritative scenario quote calibrated against that evidence. It must remain
 labeled generated scenario data rather than presented as a surviving historical quotation.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-RES-003

 12.4 Exact 1872 rail construction milepost remains a research hold

 The playtest accepted the historical Sioux City-Vermillion construction front but did not establish an exact physical
 milepost on the scenario date. Do not fabricate that precision. If the exact front becomes economically decisive,
 perform targeted research or use an explicitly uncertain authoring range.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-RES-001

 12.5 Camera versus direct observation remains open

 No final Canon lock is made on how much the strategic/sky camera itself counts as observation. The current
 design direction is that records, employees and obvious visible development can surface strategic facts while
 direct inspection yields stronger condition/evidence detail. This remains an explicit open question rather than an
 accidental omniscience rule.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-097

 12.6 Ghost Town scenario historical calibration

 For the current Ghost Town playtest history, Morrow Creek is calibrated at roughly 85 permanent residents at its
 boom-era peak, roughly 120 persons physically present during the busiest transient/mining periods and 14
 non-player permanent residents at the 1872 opening. The player household is separately real rather than omitted
 from domestic simulation. These values belong to this scenario unless separately promoted.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DES-097, GHOST-TECH-001, GHOST-DEF-006

 PART XIII - PLAYTEST CORRECTIONS, ACCEPTANCE DOCTRINE &
 TRACEABILITY

 13.1 Corrections that become future acceptance rules

  • Opportunity evaluation must include the rural catchment before concluding that a tiny town cannot support a
    business.

  • Poultry ledgers must preserve male/female juvenile pathways and must not invent retrospective revenue when a
    missing classification is corrected.

  • Egg and other sales require real counterparties or a legitimate remote market channel; anonymous infinite demand
     is invalid.

  • The player household/residence and ordinary personal consumption must exist when scenario design says the
    player is a resident; population objectives must state whether the player counts.





                                          LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 066/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXVI / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                               14




  • Wholly owned internal sourcing should use flexible requisitions over physical stock unless a real fixed contract
     exists; internal transfer prices cannot create consolidated profit.

  • Property-management labor must be charged to the business/operation receiving the work rather than
    disappearing into another business payroll.

  • Debt balances and obligations must carry forward exactly; correcting a missing debt entry must not invent
    repayments or rewrite transaction history.

  • Every property opportunity must preserve physical identity, owner/right-holder provenance and the information
    channel that exposed it.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-DEF-001, GHOST-DEF-003, GHOST-DEF-004, GHOST-DEF-005, GHOST-DEF-006, GHOST-DEF-008, GHOST-DEF-009,
 GHOST-DEF-010, GHOST-DEF-011

 13.2 Validated architecture carried forward

 The playtest positively validated population represented by identifiable Persons and household/accommodation
 arrangements rather than an independent population counter, stable Person IDs with kinship separate from
 household membership, perishable lot provenance and premises requirements that depend on the actual business
 capability. These confirmations deepen rather than replace Revision XXV doctrine.

  Playtest provenance: GHOST-TECH-001, GHOST-TECH-002, GHOST-TECH-003, GHOST-TECH-004

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXV / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                                            1

             LAND & LEDGERS
    CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE - REVISION XXV
    1870 Frontier Transformation Integration: Historical Envelope, Railway & Transport Networks, Technology
                  Diffusion, Environmental Regimes, Settlement Evolution & Research Provenance

                                                 Revision date: September 22, 2026
                          Source baseline: Canonical Project Bible Revision XXIV - September 21, 2026
                                                          Status: Active integration

 PRESERVATION GUARANTEE
 Revision XXV preserves Revision XXIV in full except where this integration explicitly adds, deepens, clarifies or supersedes prior
 wording. The complete Revision XXIV document follows this integration unchanged as the preserved baseline. Where a conflict
  exists, Revision XXV controls. Exact prices, wages, freight tariffs, farm distributions, equipment ownership shares, technology
 adoption rates, weather coefficients, route timings, clerical error frequencies and other generated values remain calibration unless this
  integration explicitly identifies a design or historical lock.
 PURPOSE
 Revision XXV integrates the dedicated 1870-start historical research program and the architecture cleanup performed after Revision
 XXIV. The central change is that the normal Open Frontier historical envelope now begins in spring 1870 rather than spring 1880. This
  is not a cosmetic date shift. It establishes an earlier wagon-, river- and emerging-network frontier and lets the player experience
  thirty-five years of transport, information, finance, settlement and technology transformation through 1905.
 The research also closes several architectural ambiguities: physical railway construction is distinct from service opening; railway
  infrastructure, legal corporation, owner, operator and controller are distinct relationships; technology progresses through availability,
 access and supportability rather than universal unlocks; non-rail transport remains economically meaningful after rail arrives;
 environmental and financial eras alter causal inputs rather than applying flat modifiers; and historically constrained regional geography
 can coexist with procedural local economies.
 REVISION XXV MASTER DOCTRINE
   * The normal Open Frontier historical envelope is spring 1870 through 1905. Scenarios may begin later or use shorter windows.
   * 1870 is an early-network frontier, not a primitive world. Hand, animal, water, wind and steam power are mature; rail, banking,
     utilities and rapid communications are sparse or uneven locally.
   * Historical geography is constrained where it matters. Major rivers, treaty/reservation/federal geography, outside market nodes
   and dated regional infrastructure approaches form a historical skeleton; local settlements, businesses, Persons and many
    roads/projects can remain procedural.
   * Track laid is not service open. Proposed, incorporated, surveyed, financed, graded, track-laid and operating railway states
    remain distinct.
   * Railway property, corporate identity, operation, lease/control and later system identity are distinct. Corporate succession
   does not rewrite the history of a physical segment, contract or Person.
   * Rail complements and reconfigures wagon, stage, ferry and river transport. It does not apply a generic Freight Obsolescence
    penalty.
   * Technology is not a global unlock tree. Existence, commercial production, regional/local availability, acquisition/connection,
    supportability and operation are separate states.
   * Historical regimes are causal contexts. Panic, drought, grasshoppers, favorable rainfall or boom conditions alter actual credit,
    projects, crops, migration and markets rather than multiplying all outcomes by a scripted percentage.
   * Business records have physical methods. Handwriting, forms, typewriters, copying devices, registers and calculating equipment
   change real clerical tasks and evidence quality rather than granting abstract administration bonuses.
   * Historical evidence itself needs provenance. A first-known date, one-town observation or unusual capital operation must not
     silently become a universal regional rule.

 PART I - 1870-1905 HISTORICAL ENVELOPE & OPENING WORLD
 1.1 Default Opening
 CANON LOCK - Open Frontier normally begins in spring 1870 and retains 1905 as the authored Historical Horizon. The exact
 opening day may remain world/scenario data. Reaching 1905 still produces the Historical Record/retrospective; continued
 simulation may proceed under the existing continuation doctrine.
  All preserved references that define spring 1880 as the ordinary Open Frontier start or define 1880-1905 as the full normal historical
 envelope are superseded by this section. Scenario-specific dates remain unchanged unless separately revised. References
  describing an 1880 condition remain historically usable as mid-campaign state rather than opening state.
 1.2 1870 Opening Character
 The opening regional economy should be sparse, physically dispersed and highly dependent on overland and river movement.
 Southeastern Dakota and Missouri-oriented settlement supply the strongest ordinary opening analog. The wider United States already
 contains railroads, mechanized farming, industrial steam, telegraphy, sophisticated printing and mature manufactured goods; the
  frontier constraint is local access, capital, transport, information and support, not ignorance of those technologies.
 A small settlement around the existing 55-95 Person target remains plausible. The early economy can contain more productive
  activity than dedicated commercial buildings: artisans may work from a house, barn, yard or mixed-use premises when the actual
  tools, space and rights support the work.
 1.3 Initial Connectivity
 Ordinary 1870 local transport is built around walking, riding, horse/ox teams, wagons, ferries, stage/freight roads and river landings.
 Sioux City is a major outside rail interface. The Sioux City-Yankton telegraph connection arrives in 1870, but communication access
 remains geographic. A settlement being in a territory with telegraph service does not mean every business has a telegraph office or
  direct wire.
 1.4 Indigenous Land, Public Land & Restricted Geography
 The 1870 opening precedes the Black Hills gold rush and the 1877 federal taking. The Black Hills cannot appear as an ordinary
 purchasable mining district at start. Treaty, reservation, agency, military, federal/public-domain and ordinary private property remain
  distinct legal/geographic states. A visually empty parcel is not automatically claimable. Public-land entry requires the applicable
  survey/status and entry process; restricted land never enters the ordinary Make Offer workflow solely because it is visible.
 1.5 Historical Transformation Phases
   Period            Working historical character

   1870-72            Sparse territorial frontier; wagon/river logistics; thin finance; first telegraph and railway promotion/construction.

   1873-77                 First local rail service plus Panic/depression; uneven settlement; drought/grasshopper risk; Black Hills transformation.

   1878-87             Great Dakota Boom; rapid rail/town expansion; rising machinery access; early telephone, waterworks and electric-light systems in
                     advanced nodes.

   1887-95                Agricultural drought/debt pressure; mature regional rail networks; statehood; Panic of 1893; uneven town fortunes.

   1896-1905          Recovery and deeper institutions; RFD and mature communications in selected areas; West River investment; first rare
                         internal-combustion machines; temporary Pierre rail crossing in 1905.

 These phases are contextual priors, not scripted outcome bands. A local town may boom or decline against the broader regime if its
  actual resources, routes, projects and actors justify it.

 PART II - HISTORICALLY CONSTRAINED PROCEDURAL WORLD
 2.1 Three-Layer World Generation
 CANON LOCK - Open Frontier combines a historical regional skeleton with historically constrained procedural geography
 and ordinary emergent simulation.

   Layer                Examples                                        Rule

    Historical skeleton         Missouri River; major outside cities/market nodes;        Must remain consistent with the historical envelope unless a scenario
                                treaty/reservation/federal geography; major dated rail        explicitly uses an alternate premise.
                           approaches; statehood and major national/regional
                              events.

   Constrained procedural    Fictional/local settlements; crossroads; secondary roads;  May vary by seed inside geographic, legal and historical constraints.
   geography                farms; small ferries/landings; plausible station sites.

   Emergent simulation      Persons; businesses; property control; exact projects;     Resolved by ordinary systems and may diverge from actual history.
                                station competition; migration; firm births/deaths; local
                               winners/losers.

 2.2 Historical Baseline Does Not Predetermine Future Local Outcomes
 Revision XXIV historical-divergence doctrine remains active. A historical railway intention, townsite or business opportunity enters the
 world through real actors, rights, finance and projects. If player/NPC action changes the prerequisites, later local history can diverge.
  Historical dates may introduce technology, outside actors, laws or external projects; they do not force an impossible local result.
 2.3 Settlement Role Instead of Universal Town Level
 Settlement physical form and business mix should depend on economic role and history. Useful archetypes include
  river/administrative center, rail-platted agricultural service town, mining supply center, rail junction, rural market town,
 industrial/company node and bypassed/declining settlement. These are authoring/generation descriptors, not progression tiers or
 bonuses.
 2.4 Railway-Created Settlements
 A railway may establish a depot/townsite away from an existing settlement. Land platting, depot siting, elevator/warehouse
 development and new businesses can create a competing node. Existing settlements may connect, shift toward the station, decline,
 lobby for service or retain a separate niche. Rail does not automatically attach itself to the nearest existing town.
 PART III - RAILWAY DEVELOPMENT, SERVICE & CORPORATE IDENTITY
 3.1 Railway Development Lifecycle
 CANON LOCK - Proposed/Incorporated, Surveyed, Financed/Authorized, Right-of-Way Secured, Grading, Track Laid,
  Facilities Ready and Service Open are different states. Track that physically exists may remain commercially useless when
 no service operates.
 The 1872-73 Winona & St. Peter extension provides the controlling example: track could physically extend well into Dakota while
 normal trains operated only to an earlier point for years. Scenarios, markets and objectives must query the state actually required.
 3.2 Physical Segment & Corporate Relationships
 A physical railway segment persists independently from the corporate relationships around it. Historical builder, infrastructure owner,
  legal railroad corporation, lessee/operator, controller/parent and later system identity may differ. Merger, lease or acquisition changes
  relationships; it does not rewrite who built a segment, which corporation signed an earlier contract or which Persons performed the
 work.





                                                 LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 075/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXV / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                                            4

 3.3 Working Regional Chronology

   Date           Regional railway anchor

   1870         No ordinary in-state common-carrier network in the normal South Dakota opening region; Sioux City functions as an external railhead/interface.

   1872           Dakota Southern construction reaches Vermillion; additional eastern penetration projects appear.

   1873           Dakota Southern reaches Yankton; national financial panic weakens railway finance.

   1878             Rail construction resumes strongly; Sioux Falls receives service; new townsite/railroad settlement effects accelerate.

   1879-80          Multiple Iowa/Minnesota penetration fronts expand; Dakota Central reaches Pierre in 1880.

   1885           Common-carrier rail reaches Buffalo Gap on the southern Black Hills approach.

   1886             Rail reaches Rapid City.

   1887           Rapid City-Whitewood connection extends Black Hills access.

   1890           Deadwood/Belle Fourche gain major common-carrier connections while mature East River networks already exist.

   1905          Temporary railway bridge/crossing at Pierre allows the first official trains across the Missouri shortly before Christmas; permanent bridge lies
                 beyond the 1905 horizon.

 3.4 Railway Town Competition & Civic Participation
 Railway route and station decisions may involve local inducements, right-of-way, depot land, bonds/subsidies, traffic expectations and
  political/legal authority. Towns can compete, refuse, overpay or lose. A civic financing decision must execute through real public
  authority/finance rather than a Town Wants Railroad flag.
 3.5 Railway Technology Evolves Through Assets
 Railroad modernization should arise through actual track, bridges, locomotives, rolling stock, brakes, couplers, yards, water/fuel
  facilities, dispatch/timekeeping and signaling. Older equipment may remain usable on lighter service while becoming inefficient,
 incompatible or legally restricted. The 1893/1903 federal safety-appliance regime supplies a later-campaign legal pressure toward
 power brakes and automatic couplers; it is not an instant whole-network conversion.

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXV / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                                            5

 PART IV - ROAD, STAGE, FERRY, RIVER & MULTIMODAL TRANSPORT
 4.1 Non-Rail Transport Is First-Class Infrastructure
  Roads/trails, ferries, stage lines, freight routes, way stations, river landings and steamboat service are real transport infrastructure. A
 stage or freight service requires vehicles, animals, crews, feed, maintenance, route access, schedules and appropriate facilities. River
  service requires vessels, landings, navigation season and cargo/passenger handling.
 4.2 Multimodal Logistics
 One economic trip may combine wagon -> river landing -> steamboat -> railhead -> distant market, or farm wagon -> depot -> rail ->
  destination drayage. Each leg preserves time, custody, cost, cargo and risk. Transshipment is an actual handling/transfer event rather
 than a free route change.
 4.3 Rail Reconfigures Rather Than Deletes Wagon Work
 CANON LOCK - Rail arrival changes route economics causally. Long wagon hauls can contract while farm-to-depot
  collection, station drayage, local delivery, hotel/livery demand and feeder freight increase. Businesses survive, change,
 move or fail according to actual demand and capacity; there is no generic pre-rail-industry obsolescence modifier.
 4.4 Route Conditions & Seasonality
 Road surface, mud, snow, river ice/high/low water, ferry availability and weather can alter travel time/capacity or close a route. Exact
  historical speeds and rates remain calibration data. The architecture must allow route availability and capacity to change without
  inventing or deleting cargo.
 PART V - TECHNOLOGY DIFFUSION, ACCESS & SUPPORTABILITY
 5.1 No Universal Technology Unlock
 CANON LOCK - Technology progression uses at least the following distinctions: Known/Technically Exists -> Commercially
 Produced -> Regionally Obtainable -> Locally Obtainable or Networked -> Acquired/Connected -> Supported/Maintainable ->
 Operational.
 A patent or national commercial date proves possibility, not local adoption. A technology already used by a well-capitalized
  rail-connected operation does not imply ordinary small-town or rural availability.
 5.2 Supportability
 Equipment may be owned yet temporarily unusable because fuel, parts, consumables, compatible infrastructure, trained operators or
  repair capability are unavailable. Supportability is therefore distinct from ownership and condition. Frontier technology should fail or sit
  idle for explainable logistical reasons rather than through arbitrary Tech Level rules.
 5.3 Confirmed Historical Anchors

   Technology/system                Historical rule for authoring

   Reapers/mowers                   Already established before 1870. Adoption depends on capital, acreage, draft power, dealer/repair access and economics.

   Hand/animal/water/wind/steam        All valid productive power sources in 1870. Steam growth does not erase older methods.
   power

   Barbed wire                       Commercially transformative 1874-era development; regional adoption should spread rather than appear universally at once.

   Typewriter                       Commercial 1874; improved upper/lowercase model 1878; office adoption uneven. Treat mainly as document-production
                                     equipment.

   Telephone                       Commercial exchange era begins 1878; Deadwood has first South Dakota exchange in 1878; requires actual local
                                         network/subscription.

   Waterworks                   Deadwood 1879; Yankton and Sioux Falls 1884 anchors; other settlements remain wells/cisterns/hauling until real projects exist.

    Electric light/power              Deadwood electric lighting by 1883; adoption begins in advanced nodes and industrial sites, not as universal household
                                             infrastructure.

   Cash register                          Ritty-era 1878 invention/commercialization; stronger business adoption later, especially after NCR development.

   Bicycles                            Useful personal transport grows in the late 1880s/1890s; not a freight replacement.

   Mechanical refrigeration              Later/capital-heavy industrial option; ordinary ice/icehouse systems remain important throughout much of the campaign.

   Automobile/gasoline tractor          Rare/cutting-edge at the 1900-05 horizon; horses remain the normal transport/agricultural core.

 5.4 Technology Changes Tasks, Capacity & Information
 Technology should primarily alter feasible task methods, throughput, labor burden, reliability, information speed, quality/control or
 network reach. It should not grant free output. A machine still needs a Person/operator, location, inputs, time, authority and often
 maintenance.
 PART VI - AGRICULTURAL MECHANIZATION & CONSTRUCTION MATERIAL
 ECONOMY
 6.1 Farm Development Is Multidimensional
 Farm scale must not collapse into one Farm Level. Land/right, improved acreage, buildings, fencing, draft power, productive livestock,
 equipment, Household labor, hired labor, working capital, debt and output remain separate. 1870 agricultural records show wide
  variation between property value and livestock value, supporting genuinely different economic structures at similar apparent scale.
 6.2 Machinery Growth Is Economic, Not a Tech Tier
 For the area that became South Dakota, farm implement/machinery investment rises sharply from about $1.55 million in 1880 to $8.37
  million in 1890 and $12.22 million in 1900. The 1880s are therefore a major mechanization/diffusion decade, but advanced machinery
 can appear earlier in exceptionally capitalized and connected operations. The game should allow uneven adoption rather than a fixed
  regional unlock date.
 6.3 Equipment Access Methods
 Revision XXIII access doctrine is reaffirmed and expanded for the 1870 start: ownership, borrowing, rental, dealer/service access,
  hired machine-and-crew operations and contractor-supplied equipment are all legitimate where history and agreements support them.
  Traveling threshing and similar services are especially important because major machinery can be commercially useful without every
 farm owning it.
 6.4 Construction Materials Follow Logistics
  Early settlements can rely on local timber/logs, earth/sod, stone where suitable, rough-sawn lumber and expensive wagon-hauled
 manufactured material. Rail connection can sharply improve access to dimension lumber, shingles, doors, windows, hardware and
 standardized components. A sophisticated frame building therefore emerges from material supply, skilled labor, equipment, money
 and transport, not SettlementLevel >= N.
 6.5 Building and Business Are Still Separate
 The early frontier strengthens the existing doctrine that a Business is not synonymous with a dedicated storefront. Productive work
 can occur in a house, barn, yard, temporary shop or mixed-use premises when the required physical capability and legal/use rights
  exist.
 PART VII - INFORMATION, MAIL, TELEGRAPH, TELEPHONE & MAIL-ORDER
 COMMERCE
 7.1 One Information World, Multiple Delivery Channels
  Letters/mail, messenger, newspaper/print, telegraph, telephone, in-person conversation and later reports all use the shared
 Information/Evidence doctrine. Delivery channel changes speed, cost, reach, documentary strength and access; it does not create
 separate knowledge truth.
 7.2 Postal Access
 Postal service is a real information network. A rural household may need to travel to collect/send mail, combining that errand with
 shopping, banking and social activity. Rural Free Delivery begins late in the period; South Dakota has an early listed RFD route at
  Ellis on May 1, 1899. RFD can reduce the Person-time cost of mail access without teleporting goods.
 7.3 Mail-Order Procurement
  Mail-order commerce is a legitimate procurement channel beginning during the campaign. Montgomery Ward begins mail-order
 business in 1872; Sears expands the form later. Information/order travel may occur by post, while heavier goods continue to require
  rail/express or other physical shipment because Parcel Post lies beyond the normal horizon. Catalog competition therefore expands
 choice but retains delivery time, freight, station collection and payment/credit constraints.





                                                 LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 078/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXV / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                                            7

 7.4 Standard Time Transition
 Before November 18, 1883, local/company railway time standards can differ. The simulation keeps one authoritative absolute time;
  historical schedules/documents may carry a TimeStandard reference for conversion/presentation. Standard railway time begins
 November 18, 1883 and gradually simplifies schedule presentation. The player is not required to manually maintain multiple clocks.
 PART VIII - BANKING, CREDIT & MACROECONOMIC REGIMES
 8.1 Thin 1870 Institutional Finance
 The 1870 frontier should not assume ubiquitous formal banks. Dakota's first bank begins as a private Yankton operation in 1869 and
 the First National Bank of Yankton is chartered in late 1872. Early financing can therefore rely more heavily on merchant/supplier
  credit, promissory notes, mortgages, seller finance, wealthy private lenders, private bankers and distant institutions. Institutional depth
 grows with settlement.
 8.2 Panic of 1873
 CANON LOCK - The Panic of 1873 is a major historical macro event whose effects propagate through actual lenders, railway
 finance, projects, businesses, labor and asset markets. It is not a global revenue penalty.
 Railroad financing can fail, projects can pause, lenders can protect liquidity, borrowers can lose renewal/refinancing options,
  distressed assets can appear and financially strong actors can exploit opportunities. Each outcome must still be attributable to actual
 balance sheets, agreements and counterparties.
 8.3 Panic of 1893 & Later-Campaign Financial Stress
 The Panic of 1893 provides a second large national credit/railroad shock at a stage when the player may control a much larger
  organization. The same financial authorities apply at greater scale: liquidity, debt maturity, collateral, lender behavior,
  securities/capital needs and business cash remain real.
 8.4 No Single Credit Availability Meter
 A historical credit regime can influence lender priors and regional capital conditions, but individual lenders still decide using their own
  liquidity, knowledge, collateral, relationship, legal rights and risk. One lender tightening does not automatically remove every possible
 source of finance.





                                                 LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 079/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXV / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                                            8

 PART IX - ENVIRONMENTAL REGIMES & CAUSAL SHOCKS
 9.1 Environment Is Economic State
  Rainfall/soil moisture, temperature, snow, wind, grasshopper pressure, prairie-fire conditions, river conditions and comparable
 environmental variables may be represented at the resolution needed to create real agricultural/logistics consequences. Do not model
  historical shocks as flat revenue or yield multipliers.
 9.2 Working Historical Context
 The opening years sit near the end of an early Dakota settlement/agricultural boom. The 1873 financial crisis, weak farm prices,
 drought and grasshopper disasters contribute to hardship and abandonment in the mid-1870s. Broadly favorable rainfall from roughly
 the mid-1870s through mid-1880s supports the Great Dakota Boom. Drought and agricultural depression from the late 1880s into the
 1890s increase debt stress, then overlap with the Panic of 1893.
 9.3 Causal Chains
 Examples: drought -> lower crop/hay yield -> feed shortage -> livestock condition/culling -> commodity prices/cash pressure ->
  debt/migration choices. Grasshoppers consume actual crop/forage state. Prairie fire uses fuel/weather/ignition/mitigation and can be
 reduced by real fireguards. Flood/river conditions alter routes/landings/ferries rather than directly changing abstract transport scores.
 9.4 Historical Regime Is Context, Not Fate
  HistoricalRegime-style authoring may supply regional/date priors for climate, migration, credit, rail investment and commodity context.
  It cannot override actual local simulation. Good water, diversified business, low leverage or strong logistics can make one actor
  resilient inside a bad regional period.
 PART X - SETTLEMENT INFRASTRUCTURE, UTILITIES & FIRE PROTECTION
 10.1 Infrastructure Is Project History
 Telegraph, telephone, waterworks, electric light/power, roads, bridges, rail facilities and organized fire protection emerge through
  actual projects, networks, institutions and service relationships. Earliest-known local dates are authoring anchors, not universal
  unlocks.
 10.2 Water & Fire
 Deadwood provides an 1879 waterworks anchor; Yankton and Sioux Falls provide 1884 anchors. Earlier settlements may rely on
  wells, cisterns, hauled water or natural sources. Fire response can progress from household/ad hoc bucket response to volunteer
  organizations, hose carts/engines and later more developed apparatus as water supply, population and institutional capacity justify it.
 10.3 Electricity
 Deadwood electric lighting by 1883 confirms rapid but localized adoption. Electricity can first appear in mines, mills, central stations or
 dense commercial nodes while nearby rural households remain non-electric. Generating capacity, motive power, wiring/distribution,
  service agreements and maintenance remain physical constraints.
 10.4 Longitudinal Settlement Evidence
 Sanborn sequences and other dated maps should be used to author/validate settlement form over time. Sheet counts or map
 coverage are research-index signals rather than direct simulation formulas. The intended use is comparative extraction of business
  mix, building material, density, stables/outbuildings, industrial sites, utilities and rail interfaces.
 PART XI - RECORDS, PENMANSHIP & OFFICE EQUIPMENT
 11.1 Records Have Method & Quality
 Important written records can distinguish content accuracy, arithmetic accuracy, legibility, copy fidelity and completeness/organization
 where those differences matter. A skilled clerk can produce excellent handwritten records; poor penmanship can create interpretation
  errors. Equipment changes specific work rather than applying one OfficeEfficiency statistic.
 11.2 Typewriters & Copying
 Typewriters become commercially possible from 1874 but diffuse unevenly. Their primary ordinary effects are faster/clearer document
  production, greater legibility and improved copy workflows when used with appropriate copying methods. A typewriter does not make
 the underlying number or bookkeeping classification correct. A typed wrong number remains wrong.

 11.3 Other Office Equipment
  Preprinted forms can improve completeness/standardization; cash registers can strengthen transaction capture and cash control;
  adding/calculating machines can reduce arithmetic workload; safes/files improve custody. Equipment should matter most when
 workload justifies it. A tiny owner-operated shop may reasonably use handwritten books for the entire campaign.

 PART XII - HISTORICAL EVIDENCE, AUTHORING & CONFIDENCE
 12.1 Historical Claims Need Provenance
 Research observations used to configure the game should preserve source, place, date/range, relationship type where relevant,
 source type and confidence. An observation from one unusual business or town should remain an observation until broader evidence
  justifies generalization.
 12.2 Preferred Research Objects
   Research object                Purpose

   Evidence Record               One sourced historical observation with exact date/geography and confidence.

   Historical State Record            What was true for a place/network/entity at a particular time.

  Game Authoring Record            Usable availability/range/prerequisite data derived from evidence.

  Canon Decision                   Only the durable rule that should govern simulation behavior.

 12.3 Observation vs General Rule
 Examples: an 1886 Yankton advertisement proving telephone use establishes local evidence, not universal Dakota telephone
 coverage. An exceptionally mechanized 1877 bonanza farm proves early feasibility under exceptional capital/connectivity, not typical
 ownership. A railway map labeled by a later system name does not prove that later corporation was the legal builder/operator in the
  earlier year.
 12.4 Research Data Should Remain Replaceable
  Historical prices, capacities, adoption curves, tariffs and rates should be data-driven/configurable where practical. Better evidence can
 replace a record without architecture rewrites or retroactively changing the meaning of fundamental authorities.
 PART XIII - REPOSITORY/ARCHITECTURE CLEANUP CARRIED FORWARD
 13.1 Repository Audit Still Precedes Implementation Claims
 Revision XXIII/Technical VI architecture remains authoritative as target behavior, but implementation must still map current code
 before migration. The earlier audit identified several classes of duplicate/synthetic truth that remain priority checks if still present:
 Person/Household membership stored from both directions, employment split between Person and business worker slots, household
 demand directly posting retail sales, synthetic periodic household income, synthetic startup business cash, service resolution without
  real Person travel/time and aggregate/town-pulse sales that can create revenue without a legitimate customer/channel.
 13.2 Economic Inflow Must Have Provenance
 CANON LOCK - Ordinary household or business cash may not replenish solely because a week/day/startup threshold
 passed. Wage, owner contribution, loan, sale, remittance, outside employer payment, investment or other inflow must have
 a legitimate source/economic event. Off-map counterparties may remain coarse, but the source class/reason persists.
 13.3 Relationship Authorities
 Household membership, employment and boarding/residential service are different relationships. A boarder can receive
 accommodation/meals without becoming part of the host household's ordinary clothing/medicine/general-goods demand. Employment
 should eventually have one authoritative relationship from which Person workplace/wage and business roster views derive.
 13.4 Customer Execution
  Existing household-need logic may remain a planning source, but local embodied purchase execution must continue through Revision
  XXIII's ProcurementNeed -> acting Person/channel -> Activity/Journey -> supplier availability -> Transaction -> possession/use chain.
 Opening a store or increasing aggregate demand never creates a customer by itself.
 PART XIV - RESEARCH & CALIBRATION HOLDS
 Revision XXV closes architecture and historical-envelope questions while deliberately leaving the following as data/calibration rather
 than universal constants:
   * exact rail freight/passenger tariff tables, timetables and route speeds by year/company;
   * complete legal/corporate succession for every railway branch, locomotive roster, rail weight and bridge rating;
   * exact farm-value percentile bands, machinery ownership percentages and agricultural generation probabilities;

   * historical wages, equipment prices, freight costs and dealer inventories by place/date;
   * weather/yield response coefficients, grasshopper frequency/severity and prairie-fire probabilities;
