 PART XV - REVISION XXV LOCK SUMMARY & SUPERSESSION MAP
 15.1 Hard Locks
   * Open Frontier normally begins in spring 1870 and runs through the 1905 Historical Horizon.
   * Historical regional skeleton + constrained procedural geography + emergent local simulation is the world-generation model.
   * Railway development states are distinct; track laid does not equal service open.
   * Railway physical ownership, legal corporation, operator/lease/controller and historical system identity remain distinct.
   * Road/stage/ferry/river transport are first-class networks and rail reconfigures rather than numerically obsoletes them.
   * Technology progresses through availability, access, supportability and operation, not global unlocks.
   * Environmental and macroeconomic eras alter causal world inputs rather than scripted revenues/yields.
   * Agricultural mechanization remains uneven and task/equipment/capital/connectivity driven.
   * Mail, telegraph, telephone and in-person information share one evidence world; mail-order still requires physical fulfillment.
   * Settlement infrastructure/utility development remains project/network state, not Town Level.
   * Record equipment changes real clerical tasks/evidence quality rather than abstract administration bonuses.
   * Synthetic local sales and unprovenanced recurring/startup cash are rejected where they remain in implementation.
 15.2 Explicit Supersessions
  All prior general Canon wording that makes spring 1880 the ordinary Open Frontier start, defines 1880-1905 as the complete normal
  historical envelope, or describes 1880 equipment reference as the opening-year baseline is superseded to 1870-1905 by this
  integration. Historical statements specifically about conditions in 1880 remain valid as dated mid-campaign evidence.
  Scenario-specific dates are not automatically shifted.
 15.3 Deepening Map
 Revision XXIV historical divergence/1:1 geography is deepened with historically constrained world generation and a 1870 baseline.
 Revision XXIII equipment/capability doctrine is deepened with technology diffusion/supportability. Existing
 Project/Agreement/Transaction doctrines are reused for railway development, civic inducements, mail-order procurement, utility
 connection and transport services. Revision XXIV environmental/livestock causality is generalized into broader environmental
 regimes. Revision XXIII Information/Evidence is deepened with postal/telegraph/telephone channels and historical-source
 provenance.
 END OF REVISION XXV INTEGRATION
 The preserved Canonical Project Bible Revision XXIV follows unchanged and remains authoritative except where Revision XXV
  explicitly adds, deepens, clarifies or supersedes a rule.

 LAND & LEDGERS
 LAND & LEDGERS
CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE - REVISION XXIV
 ASHES & NOTES Rural-Systems Integration: Capability Calibration, Livestock Biology & Markets,
 Land Expansion, Delegated Authority, Calendar UX, World Scale & Historical Divergence
  Revision date: September 21, 2026
 Source baseline: Canonical Project Bible Revision XXIII - September 19, 2026
  Status: Active Canon integration
 PRESERVATION GUARANTEE
  Revision XXIV preserves Revision XXIII in full except where this integration explicitly adds, deepens, clarifies or supersedes prior
  wording. The complete Revision XXIII document follows this integration unchanged as the preserved baseline. Where a conflict
  exists, Revision XXIV controls. Exact playtest prices, wages, farm values, cattle prices, land prices, mortality rates, skill-distribution
  percentages, yields, freight rates, carrying capacities, task durations and other generated values remain calibration unless this
  integration explicitly identifies a design, historical or scenario lock.
 PURPOSE
  Revision XXIV integrates the complete ASHES & NOTES Crisis & Recovery / Agriculture & Property playtest and the subsequent full
  playtest-integration review. The campaign progressed from a burned and indebted single farm through herd rebuilding, dairy-market
  development, rail access, delegated operation, stocker cattle, multiple farms, a small freight company, land assembly and more than
  100,000 pounds of qualifying rail-shipped cattle. The principal result is not a fixed cattle progression or a new table of historical prices.
   It is a deeper causal connection among people, capability, animal biology, land, finance, markets, transport, information and
  delegation.
 REVISION XXIV MASTER DOCTRINE
    • Average means average. Capability bands must retain population meaning; ordinary competent workers must not drift into Great
     merely through routine tenure.
    • Confidence is presentation of knowledge, not capability. High shows one band, Moderate two adjacent bands, Low three
     adjacent bands, and insufficient evidence remains Not enough information.
    • Delegation is the authority mechanic. Manager, foreman, superintendent and general manager are optional descriptive titles
     rather than progression tiers or sources of power.
    • Livestock are persistent biological capital. Breeding, growth, disease, mortality, production, culling and sale arise from actual
     animal state and environment.
    • Mortality is causal. There is no universal calf-death roll. Reproductive and calf loss emerges from biological, environmental,
    management, disease and weather conditions, including correlated events.
    • There is no universal cattle market. Breeding stock, stockers/feeders, finished cattle and culls can face different buyers, evidence,
     timing and transport economics.
    • Stocker cattle are a legitimate business model. Profit comes from buying biological weight, adding value through
     feed/pasture/time and selling through real markets after all costs and risks.
    • Farm production is not automatically sold. Fresh milk, butter, cheese, eggs and other outputs require real outlets, finite buyer
     capacity, processing, storage and logistics.
    • Land control is layered. Owned land, leases, grazing agreements and nonexclusive/open-range use are distinct rights with different
      security.
    • Represented geography is 1:1. Off-map resolution exists because the continental world cannot all be rendered at full detail, not
    because distance is compressed.
    • Historical chronology is a causal baseline, not predestination. Legitimate player and NPC action may alter future commercial
    and infrastructure history.




                                               LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 085/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXIV / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                                    2


    • Information should have provenance. Where an actual worker, buyer, agent, lender or institution is the source, the player should
     normally learn through that source rather than an omniscient generic popup.
    • Scenario objectives measure accomplishments. ASHES & NOTES validates the existing doctrine that ordinary systems create
      difficulty and objectives should not forbid legitimate strategy merely because it is unexpected.
 PART I - CAPABILITY DISTRIBUTION, EXPERIENCE & CONFIDENCE
 1.1 Capability Bands Retain Population Meaning
 CANON LOCK - Average must represent ordinary capability within the relevant reference population. Great, Excellent and
 Mastered are not ordinary endpoints of employee tenure.
  Player-facing bands remain Abysmal / Bad / Poor / Average / Great / Excellent / Mastered. Exact population percentages remain
  calibration, but the underlying distribution should be centrally concentrated around ordinary capability, with Abysmal and Mastered
  occupying relatively rare tails.
  Candidate pools may legitimately differ. An experienced cattle-hand applicant pool should be stronger in cattle work than a random
  adult population. A young or inexperienced applicant should generally begin farther left in relevant occupational capabilities. Selection
  effects change who appears in the pool; they do not redefine what the bands mean.
 1.2 Experience Does Not Equal Excellence
  Capability growth requires relevant learning, challenge, feedback and actual participation. Calendar time or repetition of
  already-routine work must not automatically increase capability. An employee can work a trade for decades and remain Average.
  Another can become Great or Excellent through aptitude, broad difficult experience and consistently strong outcomes.
  Learning should generally diminish as a task becomes routine and as a Person approaches their practical ceiling in that domain.
 Domain familiarity remains separate enough that expertise in one family of work does not create universal competence.
 1.3 Mastered
 Mastered represents exceptional career-level capability. It is not the final rung of a generic XP progression. Long relevant experience
  is normally necessary but never sufficient. As a calibration direction, Mastered will usually be associated with multiple decades of
  meaningful relevant work, often in the approximate 20+ year minimum and 25-35 year career territory discussed during the playtest,
  plus unusual breadth and repeated exceptional results. Exact thresholds remain calibration.
 1.4 Abysmal
 Abysmal represents exceptional inability in one capability. It is not the normal rating for inexperience and is not a global intelligence or
  moral label. Extreme lack of aptitude, poor learning, injury/disability where individually modeled, catastrophic judgment or other
  specific causes can contribute. A Person can be Abysmal in one capability and ordinary or strong elsewhere.
 1.5 Confidence Presentation
 CANON LOCK - High confidence displays one band; Moderate displays two adjacent bands; Low displays three adjacent
 bands; insufficient evidence displays Not enough information.
  Confidence describes the width of the observer's plausible estimate, not the actual skill. Confidence can improve without capability
  improving, and capability can change while the player remains uncertain. Evidence may come from references, demonstrations,
  observed work, outcomes and reputation, with source quality and recency mattering.
 1.6 Playtest Defect - Skill Inflation
 ASHES & NOTES exposed a calibration defect in which too many employees drifted into Great across many unrelated capabilities.
  This is explicitly rejected. Future simulation and QA should treat population-wide upper-band inflation as a regression failure rather
  than desirable progression.
 PART II - DELEGATION, AUTHORITY & OWNER ABSENCE
 2.1 Delegation Is Primary
 CANON LOCK - Delegated authority is the canonical mechanic. Manager, general manager, foreman, superintendent and
  similar titles are optional descriptions of real assignments; titles do not create authority or capability.
 An authority arrangement should answer: who may act, for which business/site/task or decision family, within what financial or
  procedural limits, under what standing policy, and what must be escalated. A trusted farm hand can hold broad operating authority


                                               LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 086/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXIV / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                                    3


  without a formal managerial title. A titled manager can have narrow authority.
 2.2 No Mandatory Management Ladder
 There is no required Manager -> General Manager progression. A Person may oversee several sites when workload, geography,
  information, capability, communication and travel permit it. The title used by UI or narrative remains a presentation choice under
  active design.
 2.3 Layered Delegation
 A delegated Person may coordinate subordinate work when their authority permits it. Scheduling, purchasing, routine livestock
  decisions, staffing, freight dispatch and similar work can be passed downward without hidden owner clicks, while owner-reserved
  actions continue to escalate according to policy.
 2.4 Cross-Business Authority Does Not Merge Businesses
 One Person may hold authority across several controlled businesses. Each business retains separate cash, debt, property, inventory,
  employees, agreements, transactions and operating history unless a real merger or consolidation changes those facts.
 2.5 Delegated Activity
 The existing Manager Activity concept should be broadened in design toward Delegated Activity unless later UX testing establishes
  that the older label is clearer. The player-facing purpose is to answer: What did delegated people decide, perform or resolve so the
 owner did not have to? Events should identify actor, scope, authority source, trigger, decision/action, escalation where any and
 measurable consequence where defensible.
 2.6 Owner Withdrawal Is a Valid Mature State
 A mature agricultural or commercial portfolio may operate with zero routine owner labor when real delegated people, schedules,
  authority, records and controls exist. This is not passive income. The people continue to work and make decisions, obligations
  continue to mature and the owner retains only the authority that has not been delegated.
 PART III - LIVESTOCK IDENTITY, INFORMATION & RECORDS
 3.1 Persistent Animal Identity
 Where individual identity matters, livestock retain stable IDs across birth, ownership changes, reproduction, sale and death. Individual
  identity is particularly important for breeding animals, valuable sires, animals under reproductive or health observation, purchased
  stockers with meaningful provenance, sale candidates and objective-tracked animals.
  Economically useful state can include species/breed context, sex, birth date or estimate, birthplace, breeder/source, ownership
  history, parentage, reproductive history, health history, production history, acquisition basis, commercial class and final disposition.
 3.2 Historical Records Survive Disposition
  Sold or dead animals can collapse into lightweight historical records where pedigree, transaction history, genetic relationships or later
  audit still depends on them. Animal IDs are never reused.
 3.3 Actual State vs Known State
  Underlying animal truth and player knowledge are separate. Examples include actual weight vs estimated weight, actual pregnancy
  vs suspected pregnancy, actual pedigree vs claimed pedigree and actual illness vs signs/diagnosis. Unknown pedigree does not
 mean unrelated. Sellers, breeders, employees and written records may be incomplete, mistaken or deceptive.
 3.4 Terminology
 Male cattle presentation should use Breeding Bull, Breeding Bull Prospect, Bull Calf and Steer. Female presentation should use Type
 = Cow or Heifer, with reproductive state shown separately. A heifer remains a heifer until first calving; pregnancy and lactation are
  states rather than alternate biological types.





                                               LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 087/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXIV / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                                    4

 PART IV - GENETICS, BREEDING & HERD DEVELOPMENT
 4.1 Genetics Are Inherited State
  Breeding quality must not reduce to one generic bonus. Hidden inherited traits can influence supported characteristics such as
  growth, mature size, structure, fertility, calving characteristics, milk production, temperament and survivability. Exact genetic depth is
 an implementation/calibration question, but outcomes should emerge through inherited state and environment.
 4.2 Pedigree Inbreeding
  Pedigree relationship should affect risk through increased homozygosity and inherited trait expression rather than one direct
  Inbreeding Penalty. Genetic problems can become visible during gestation, birth, growth, breeding age or adult production depending
 on the underlying trait.
 4.3 Premium Sire Economics
 A superior sire can improve expected offspring because he contributes inherited material to every calf he sires, but purchase price
  alone does not establish superiority. Evaluation can use credible pedigree, breeder reputation, conformation, feet/legs, temperament,
  growth, fertility and progeny evidence.
  Replacing the herd sire with an unrelated animal makes current matings easier but does not permanently reset inbreeding. Once
  daughters are retained, future sire selection must again account for relationship.
 4.4 Sire Return Is Realized
  Return on an expensive breeding animal emerges through real offspring outcomes, retained daughters, breeding-stock premiums,
  growth, fertility and later herd value. There is no hidden Premium Bull percentage bonus. Retained daughters can be a larger part of
  long-term sire value than extra pounds on steers.
 4.5 Breeding-Stock Sales
 A bull or heifer that is genetically redundant inside one controlled herd may still have substantial value to an unrelated outside buyer.
  Breeding-stock sale and meat-market sale remain different commercial decisions.
 PART V - MALE CATTLE PATHWAYS & CASTRATION
 5.1 Bull Calves Do Not Share One Decision Date
 Not every male calf should remain intact until one universal evaluation age. Where pedigree, parental performance, structure, growth
 and other evidence provide little reason to preserve breeding optionality, early castration and entry into the steer pathway can be
  rational.
 5.2 Preserve Genuine Breeding Optionality
  Promising males may remain intact while evidence accumulates. The value of waiting is the possibility of breeding-stock value; the
  cost includes management difficulty, unwanted breeding risk, market-channel differences and the possibility that later castration is
  less convenient.
 5.3 Bull vs Steer Markets
  Intact males and steers can grow differently and can face different buyer preferences. A breeding bull commands value only where a
  buyer believes the reproductive evidence. A commercial intact male does not automatically receive a premium over a steer merely
 because it remained uncastrated.
 PART VI - LIVESTOCK MORTALITY, CALVING & HEALTH
 6.1 Causal Mortality
 CANON LOCK - Do not implement one flat calf mortality percentage. Reproductive and calf loss must emerge from causal
  biological, environmental, management, disease and weather state.
  Relevant stages include late pregnancy, calving, the first hours, neonatal life, pre-weaning growth and weaning. Relevant inputs can
  include dam nutrition/condition, age/parity, fetal size, presentation, inherited defects, labor duration, observation delay, assistance
  quality, temperature, wind and wetness, shelter, calf vigor, nursing/colostrum success, maternal behavior, bedding, sanitation,
  crowding, infection, respiratory disease, injuries, parasites where supported, predators where relevant and weaning stress.



                                               LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 088/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXIV / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                                    5

 6.2 Correlated Risk
  Livestock deaths are not always independent events. Contaminated crowded maternity space can expose several calves. One cold
 wet storm can strike several births. Purchased cattle can raise pathogen pressure. Shared feed or water problems can affect a cohort.
 The simulation must allow clustered outcomes that share one underlying cause.
 6.3 Shelter Capacity Is Not Health Capacity
 Nominal cattle capacity does not fully describe safe maternity or disease-control capacity. Actual usefulness depends on animal size,
  group composition, bedding, drainage, ventilation/drafts, cleanliness, separation ability, traffic through the space and weather. A farm
 can have enough square footage and still have poor calf-health conditions.
 6.4 Calibration Direction
 The playtest research did not establish one defensible exact Dakota-Territory calf-mortality constant. A provisional historical tuning
  envelope around roughly 8-12 percent loss from late pregnancy/full-term birth through weaning was identified only as a calibration
  target for ordinary operations, with well-run operations capable of doing materially better and bad weather, disease or management
  producing materially worse outcomes. This is a calibration hold, not a Canon probability.
 6.5 ASHES & NOTES Mortality Defect
 The original campaign produced far too few calf deaths for the scale and period. That result is explicitly rejected as a
  simulation-quality baseline. The later corrected season demonstrated the intended kind of causal mix: late-pregnancy loss, stillbirth,
  exposure, enteric disease and respiratory loss, including clustered outcomes.
 PART VII - LIVESTOCK COMMERCE & STOCKER/FEEDER CATTLE
 7.1 Stocker/Feeder Operations
  Buying young or unfinished cattle, adding economically valuable biological weight and reselling them is a first-class rural business
  strategy distinct from maintaining a breeding cow-calf herd.
  Profit arises from purchase cost, starting weight and condition, biological gain, pasture, stored feed, water, labor, health losses,
  land/access costs, financing, transport, market conditions and sale timing. There is no Stocker Profit bonus.
 7.2 Scaling Stocker Operations
 A successful small lot can justify a larger later commitment, but cash alone does not create carrying capacity. Pasture, winter feed,
  water, shelter, labor, disease separation, transport, working capital and buyer depth remain binding. The player may knowingly
  overstock or overleverage and accept the consequences.
 7.3 Livestock Working-Capital Credit
 Purchased cattle may be financed through historically appropriate seller notes, livestock-secured credit, merchant arrangements or
  other supported structures. Financing cost reduces actual contribution. The financed animals remain assets and may be collateral.
 7.4 Creditor Workouts
 A maturing livestock note need not force an automatic sale if the creditor has reason to extend, restructure or refinance. Any
  extension remains a real agreement with cost and risk rather than a scripted rescue.
 PART VIII - LIVESTOCK MARKETS, SALES & SEASONALITY
 8.1 No Universal Sell-Cattle Market
 CANON LOCK - Breeding stock, stocker/feeder animals, finished commercial cattle and cull cattle may face different
  buyers, evidence, costs and prices. The game must not collapse them into one universal cattle price or Sell button.
  Valid channels can include private farm sale, local dealer/aggregator, feeder/stocker buyer, slaughter/cull buyer, railhead buyer,
  distant commission market, breeding-stock private sale, herd dispersal/breeder sale and historically appropriate fair or exposition
  channels.





                                               LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 089/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXIV / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                                    6

 8.2 Dated Market Opportunities
 Some livestock opportunities can exist as dated events with location, entry deadline, sale date, eligible classes,
  documentation/evidence, fees, buyer pool, transport requirement and settlement terms. Special sales gather different buyers; they do
  not guarantee better prices.
 8.3 Commission Merchants
 A producer may use a commission merchant or agent to reach a distant livestock or produce market. The relationship can include
  market information, consignment, commission, shipment coordination, inspection, handling/yard expenses and settlement. The agent
  improves access; the agent does not guarantee profit.
 8.4 Seasonal Markets Are Causal
 Do not apply month-based price modifiers simply because a season historically tended to be stronger or weaker. Seasonal outcomes
  should arise through actual supply, feed pressure, pasture conditions, animal finishing, buyer demand, credit and transport
  availability.
 8.5 Holding vs Selling
 A sale-timing policy should compare expected marginal value from further gain against feed, land, labor, health risk, market risk,
  capital tie-up and opportunity cost. The player or manager never knows the future price top with certainty.
 8.6 Rail Qualification
  Rail-shipment objectives qualify only from actual qualifying physical shipment and recorded liveweight/origin evidence. Booking a
  shipment, owning a railway connection or selling to a rail buyer is not sufficient if the cattle have not physically moved according to the
  authored predicate.
 PART IX - DAIRY, EGGS & FARM PRODUCT PROCESSING
 9.1 Production Is Not Sale
 CANON LOCK - Milk produced is not automatically milk sold, and eggs laid are not automatically eggs sold. Farm products
  require actual customers, agreements, internal use, storage, processing or loss/spoilage.
 9.2 Finite Buyer Capacity
 A recurring buyer can have practical quantity limits that vary with season, their own customers, working capital, spoilage risk, storage
 and resale performance. There is no invisible infinite buyer behind a standing account.
 9.3 Dairy Allocation
  Milk can flow among calf nursing, household/employee consumption, fresh sale, butter, cheese, other supported processing,
  animal-feed/byproduct use and spoilage. Processing allocation should use actual available milk rather than one abstract Dairy Output
  value.
 9.4 Fresh Milk
  Fresh milk has short practical market reach unless real transport speed, handling/cooling and receiving arrangements extend it.
 Nearby high-net-price customers can rationally receive priority before milk is converted into more durable products. A wagon route
 can widen the fresh-milk market when actual time and conditions permit.
 9.5 Butter
  Butter converts highly perishable milk into a denser and more durable product but requires labor, equipment, packing, storage and
  quality control. Rail or distant buyer access creates market reach, not free processing capacity.
 9.6 Cheese
 Cheese is a legitimate processing path where history, capability and demand support it. Cheesemaking may require specialized
  knowledge, workspace, vats or vessels, rennet/ingredients, curd handling, pressing, curing/storage and delayed sale. It must not be a
  one-click Milk -> More Valuable Product conversion. Larger cheese/creamery operations may aggregate milk from surrounding farms
 where historically and economically justified.





                                               LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 090/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXIV / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                                    7

 9.7 Dairy Byproducts
 Whey, buttermilk, skim milk and other residues should be represented only where they create meaningful feed, disposal or customer
  decisions. Their existence can support integrated livestock choices such as feeding pigs, but should not force unnecessary
 micromanagement.
 9.8 Poultry
 Egg output remains biological and seasonal. Eggs set for incubation are unavailable for sale. Chicks do not immediately become
  adult laying inventory. Poultry breeding, household use, mortality and surplus males remain physical outcomes rather than a fixed
 Eggs Per Day business stat.
 PART X - LAND, RANGE & AGRICULTURAL EXPANSION
 10.1 Rural Control Types
  Agricultural scale can expand through fee ownership, purchase contracts, tenancy/lease, seasonal grazing agreements, other lawful
 use rights and nonexclusive/open-range use where historically applicable. These relationships must not be collapsed into one Owned
  Acres number.
 10.2 Parcel-Level Acquisition
 The player should be able to inspect nearby parcels and pursue control through the appropriate owner or legal process. A private
 owner can be approached for sale or lease. Corporate or railroad land may require an agent. Public-domain land uses the applicable
  entry process rather than a private Make Offer action. Restricted land does not become purchasable merely because it is visible.
 10.3 Open Range Is Insecure
 CANON LOCK - Nonexclusive open-range use is not ownership, not a lease and not permanent carrying capacity.
 A ranch can benefit from land it does not securely control while accepting that settlement, legal claims, fencing, competing grazing or
  policy change can reduce or eliminate that access. Losing such use is not confiscation of a player asset if no secure right existed.
 10.4 Land Assembly vs Whole-Farm Acquisition
 A growing operation may acquire another farm or assemble additional land around an existing operation. A whole farm may add
  buildings, wells, fences, labor and livestock but creates another operating site. Adjacent land strengthens one site but may require
 new fencing, water and shelter. Neither route is universally superior.
 10.5 Adjacency Has Operational Value
 Nearby land and farms can reduce travel, herding, fencing, dispatch and supervision burden. Adjacency therefore affects real
 economic value rather than merely map aesthetics.
 10.6 Land Market Agency
 A neighboring owner can refuse to sell, ask more, offer a lease or have legal/title constraints. Land does not become available simply
 because the player clicks it.
 10.7 Calibration Hold - Farm and Acre Prices
 ASHES & NOTES exposed likely underpricing in several farm-acquisition values. Those playtest prices are calibration placeholders
 and must not be treated as historical anchors. Rural valuation and financing terms require dated regional calibration.
 PART XI - FREIGHT, HORSES & PORTFOLIO LOGISTICS
 11.1 Micro-Freight Company
 A legitimate local freight business can begin with one team, one wagon and one teamster and may have no yard or warehouse.
  Capability derives from actual animals, vehicle, driver, stable/feed access, cargo handling and route rights. Lack of a yard means lack
  of magical storage.





                                               LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 091/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXIV / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                                    8

 11.2 Portfolio Freight
 An owned freight company may haul for controlled farms and take outside work when capacity is available. Internal service still
 consumes animals, labor, feed, wear and time. Separate businesses may record real intercompany charges, while consolidated
  reporting must not treat internal transfers as external profit.
 11.3 Rail Complements Wagon Freight
  Rail can create local collection, drayage and depot-interface demand rather than eliminating wagons. Freight can also extend
  fresh-product selling radius and reduce dependence on ad hoc trips by farm labor.
 11.4 Expansion Follows Persistent Utilization
 One seasonal spike does not automatically justify another freight team. Repeated profitable refusals during ordinary weeks are
  stronger evidence that permanent capacity is constrained.
 11.5 Horse Capital
 Horse ownership should solve real work or travel constraints. A dedicated riding/management horse can be valuable because it
  leaves a work team available. Hiring or borrowing draft power can outperform ownership for seasonal peaks. Permanent animals
  carry year-round feed and care cost.
 PART XII - CALENDAR, HUD & CHARACTER-SOURCED INFORMATION
 12.1 Universal Calendar
 Land & Ledgers should provide one player-facing calendar with year/month overview and drill-down to month, week and day. The
  interface may use familiar modern calendar conventions for usability even though the world itself remains historical.
 Known events can include payroll, debt payments, supplier credit, rents/leases, agreement deadlines, planned shipment
  departures/arrivals, projects, expected calving windows, weaning/evaluation dates, market events and player-created notes.
 12.2 Delegated Events Remain Visible
  Delegating work does not remove important dates from the owner's calendar. A delegated calving or shipment can remain visible with
  the responsible Person/business identified.
 12.3 Exact Dates vs Forecast Windows
 CANON LOCK - The calendar must preserve uncertainty. Known due dates display as dates; biological, shipment or market
  forecasts may display as windows/ranges.
 12.4 Calendar Filters
  Players may hide categories without changing simulation. Candidate families include payroll, finance/debt, property/rent, contracts,
  freight, livestock, markets, projects and personal notes. Exact defaults remain UX calibration.
 12.5 Main Financial HUD
 The universal top-level financial presentation should prioritize Date, Owner Cash, current Business Cash and Debt/Liabilities.
  Scenario-specific state such as cattle, hay, shelter or stocker lots belongs in contextual panels rather than the universal strip.
 12.6 Information Should Have a Source
 Where a legitimate Person, business or institution is the source of commercially useful information, player-facing presentation should
  preserve that provenance. A buyer can say they cannot take more butter. A farm hand can report bedding problems. A freight agent
 can report a delayed car. A lender can warn of an obligation. Generic system notices remain appropriate for UI-owned information
 such as objective completion and calendar organization.
 12.7 Guidance Without Solving the Game
 Because period business practice is unfamiliar to modern players, NPCs and contextual actions may explain plausible mechanisms
 such as contacting a station agent, hiring a commission merchant or processing surplus milk. Guidance should expose options and
 mechanics rather than identify the mathematically optimal strategy.

 PART XIII - WORLD SCALE, HISTORICAL BASELINE & SCENARIO
 BASIS
 13.1 One-to-One Spatial Scale
 CANON LOCK - Represented world distance uses 1:1 physical scale. Off-map/coarse simulation exists because a
  continental world cannot all be rendered at full detail, not because local geography is compressed.
 When a represented road is one mile in the simulation, it should correspond to approximately one real mile of economic/travel
  distance. Off-map transitions preserve travel time, route, cargo, identity and cost.
 13.2 Historical Baseline Is Causal, Not Predestined
  Historical chronology establishes starting geography, institutions, outside actors, technologies, known projects and plausible
  intentions. It does not reserve future outcomes against legitimate player or NPC action.
   If the player buys land another actor historically acquired, establishes a railway, changes a route, founds a competing business or
  otherwise changes the prerequisites that produced historical development, later commercial and infrastructure history may diverge.
 The game must not reject a valid action merely because history later used that land or opportunity differently.
 13.3 Historical Actors Persist in the Changed World
  Historical actors continue pursuing plausible goals according to their resources, knowledge, rights and incentives after divergence.
  Historical dates may introduce actors, technologies, political conditions or outside projects, but must not force a local result whose
  prerequisites no longer exist.
 13.4 Historical, Fictional & Emergent Settlements
  Real towns, fictional scenario settlements and settlements that emerge from simulation may coexist. Historical settlements preserve
  their historical starting identity and geography where relevant. Fictional settlements allow authored scenarios within the same
  historical economy. Sufficient player or NPC development may create a durable new settlement that can receive an appropriate
  world-generated or player-selected name.
 13.5 Scenario Basis Labels
  Scenario selection should distinguish historically based and fictional authored scenarios. Current preferred badges are HISTORICAL
 and FICTIONAL. Historical means the opening premise/geography/actors are materially based on documented history; it does not
 mean outcomes are scripted. Fictional means the authored premise or local setting is invented but still follows the historical world's
  technology, law and economy. Historical scenarios may expose a short Historical Basis section.
 PART XIV - ASHES & NOTES CANONICAL SCENARIO UPDATE
 14.1 Scenario Identity
 ASHES & NOTES remains a Crisis & Recovery / Agriculture & Property scenario. The player begins with an operating farm and
  meaningful secured/seller debt after a major physical fire destroys much of the productive/residential base. Recovery uses ordinary
  systems: rebuild, sell, haul, contract, refinance, negotiate, lease, restructure, partner, change commercial direction or expand into
 new businesses.
 14.2 Objective Philosophy
  Objectives continue to measure accomplishments rather than prescribe strategy. The player is not required to employ a specific
 number of workers, retain every asset, use stocker cattle, acquire multiple farms or become debt-free unless such a restriction is
  explicitly authored as an objective.

 14.4 Removed / Rejected Objectives
 The former requirement to sell ten cattle in one sale is removed. A proposed employee-count objective is rejected because staffing
  should emerge from workload. A debt-payoff-without-missed-payment objective is not currently part of the locked structure because
  ordinary debt service already exists as a causal business constraint.
 14.5 Objective Presentation
  Incomplete objectives should show exact numeric progress rather than generic In Progress text. Once an event objective is
  completed, the scenario UI should retain its completion date and evidence instead of replacing it with later current totals. Separate
  lifetime metrics may continue updating.
 14.6 Calibration Holds
 The playtest completed the 100,000-pound objective by May 1878, well before the 1890 deadline. This may indicate generous
  pacing, successful leveraged strategy, underpriced land/cattle or a combination. Deadline and economic rebalance require
  comparative runs before any further objective change. Exact opening farm price, later acquisitions and most generated economic
  values remain calibration.
 PART XV - RESEARCH & CALIBRATION HOLDS
  Revision XXIV locks system behavior while explicitly leaving the following as researched/calibrated data rather than universal
  constants:
    • capability-band population shares and the final rarity of Abysmal/Mastered;
    • exact experience envelope associated with Mastered;
    • historical calf mortality by region, year, management type and stage;
    • dystocia, stillbirth, scours, respiratory disease and treatment frequencies;
    • regional cattle growth rates, prices, breeding premiums and stocker spreads;
    • milk, butter, cheese and egg yields, prices, spoilage and buyer capacities;
    • rural wages, farm prices, acre values, railroad-land terms and seller-finance customs;
    • the private/public/railroad-land mix for specific regions and dates;
    • open-range legal/customary access by place and year;
    • forage carrying capacity, hay yields and winter-feed requirements;
    • shelter costs, capacities and maternity-space performance;
    • horse/wagon purchase and operating costs and local freight rates;
    • ASHES & NOTES objective pacing and the economic effects of aggressive leverage.

 PART XVI - REVISION XXIV LOCK SUMMARY & DEEPENING MAP
 16.1 Revision XXIV Hard Locks
    • Average retains ordinary population meaning; capability bands cannot inflate until Great becomes the default.
    • High/Moderate/Low confidence must render one/two/three adjacent bands respectively.
    • Delegation is primary; management titles are descriptive and do not create capability or authority.
    • Livestock identity, pedigree, biological state and player knowledge remain distinct authoritative/observed facts.
    • Mortality emerges causally and may be correlated across animals.
    • Stocker/feeder cattle are a legitimate livestock-commerce lane.
    • Livestock markets are differentiated by commercial use, buyer/channel and physical delivery.
    • Farm production is not automatically sold; repeat buyers have finite capacity.
    • Owned, leased, contractual grazing and open-range use are distinct land-control relationships.
    • Represented geography uses 1:1 physical scale; off-map is resolution, not compressed geography.
    • Historical chronology is a causal baseline and may diverge through legitimate world action.
    • A universal calendar projects known and forecast events without becoming a second authority.
    • Important commercial information should preserve a legitimate in-world source where one exists.
    • ASHES & NOTES uses the revised 15,000-pound and 100,000-pound rail objectives; the ten-head single-sale and employee-count
     objectives remain removed.
 16.2 Deepening Map
    • Revision XXIII continuous-Person and capability doctrine is deepened by population-calibrated capability meaning and anti-inflation
      rules.
    • Revision XXI/XXII delegation and Full Autonomy are deepened by a delegation-first authority model and optional management titles.
    • Existing agriculture biological-capital doctrine is deepened by persistent animal identity, genetics, male pathways and causal
      mortality.
    • Existing livestock-commerce doctrine is deepened by explicit stocker/feeder strategy and differentiated livestock markets.
    • Existing physical logistics and freight doctrine is deepened by micro-carriers, portfolio hauling and rail/wagon complementarity.
    • Existing property/provenance doctrine is deepened by parcel-level agricultural acquisition, railroad land, grazing rights and insecure
     open-range use.
    • Existing historical-skeleton doctrine is clarified so player action can causally alter future commercial/infrastructure history.
    • Existing large-world/on-map/off-map doctrine is deepened by an explicit 1:1 distance requirement.
    • Existing UI/read-model doctrine is deepened by a universal calendar, exact financial HUD and character-sourced information.
    • ASHES & NOTES is deepened from a general crisis-recovery concept into the tested agriculture/rail objective structure above.
 END OF REVISION XXIV INTEGRATION
 The preserved Canonical Project Bible Revision XXIII follows unchanged and remains authoritative except where Revision XXIV
  explicitly adds, deepens, clarifies or supersedes a rule.

LAND & LEDGERS
 CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE - REVISION XXIII
 Commercial & Human Continuity Integration: Continuous Personhood, Physical Capability &
 Equipment, Agreement/Transaction/Project Depth, Institutional Authority & Long-Run Continuity
 Revision date: September 19, 2026
 Source baseline: Canonical Project Bible Revision XXII - September 18, 2026
 Status: Active Canon integration

 PRESERVATION GUARANTEE
 Revision XXIII preserves Revision XXII in full except where this integration explicitly adds, deepens, clarifies or supersedes
  prior wording. The complete Revision XXII document follows this integration unchanged as the preserved baseline. Where
 a conflict exists, Revision XXIII controls. Exact wages, prices, equipment prices, equipment counts, task durations, tool
 wear rates, household-consumption quantities, insurance premiums, legal time limits, utility tariffs, project allowances and
 other generated values remain calibration unless this integration explicitly identifies a design or historical lock.
 PURPOSE
 Revision XXIII integrates the post-Contractor depth review, including the dedicated continuous-Person pass, the
 occupation/equipment research pass and the subsequent shared-authority cleanup. It does not add a new progression
 ladder. It deepens the connective tissue of the existing economy so that people, work, tools, contracts, transactions,
 organizations and institutions remain physically and economically continuous.
 The principal result is a stricter doctrine: local economic activity must be attributable to real Persons, households,
 businesses and institutions; work capability must arise from real people, tools, equipment, space, materials and authority;
 and broad systems such as Agreements, Projects, governance, succession, internal controls, law, insurance, distress and
  utilities must use reusable shared lifecycles instead of shallow bespoke flags.
 REVISION XXIII MASTER DOCTRINE
    • Every local Person is a persistent human actor through time. Work, unemployment, shopping, meals, drinking, sleep,
     family life, travel, illness, migration and business interaction are states and activities of that same Person.
    • No anonymous local customer. Ordinary local sales and services require a real economic principal and, when
    embodied action is required, a specific acting Person. Aggregate demand may summarize history; it may not fabricate
     transactions.
    • Time is exclusive across life, not only across paid work. A Person cannot work, shop, travel, sleep or socialize in
      physically incompatible places at the same time.
    • Households remain ordinary domestic-economic consumption units, but individuals perform physical actions. The
     payer, acting Person and beneficiary may be different legitimate entities.
    • Business capability emerges from actual people, tools/equipment, suitable space, materials/inputs, legal or
     organizational authority, information and available time. A business label does not grant a capability by itself.
    • Equipment requirements attach primarily to tasks/capabilities rather than rigid occupations. Ownership is not
      universally required; equipment can be owned, leased, borrowed, rented, contractor-supplied or obtained through hired
     service where historically plausible.
    • Customer traffic, market demand, Opportunity & Pressure and business-attractiveness summaries are derived
     observations over real needs, awareness, choices and transactions. They are not independent sale generators.
    • Agreement existence, obligation performance, physical fulfillment, acceptance, economic recognition, cash settlement
    and bookkeeping are different states. Partial performance remains partial rather than collapsing to success/failure.
    • Projects preserve baseline estimate, current forecast and actual outcome as distinct histories. Changes, delays and
     cost growth should not overwrite the original promise.




                                               LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 096/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXIII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                                 2



    • Governance, succession, internal controls, insurance, dispute resolution, distress, civic projects, utilities and labor
     markets use real counterparties, rights, resources, information and procedures rather than generic scores.
    • Simulation resolution can reduce detail but cannot change ontology. Coarse/off-map activity must reconcile to the
    same Persons, assets, cash, inventory, obligations, relationships and histories that exist on-map.
 PART I - SHARED-AUTHORITY CLEANUP & ONE-TRUTH DOCTRINE
 1.1 One Authority Per Consequential Fact
 When several systems need the same consequential truth, they should query or derive it from one authority rather than
 store competing copies. Read models may summarize or forecast authoritative state but cannot become a second causal
 source.
 1.2 Economic Event, Bookkeeping & Lifetime Ledger
 Economic events own what actually happened: goods moved, a service was accepted, cash changed hands, a receivable
 arose, an asset was acquired or a loss was recognized. Bookkeeping records those events. The Lifetime Ledger
 aggregates qualifying history. Neither bookkeeping nor scenario summaries may manufacture an economic event that did
 not occur.
 1.3 Agreement & Obligation Authority
 Supply agreements, construction contracts, freight contracts, employment terms, leases, concessions, finance
 agreements, utility service arrangements and similar commitments share a common conceptual grammar: parties,
  obligations, conditions, performance windows, pricing/consideration, allocation of cost/risk, amendment, breach/cure,
 termination and evidence of performance. Domain-specific terms remain specialized data rather than separate contract
  truth.
 1.4 Person Time & Activity Authority
 Employment scheduling, management work, travel, shopping, sleep, domestic work, school, medical care and leisure must
 consume one authoritative Person time budget. Domain systems may request or create activities, but none may
 independently decide that a Person is free when another authoritative activity already occupies incompatible time.
 1.5 Information & Evidence Authority
 Awareness, market research, references, competitor intelligence, lender diligence and reputation evidence should use one
 information/evidence grammar where practical: subject, source, observer, time learned, evidence type, confidence,
 staleness and access. A rumor, signed agreement, ledger entry, witnessed event and manager estimate are not equally
 strong evidence.
 1.6 Shared Resource Reservation
 Workers, wagons, horses, machines, workstations, inventory lots, project stockpiles, freight capacity and committed funds
  all require defensible reservation/commitment semantics. A resource cannot be promised twice merely because two
 domain systems use different labels.
 1.7 Rights & Relationship Query Layer
 Ownership, possession, occupancy, leasehold, employment, management authority, corporate office, security interest,
 easement and service rights remain legally/economically distinct. Systems should use a common way to ask what right or
  authority a Person/entity has over a thing without collapsing those distinct relationships into one Owner field.
 1.8 Derived Demand, Traffic & Opportunity
 MarketDemand, CustomerTraffic, LaborPressure, HousingPressure and Opportunity/Pressure may exist as read models
 or synthesized evidence, but they are not independent causal authorities. A traffic chart summarizes Persons who actually
  visited. Lost-sales evidence comes from failed or abandoned real purchase attempts. Opportunity analysis interprets
  existing conditions rather than spawning the conditions.
 PART II - CONTINUOUS PERSONHOOD & DAILY LIFE
 2.1 Continuous Personhood
 Every Person who participates in the simulated regional economy retains persistent identity and history across
 employment, household membership, housing, travel, consumption, relationships, health and aging. Employment loss,
  retirement, injury or temporary travel changes state; it does not suspend personhood.



                                               LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 097/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXIII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                                 3



  CANON LOCK - No temporary anonymous worker, shopper, drinker, hotel guest, resident or local customer
   may be created solely to satisfy a demand, traffic or labor calculation when the activity is meant to occur
    inside the represented regional economy.
 2.2 Economic Principal, Acting Person & Beneficiary
 A household, business or institution may be the economic principal while a specific Person performs the physical action. A
  father can buy boots for a child; a manager can order lumber for a business; a boarder can receive a meal paid through a
 boarding arrangement. Transactions and activities should preserve these roles when materially relevant.
 2.3 The Day Belongs to the Person
 A Person has one continuous day. Paid work, management, travel, household duties, errands, job search, school, meals,
  social/leisure activity, medical care and sleep compete for time. The player need not see minute-by-minute life simulation,
 but the underlying schedule cannot permit physical contradictions.
 2.4 Sleep & Nightly Shelter
 Each Person needs a legitimate nightly state such as household accommodation, rented room, boarding bed, hotel room,
 employer bunk, camp, temporary hosting, travel lodging, precarious shelter or explicit no-stable-shelter state. Residential
 Occupancy answers the continuing shelter arrangement; actual Sleep answers where and when the Person rested that
  night. They are related but not identical facts.
 2.5 Food, Meals & Nutrition
 Food remains primarily a household/institution inventory and budget problem rather than a bite-by-bite minigame. Meals
 must nevertheless have a legitimate source. Household food, board-included meals, employment meals, purchased
 prepared food, restaurant/saloon meals or another real source can satisfy Persons. Nutrition/food adequacy is a
 consequence of actual access, reserves, affordability and regularity rather than an independent FoodPoints inventory.
 2.6 Water & Alcohol Are Distinct
 Ordinary hydration can be represented through practical access at home, work, institutions and travel without simulating
 every cup. Alcohol is discretionary Person-specific consumption. Saloon drink revenue requires a real patron, real
  inventory, service and payment/credit. Alcohol can affect spending, time, sleep, fatigue and behavior where relevant
 without requiring a perfect biological BAC simulation or moral score.
 2.7 Family & Domestic Labor
 Cooking, cleaning, laundry, water/fuel handling, childcare, elder care, household animal care, gardens, coops, boarding
 work and similar domestic production consume real Person time. Allocation depends on actual household composition,
  capability, availability, relationships and historically calibrated behavior rather than fixed gender penalties. Family labor
 remains labor even when no ordinary wage is paid.
 2.8 Children, Elderly, Sick & Disabled Persons
 A child is not merely a dependency number. Age-appropriate schooling, chores, care, consumption, skill formation and
 family work can occur where supported. Elderly, sick and disabled Persons remain consumers, owners, relatives,
 knowledge holders and potential contributors even when wage labor capacity falls. Reduced labor participation never
 deletes a Person from society.
 2.9 Unemployment Does Not Suspend Life
 An unemployed Person can still have savings, household support, prior wages, casual earnings, remittances, credit,
 property income or assets. They may have more daytime availability for job search, errands, shopping, social contact and
 services while simultaneously facing greater future-income uncertainty. No Job does not mean No Consumption or Idle
  Until Hired.
 2.10 Travelers, Visitors & Transients
 A traveler who physically enters or participates in the represented regional economy should be a persistent or promoted
 Person with origin, destination/purpose, means, transport, lodging/food needs and timing. Hotel, livery, meal, saloon and
 store transactions should attach to that Person. Returning visitors should retain identity where practical.
 2.11 Coarse Simulation Preserves Ontology
 A Person may be represented through activity blocks, scheduled events or coarse travel outside the active region, but the
 same identity, location continuity, money/household state and commitments persist. Coarse simulation may compress




                                               LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 098/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXIII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                                 4



  footsteps; it cannot fabricate time, purchases or duplicate a Person.
 PART III - REAL CUSTOMER DEMAND, SHOPPING & SERVICE USE
 3.1 Household/Person Procurement Loop
 Ordinary local consumption follows a causal loop: need/reserve change -> awareness of possible sources -> decision
 whether to act now -> selection of acting Person or delivery mechanism -> travel/contact -> supplier availability ->
 service/choice -> transaction or abandonment/substitution -> possession/use -> future need state. Needs can be
 postponed or go unsatisfied.
 3.2 Opening Hours Create Availability, Not Customers
 A business being open does not spawn traffic. Opening hours only make service possible to Persons whose needs,
 schedules, location, knowledge and means overlap with those hours. A late-closing store may capture workers who cannot
 shop earlier; a closed store may lose the sale, delay it or push the customer to a rival.
 3.3 Feasible Choice Sets
 A supplier is not in a customer's feasible choice set if the customer does not know about it, cannot reach it, cannot
  afford/finance the purchase, the store is closed, stock/service is unavailable or timing is unacceptable. Price, quality,
 distance, wait, trust, credit, prior experience, reliability and suitability can then shape choice among feasible options.
 3.4 Substitution, Reduction & Abandonment
 When the preferred purchase fails, the Person/household may accept a substitute, use another supplier, reduce quantity,
 delay, borrow/use credit, produce internally or go without depending on urgency, alternatives and circumstances. Failed
 purchase attempts should create evidence for merchants and Opportunity/Pressure without automatically generating a
 sale elsewhere.
 3.5 Repeat Business & Relationship Memory
 Repeat trade should emerge from actual experiences: reliable stock, fair dealing, product quality, useful credit, service
 speed, convenience and social/commercial relationships. Marketing primarily changes awareness and consideration;
 operations and experience create retention.
 PART IV - PHYSICAL CAPABILITY, EQUIPMENT & WORKSTATIONS
 4.1 Capability Formula
 A task is executable only when the relevant combination exists: capable Person(s) + required tool/equipment method +
  suitable workspace/location + materials/inputs + motive power where needed + authority/right + available time.
 Information/diagnosis may also be required for tasks whose problem is not yet known.
  CANON LOCK - A job title or business label never grants physical capability by itself. Capability emerges from
   the actual resources and people that can perform the task.
 4.2 Requirement Types
    • Hard requirement - the task is physically impossible without a suitable item/setup.
    • Alternative equipment set - several historically plausible methods can perform the same task.
    • Capacity equipment - manual work remains possible but equipment materially changes throughput, acreage, crew
    need or time.
    • Workstation - a fixed or prepared operating place such as forge, oven, print press, compounding bench, saw line or
      bar.
    • Shared capital asset - a wagon, thresher, steam engine, locomotive, hoist, dynamo or other scarce durable productive
     asset.
    • Personal/small tool kit - ordinary hand tools grouped for usability while preserving their real contents.
    • Consumable - fuel, nails, shoes, twine, ink, chemicals, medicine ingredients and similar items consumed through work.
    • Motive power - human, horse, mule, ox, water, steam or electric power where historically and physically appropriate.
    • Support equipment - ladders, scaffolds, lighting, storage, jacks, pumps, animal restraint or other enabling gear.




                                               LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 099/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXIII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                                 5



 4.3 Task Requirements, Not Occupation Gates
 A Farmer does not require every farm implement at all times. PlowField may require a plow, draft power and harness;
 HandHarvestGrain may use a cradle/sickle method; MechanicalHarvest may require a reaper/binder and team. A Person
 may perform compatible tasks across occupations when capability and circumstances allow.
 4.4 Access Instead of Mandatory Ownership
 The performer may use employer-owned, household-owned, rented, leased, borrowed, customer-supplied,
 contractor-supplied or hired-service equipment. A small farm can hire a traveling threshing outfit rather than own one. A
 contractor can rent a scraper. A repairperson can travel with a field kit while large machine work remains shop-bound.
 4.5 Location, Reservation & Condition
 Tools and equipment have location and availability. A wagon at another worksite is unavailable. One exclusive machine
 cannot perform two jobs simultaneously. Condition, maintenance and defects can reduce capacity or make a method
 unusable, feeding the existing repair/failure systems.
 4.6 Tool-Kit Abstraction
 Ordinary small tools may be grouped into historically defined kits to avoid inventory micromanagement. A Carpenter Hand
 Tool Kit still canonically contains saws, planes, chisels, brace/bits, square and related hand tools; the player need not
 maintain twenty-seven individual chisels unless an individual object becomes materially important.
 4.7 Mechanization Is Usually Scale, Not a Binary Tech Gate
 Hand methods may remain physically possible at small scale while animal-powered or powered machinery changes
 throughput and labor economics. Large acreage, industrial volume or contract deadlines can make the slower method
 commercially infeasible without making it physically impossible.

 adoption and specialist sub-tools remain data/calibration unless separately locked. Future occupations must follow the
 same task-level rule rather than receiving a generic Tools=true flag.

 5.17 Household Domestic Equipment Baseline
 People can exist without formal employment, but an ordinary household needs physical domestic capability for the way it
  lives. The simulation should distinguish access to sleeping arrangements, heating, cooking, water, washing, laundry,
  sanitation, food storage and light where those functions are materially simulated.

   Domestic function                  Physical capability
   Sleep                            Bed/bunk or legitimate sleeping arrangement; bedding.
   Heating                              Stove/hearth or other supported heat source; fuel; safe vent/chimney where required.

 PART VI - AGREEMENTS, ECONOMIC EVENTS & PROJECT
 EXECUTION DEPTH
 6.1 Commercial Commitment Lifecycle
 Use a reusable lifecycle: inquiry/proposal -> negotiation/counterproposal -> conditional or final acceptance -> effective
 agreement -> individual obligations mature -> attempted performance -> inspection/acceptance -> payment/deficiency ->
 cure/waiver/dispute -> completion/renewal/termination. Conditions precedent can delay effectiveness or performance
 without pretending no agreement exists.
 6.2 Obligations Are Smaller Than Agreements
 An agreement can contain multiple obligations with different obligors, due dates, performance standards and
 consequences. A lumber contract can obligate the seller to deliver, the buyer to provide unloading, the buyer to pay after
 accepted delivery and the seller to replace rejected material. Performance should be measured obligation by obligation.
 6.3 Partial Performance, Defect & Breach
 Delayed, incomplete, defective, unauthorized-substitution, non-payment and repudiation outcomes remain distinct.
 Accepted quantity, rejected quantity, outstanding quantity, invoice amount and paid amount can all differ. Cure, waiver,
  renegotiation, withholding or termination must result from actual rights/choices.
 6.4 Economic Event Lifecycle
 Use the sequence Intent/Order -> Commitment/Reservation -> Fulfillment -> Acceptance -> Economic Recognition ->
 Settlement -> Adjustment/Reversal -> Historical Record. A deposit is cash but may not yet be fully earned revenue. Credit
 sale can create revenue/receivable without cash. Receivable collection is cash but not a second sale. Return, bad debt,
 spoilage or later-discovered error can append correcting events rather than erasing history.
 6.5 Capital Assets Versus Operating Inputs
 Buying a wagon, boiler, building or machine changes cash and asset state but is not economically identical to consuming
  flour or paying wages. Asset cost basis, continued ownership, condition, productive use and later disposal should remain
 traceable enough to measure real gain/loss without turning the game into a modern accounting textbook.
 6.6 Project Baseline, Forecast & Actual
 Every consequential Project should preserve the original approved estimate/schedule as Baseline, the best current
 expectation as Current Forecast and completed outcome as Actual. Hidden site conditions, supplier delay, customer
 change, rework or weather can change the forecast without rewriting the original bid.
 6.7 Work Packages, Change Orders & Acceptance
 Projects decompose into meaningful Work Packages and Tasks with dependencies, resources, materials, location and
 acceptance conditions. Customer changes, design changes, unknown conditions, substitutions and defects can create
  explicit change proposals/orders. Completion can pass through substantial physical completion, inspection,
  punch-list/corrective work, acceptance, final account/payment and any supported warranty/defect responsibility.
 PART VII - NPC PLANNING, CUSTOMER CHOICE & INFORMATION
 DEPTH
 7.1 Persistent NPC Plans




                                               LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 105/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXIII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                                11



 NPC owners/managers should form and revise plans rather than resolve every decision through one instantaneous utility
 score. A plan may progress through awareness, investigation, inspection, estimates, financing, negotiation, commitment,
 development, opening and later reassessment. Plans can die or change because land is lost, finance fails, prices change,
 a rival enters, household circumstances change or a better opportunity appears.
 7.2 Capital Allocation Competition
 One dollar cannot simultaneously fund maintenance, inventory, debt repayment, wages, reserves, equipment and
 expansion. NPC enterprises should face the same competing uses of scarce cash/capacity as the player and act according
  to policy, risk tolerance, time horizon, obligations and information.
 7.3 Customer Decision Processes Are Contextual
 Staple groceries, emergency equipment repair, hotel lodging, freight service and a long-term construction contract should
 not share one hidden attractiveness formula. Each purchase type can weight price, distance, urgency, reliability, wait,
  quality, trust, credit, suitability and prior experience differently while using the same general feasible-choice doctrine.
 7.4 Information Can Conflict
 Observed fact, rumor, advertisement, signed agreement, newspaper report, customer statement, manager estimate and
  official record can coexist and conflict. Actors can investigate. Communication technology changes access and latency; it
 does not make information automatically true or omniscient.
 7.5 Reputation Is Evidence-Specific
 Supplier-payment reputation, lender standing, employer reputation, customer-service reputation and project-completion
  reliability can differ. A single universal Reputation score should not overwrite these dimensions, although player-facing
 summaries may exist when they are traceable to evidence.
 PART VIII - GOVERNANCE, SUCCESSION & INTERNAL CONTROLS
 8.1 Governance Decision Lifecycle
 Corporate/partnership governance should support Proposal -> authority classification -> notice/information -> required
 approvals -> negotiation/amendment -> approval/refusal -> execution -> record. Economic ownership, voting rights, office,
 board authority, reserved decisions and creditor restrictions remain separate.
 8.2 Capital Calls & New Financing
 A company needing capital can propose contributions, borrowing, new equity or other financing. Investors can participate,
 refuse or negotiate according to their rights. New money is not automatically filled pro rata. Dilution, covenants, collateral
 and control consequences must be real where applicable.
 8.3 Succession & Continuity Case
 Death, incapacity, retirement, relocation or partner exit redistributes ownership and authority; it does not automatically
 delete a business. When a consequential Person disappears from an ownership/authority role, create a continuity problem
  that identifies surviving operating coverage, ownership claims, obligations, signing authority, heirs/partners, manager
 coverage and viable outcomes such as family continuation, hired management, buyout, sale, dormancy or liquidation.
 8.4 Internal Controls Are Operational Structure
 Cash custody, purchase authority, record entry, receiving and verification can belong to different Persons. Very small firms
 may legitimately combine them; larger firms can reduce error/theft/concealment risk through separation, approvals,
 physical counts and reconciliation. A discrepancy can remain ambiguous until evidence distinguishes mistake, shrinkage,
 short delivery, spoilage or theft.
 8.5 Acquisition Diligence Consumes Controls & Records
 A buyer evaluating a well-controlled business should have stronger evidence than one evaluating informal, unreconciled
 books. Internal controls do not guarantee honesty; they change what can be checked and how reliably discrepancies can
 be explained.
 PART IX - LAW, INSURANCE, DISTRESS & INSTITUTIONAL DEPTH
 9.1 Commercial Dispute Lifecycle





                                               LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 106/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXIII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                                12



 A legal right does not automatically produce an outcome. Commercial disputes should support claim/demand -> response
 -> negotiation/settlement -> formal proceeding where needed -> decision/judgment -> enforcement. Notice, proof,
 professional expertise, cost, delay and enforcement capacity matter. Exact court procedure, lien priority, redemption and
  filing law remain dated research.
 9.2 Insurance & Risk Transfer
 Insurance should begin with historically supported property/fire and cargo/commercial-asset coverage, then expand where
 research supports it. Policy terms identify insured interest, covered risk/property, term, premium, limit, retained
 loss/deductible concept where period-appropriate, conditions/exclusions and insurer. Insurance never prevents physical
  loss. Claims follow loss -> notice -> investigation/assessment -> coverage decision -> valuation -> payment/partial
 payment/denial -> dispute where applicable.
 9.3 Distress, Workout & Insolvency
 Distinguish illiquidity, insolvency and operational failure. Creditors have agency and may demand cure, extend, waive,
  restructure, require collateral, restrict activity or enforce based on expected recovery and legal rights. Recovery can use
 asset sales, owner capital, refinancing, new partners, inventory reduction, layoffs, lease/supplier workout, partial liquidation
 or going-concern sale. Commercial Ruin remains an endpoint of no viable recovery, not a single cash threshold.
 9.4 Civic Project Institutions
  Civic infrastructure follows need -> promoter/proposal -> authority/franchise -> financing -> engineering/source ->
 procurement/construction -> initial service -> maintenance/expansion. Residents, merchants, utilities, railroads, lenders or
  civic bodies can promote or oppose a project. Public procurement should reuse ordinary Agreement/Project systems rather
 than a civic minigame.
 9.5 Utility Service Economics
 Physical generation/source, network and connection remain authoritative. Add the commercial layer: request/offer for
 connection, connection cost, service agreement/tariff, billing, arrears, disconnection/reconnection, capacity/load
 commitments and network expansion economics. Large customers may justify line extension through real expected
 load/revenue rather than a Boolean UtilityAvailable flag.
 9.6 Labor-Market Lifecycle
 Vacancy -> information/search -> candidate awareness -> mutual evaluation -> offer -> negotiation/counteroffer ->
 acceptance/refusal -> start/probation -> retention/promotion -> resignation/dismissal/layoff. Poaching changes both
 employers because the same Person leaves one organization and joins another. Housing, commute, family obligations,
  safety, wages, meals/board, reputation and alternatives all remain relevant.
 PART X - PERFORMANCE, RESEARCH & REVISION XXIII LOCK
 SUMMARY
 10.1 Life Simulation Must Remain Scalable
 Continuous Personhood is a causality requirement, not permission to frame-poll every Person. Use event-driven
 schedules, activity blocks, household-level batching and coarse-resolution execution so long as identity, time, money,
  inventory, relationships and outcomes remain reconcilable.
 10.2 Equipment Research Is a Starting Data Set
 The occupation table establishes historically grounded categories and required physical methods. Exact equipment
 ownership prevalence, prices, model adoption, counts, wear, maintenance intervals and productivity effects remain
 regional/date calibration unless separately researched. The game should prefer plausible alternative methods over false
 universal minimum loadouts.
 10.3 Systems Already Strong
 Revision XXIII does not replace the existing strong household/housing ontology, asset condition/maintenance/failure
 system, core physical logistics, provenance, basic demography or banking/liquidity architecture. These are deepened
 through shared Person, Agreement, Transaction, Equipment and institutional rules rather than rebuilt.

 10.5 Revision XXIII Hard Locks
    • Continuous Personhood is authoritative; local customers and workers are not anonymous demand/labor tokens.
    • Local in-person transactions require a legitimate buyer principal and acting Person.
    • Household consumption and individual action remain separate but causally linked.
    • Person time/location are exclusive across work and non-work life.
    • Customer traffic and demand summaries are derived, not transaction generators.
    • Business capability derives from people, equipment/tools, space, materials, authority, information and time.
    • Equipment requirements attach to tasks/capabilities and can use alternative historically plausible methods.
    • Agreement/Obligation, Economic Event, Activity/Time, Information/Evidence and Resource Reservation are preferred
     shared grammars.
    • Projects preserve baseline, current forecast and actual outcome separately.
    • Governance, succession, internal controls, insurance, disputes, distress, civic projects, utilities and labor markets
     require real institutional processes.
    • Coarse simulation preserves the same entities and economic truth.

 The preserved Canonical Project Bible Revision XXII follows unchanged and remains authoritative except where Revision
  XXIII explicitly adds, deepens, clarifies or supersedes a rule.
