LAND & LEDGERS
 CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE - REVISION XXII
 The Contractor Full-Systems Playtest Integration: Scenario Accomplishment Doctrine, Contract Access, Settlement
  Integrity, Delegated Capital & Opportunity Provenance
  Revision date: September 18, 2026
 Source baseline: Canonical Project Bible Revision XXI - September 15, 2026
  Status: Active Canon integration
 PRESERVATION GUARANTEE
 Revision XXII preserves Revision XXI in full except where this integration explicitly adds, deepens, clarifies or supersedes prior wording.
 The complete Revision XXI document follows this integration unchanged as the preserved baseline. Where a conflict exists, Revision XXII
  controls. Exact Contractor playtest prices, wages, rents, populations, project costs, contract values, interest rates, margins, work durations,
 crew sizes, timber quantities, equipment counts and other generated values remain calibration unless this integration explicitly identifies a
 design or scenario lock.
 PURPOSE
 Revision XXII integrates THE CONTRACTOR full-systems playtest and the subsequent four-pass Master Playtest Integration. The
 campaign moved from broke handyman work through hired labor, multi-crew construction, railway contracting, delegated operations and the
 causal creation of Cinder Creek. The principal result is not a fixed contractor progression or a new table of historical prices. It is a tighter set
  of rules connecting scenario accomplishments, opportunity provenance, organizational qualification, external infrastructure progress,
  physical settlement state, delegated capital policy and persistent obligations.
 The review also validates substantial existing Canon from Revisions XIX-XXI: Construction & Contracting, Full Autonomy, Manager Activity,
 NPC parity, exact-known-information doctrine, physical logistics, maintenance/failure causality, migration, housing, sawmilling, Lifetime
 Ledger authority, separate owner/business cash and scenario failure without world deletion. Those systems remain authoritative and are not
  duplicated here.
 REVISION XXII MASTER DOCTRINE
  •   Scenario objectives normally measure accomplishments, not designer-preferred routes. A difficult but legitimate strategy remains
     valid unless the restriction itself is an authored objective or premise.
  •   Opportunities require causal world provenance. A scenario may author circumstances and schedules, but it should not spawn a
     qualifying contract merely because the player needs one for a checklist.
  •   External infrastructure projects progress through persistent world state. Railways, roads and other projects may advance, delay or
    change independently of player objective completion.
  •   Contract access may depend on evidence. Prior work, references, relationships, specialist staff, equipment, capital, geography and
     current commitments can affect whether a counterparty considers the player capable.
  •   Settlement population remains physical. Reported residents must correspond to actual Persons and legitimate
    accommodation/residence relationships.
  •   Building completion, business opening and business profitability are separate facts. Scenario predicates must ask the authority
     that actually owns the required truth.
  •   Delegated policy can include recurring capital mandates. A manager may be told to reinvest, expand or protect liquidity while still
    executing real projects, transactions and financing decisions.
  •   Financing authority is delegable when explicitly granted. Major borrowing is commonly owner-reserved, but it is not universally
    owner-only.
  •   Settlement durability is multidimensional. Do not collapse housing, employment, services, transport, imports and boom exposure into
    one authoritative Self-Sufficiency score.
  •   Migration incentives alter ordinary economics and information. Free rent, relocation aid or discounted lots can improve feasibility
    and attractiveness; they do not directly create population.
  •   Destroyed collateral does not automatically erase surviving debt. Asset loss, insurance, security value, lender response and the
    underlying obligation remain separate facts.
 PART I - SCENARIO ACCOMPLISHMENTS, OPPORTUNITY & EXTERNAL PROJECTS
 1.1 Objectives Measure Accomplishments
 Primary objectives should describe the economic or world accomplishments required for completion. They should not prohibit a strategy
 merely because it is faster, more leveraged, more vertically integrated, more decentralized or otherwise different from the route the designer
 expected, provided the ordinary systems, costs, authority, labor, time, law, provenance and consequences actually execute.


                                                       LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 109/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                                       2


 CANON LOCK - Gamey player optimization remains valid when the simulation is not cheating. Scenario restrictions are legitimate
 when the restriction itself is part of the authored challenge, historical premise or qualifying accomplishment.
 1.2 Opportunity Provenance
 A material contract, acquisition, supplier proposal, property opportunity or customer project should exist for a world reason. Useful
 provenance can include an actual counterparty need, project stage, shortage, seller motive, route change, maintenance burden, customer
  request, public program, financing condition or other causal source. Scenario authors may shape initial circumstances and broad timing, but
 should not create otherwise unsupported qualifying transactions solely because an objective requires them.
 1.3 Contract Access Through Demonstrated Capability
 Larger or more specialized work can require credible evidence that a contractor can perform it. Relevant evidence may include completed
 work, references, known personnel, specialist employees, equipment, working capital, insurance/security or bonding where historically
  appropriate, current workload, geography, commercial standing and relationships with engineers, customers or other counterparties. There
  is no abstract Contractor Level that replaces those facts.
 1.4 Increasingly Demanding Opportunities Are Not Unlock Tiers
 A scenario may deliberately arrange a plausible sequence of increasingly demanding opportunities. THE CONTRACTOR reference arc
 used ordinary building work, railway structures, grading, bridges and multi-site execution. Completing an earlier objective does not magically
 unlock the next contract. The next opportunity must still exist through world schedule, geography, counterparty need, information and
  qualification.
 1.5 External Infrastructure Has Its Own Timeline
 A scenario-authored railway, road, canal, utility or similar external project can maintain its own route, work fronts, construction stages,
 delays and service openings. The player may follow, ignore, service, invest around or relocate relative to that project. Objective completion
 must not teleport the infrastructure front to the player or freeze it until a checklist condition is met.
 1.6 Active Work Is Distinct From Agreement Existence
 Where an objective requires overlapping work, simultaneous crews or maintained execution, qualification depends on actual active work
 across the authored period. Merely having two signed contracts, two named crews or two planned projects is insufficient unless the
 authored predicate explicitly says otherwise.
 PART II - SETTLEMENT, POPULATION & PROPERTY-STATE INTEGRITY
 2.1 Resident Population Must Reconcile to Persons
 A settlement resident count is a read model over actual persistent Persons and legitimate residence/accommodation relationships. The
  simulation must not maintain an independent population number that can exceed or contradict the people physically represented by the
 economy.
 A practical audit question is: Where does this Person sleep tonight? A valid answer may be a house, rented room, boarding house, hotel,
 bunkhouse, employer lodging, temporary camp or another historically and physically legitimate accommodation. Homeless/displaced
 Persons may exist, but they should be represented explicitly rather than silently counted as housed residents.
 2.2 Permanent, Transient and Daytime Presence Remain Distinct
 Permanent residents, transient overnight residents, temporary camp populations and daytime workers/visitors are different economic facts.
 Employment in a settlement does not automatically make the worker a resident. Settlement reports should preserve the distinction when it
  materially affects housing, consumption, labor supply or durability.
 2.3 Building State and Business State Are Separate
 Preserve the existing Parcel -> Building/Improvement -> Functional Space -> occupancy/business-use separation and deepen it with
  explicit state semantics. A construction project may be complete, the resulting building may be physically usable, a business may later
 occupy it, the business may open, and it may later become profitable or fail. These events can occur at different times.
 CANON LOCK - A permanent-building objective should qualify from authoritative physical/project state, not from whether an
 occupying business has opened, unless the objective explicitly requires operation.
 2.4 Settlement Durability Is Multidimensional
 A settlement can be strong in some dimensions and fragile in others. Cinder Creek demonstrated that a place may have stable housing and
  repair capacity while remaining dependent on imported food, imported finish lumber, railway access or transient construction demand. Do
  not create one authoritative Self-Sufficiency meter that hides those dependencies.
  Useful explanation dimensions include employment concentration, permanent versus transient demand, housing fit, essential services,
  transport access, import dependence, local production diversity, vacancy, infrastructure continuity and exposure to temporary booms.
 These are read models over real state, not substitute economic truth.

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                                       3


 PART III - DELEGATED CAPITAL POLICY & FINANCING AUTHORITY
 3.1 Standing Capital Mandates
 Delegation can include recurring strategic policy such as reinvesting distributable rental earnings into qualifying housing, protecting a
  liquidity band, replacing failed equipment, expanding within a defined geography or staging projects when evidence supports them. A
  standing mandate changes who is authorized to decide; it does not spawn buildings, loans, workers, inventory or cash.
 The responsible manager must still identify real opportunities, evaluate information, arrange land, labor, materials and financing, create
  actual projects/agreements, and accept the consequences of their judgment.
 3.2 Financial Authority Need Not Use a Universal Dollar Cap
 Delegated financial authority may use dollar limits, transaction classes, risk constraints, approved collateral, geography, business scope,
  strategic mandate, escalation rules or broad discretionary authority. A fixed numerical ceiling is optional rather than mandatory.
 3.3 Major Borrowing Can Be Explicitly Delegated
  Full Autonomy does not automatically grant authority over every mortgage, major loan, ownership change or sale. Those acts remain
  subject to the owner/governance authority actually granted. However, the player may explicitly authorize a trusted manager or executive to
 arrange borrowing, refinancing, mortgages, seller finance or other capital transactions within defined scope. Lenders, collateral, legal
 powers, liquidity and governance still apply normally.
 3.4 Management Remains Decision-Making Labor
 The Contractor validates that recurring reinvestment and financing work should appear through actual manager decisions, Manager Activity,
  negotiations, Projects and Transactions. Do not replace this with a passive Property Growth or Management Efficiency modifier.
 PART IV - MIGRATION INCENTIVES & SETTLEMENT PROMOTION
 4.1 Incentives Enter the Ordinary Migration Chain
 Free or discounted introductory rent, relocation assistance, employer-paid travel, discounted lots, cheap commercial leases and similar
  incentives can affect destination awareness, expected housing cost, relocation feasibility, household budget and perceived opportunity.
 They do not directly increment population.
 Households still evaluate available work, household needs, housing fit, travel, family constraints, information quality, alternatives and
 expected durability, then physically move and either remain or leave according to subsequent conditions.
 4.2 Growth Is Not Durable Merely Because a Threshold Was Touched
 Settlement-development scenarios may require a population threshold to be sustained, paired with economic viability or maintained after
  extraordinary subsidies expire. The exact threshold and duration remain scenario calibration. The design purpose is to distinguish durable
  settlement from a one-day or heavily subsidized temporary boom.
 PART V - PHYSICAL LOSS, COLLATERAL & SURVIVING OBLIGATIONS
 5.1 Asset Destruction and Debt Resolution Are Different Events
  Fire, accident, theft, disaster or deterioration can destroy or materially reduce the value of collateral without extinguishing the debt it
 secured. The obligation continues according to the Agreement, insurance, lender response, collateral/security rights, repayment,
  settlement, discharge and dated law.
 CANON LOCK - Destroyed collateral is not debt forgiveness. Loss of security may increase lender exposure, trigger contractual
 remedies, reduce refinancing options or produce a deficiency after collateral proceeds, but the liability changes only through an authoritative
  financial/legal event.
 5.2 Crisis Recovery Uses Shared Systems
 A crisis scenario should create severe circumstances rather than a parallel recovery minigame. Rebuilding, asset sale, hauling, contracting,
  refinancing, workouts, leasing, partnership capital, occupation change and other responses should use the same systems available
 elsewhere. Investigating sabotage or arson, when present, is a separate legal/information thread and does not erase the balance sheet by
  fiat.
 PART VI - CANONICAL SCENARIO ADDITIONS
 6.1 THE CONTRACTOR
 THE CONTRACTOR is a canonical Construction & Infrastructure / Settlement Development scenario concept built around the arc broke
 handyman -> contractor -> employer -> railway contractor -> multi-crew organization -> town builder. An external railway project
  already exists and advances physically through the region. The player succeeds by building organizational capability alongside the
 changing opportunity rather than by unlocking contractor tiers.
 The tested reference objective structure is preserved below. The dates are scenario-authored requirements for this scenario structure and
 do not replace the ordinary Open Frontier start-year doctrine:
1   By June 30, 1875 - complete one paid contract with all construction labor personally performed by the player.
2   By December 31, 1875 - complete eight paid contracts.



                                                       LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 111/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                                       4


3   By December 31, 1876 - complete five paid contracts using hired labor.
4   By December 31, 1877 - complete two paid permanent new-building contracts.
5   By December 31, 1878 - complete one paid contract with zero manual construction labor by the player.
6   By December 31, 1879 - have active work on two paid contracts overlap for at least seven consecutive days.
7   By December 31, 1880 - complete one paid contract at least twenty road miles from the starting settlement.
8   By December 31, 1881 - complete one railroad-issued construction contract.
9   By December 31, 1882 - maintain two separate construction crews at two active worksites for at least thirty consecutive days.
10  By December 31, 1883 - complete five railroad-issued contracts in total.
11  By December 31, 1883 - complete five cumulative route miles of railroad grading/earthwork.
12  By June 30, 1884 - complete one permanent railroad bridge.
13  By September 30, 1884 - complete twelve permanent buildings in one developing railroad town/railhead.
14  By December 31, 1884 - complete twenty-five permanent new-building contracts in total.
15  By December 31, 1884 - maintain four separate construction crews at four active worksites for at least thirty consecutive days.
 For the maintained crew objectives, a qualifying crew in the tested structure contains at least three employees at one worksite with a
 designated working lead/foreman capable of routine progress without player manual labor. That definition is scenario-specific and does not
  create a universal minimum construction-crew rule.
 6.2 ASHES & NOTES
 ASHES & NOTES is a Crisis & Recovery / Agriculture & Property scenario concept. The player begins with an operating farm and
 meaningful seller debt or other secured obligation. A major physical fire destroys much of the productive/residential base while leaving
 some surviving assets and the financial obligation intact. Recovery remains open-ended through ordinary systems: rebuild, sell, haul,
  contract, refinance, negotiate, lease, restructure, seek partners or change commercial direction. Exact opening debt, surviving assets, fire
 cause and deadline remain authored scenario calibration.
 6.3 A TOWN FROM NOTHING / THE PROMOTER
 A TOWN FROM NOTHING / THE PROMOTER is a Settlement Development scenario concept. The player begins with land and limited
  capital but no durable town under their control. The objective is to create enough economic gravity that households and independent
 businesses choose to arrive, remain, invest and expand. Possible tools include industrial anchors, freight access, housing, free/discounted
  introductory rent, relocation assistance, cheap lots/leases and commercial promotion. The player may vertically own much of the settlement
  or act mainly as promoter/landowner; neither route is mandatory.
 A useful completion pattern is a permanent-population threshold plus a sustained retention or viability requirement after extraordinary
  recruitment support ends. Exact population, duration and subsidy rules remain scenario calibration.
 PART VII - CONTRACTOR PLAYTEST VALIDATION & CALIBRATION
 7.1 Existing Canon Strongly Validated
  •   Construction & Contracting scales through real workload, people, supervision, equipment, transport, cash and backlog rather than
     abstract crew slots.
  •    Full Autonomy and Manager Activity can support mature operations with zero routinely owner-managed businesses.
  •  Owner cash, business cash, consolidated reporting, profit, cash flow, book equity and market value remain distinct.
  •   Employee capability is evidence-limited; role or promotion does not manufacture competence.
  •   Task assignment does not guarantee execution; people, animals, vehicles and equipment remain exclusive physical resources.
  •   Maintenance, defects and downtime produce causal work, lost capacity and repair decisions rather than generic debuffs.
  •   Sawmill/logging/lumber and internal-supply chains remain physical and cost-bearing.
  •   Housing pressure is household-type-specific; transient labor and durable population remain different.
  •  NPC entry and competition use the same economic systems and can succeed, fail or misjudge opportunities.
  •   Lifetime Ledger evidence is necessary for long scenarios; narrative reconstruction is not authoritative.
 7.2 Contractor Calibration Holds
 The following Contractor playtest values remain calibration/research rather than universal historical constants:
  •   exact wages, room rents, business margins, debt terms and supplier credit;
  •   construction contract prices, bridge costs, grading prices and project contribution margins;
  •   crew sizes, horse/team counts, equipment ratios and exact output rates;

  •   exact migration-incentive response and post-subsidy retention thresholds.
 PART VIII - REVISION XXII LOCK SUMMARY & DEEPENING MAP
 8.1 Revision XXII Locks
  •   Scenario objectives normally measure accomplishments rather than prescribe one expected strategy.
  •   Material opportunities require causal world provenance.
  •   External infrastructure projects progress through persistent world state independent of objective checkmarks.
  •   Contract access can depend on demonstrated capability, capacity, relationships and prior performance.
  •   Settlement resident counts reconcile to actual Persons and legitimate accommodation.
  •   Physical building completion and business opening/performance remain separate state.
  •   Recurring manager reinvestment/capital mandates are valid delegated policy.
  •   Major financing authority may be explicitly delegated within real scope and constraints.
  •   Settlement durability is multidimensional rather than one Self-Sufficiency score.
  •   Recruitment incentives affect ordinary migration economics rather than directly creating population.
  •   Collateral destruction does not automatically extinguish the secured obligation.
  •  THE CONTRACTOR, ASHES & NOTES and A TOWN FROM NOTHING / THE PROMOTER are preserved scenario concepts.
 8.2 Deepening Map
  •   Revision XXI Part I / objective semantics is deepened by accomplishment-versus-route doctrine and active-work qualification.
  •   Revision XIX Construction & Contracting and Railway Project doctrine is deepened by contract qualification, opportunity provenance and

  •   Revision XXI Part V and earlier Housing/Settlement doctrine is deepened by hard population/accommodation reconciliation and explicit
     physical-building versus operating-business state.
  •   Revision XXI Part IV and Revision XIX Manager Activity/Autonomy are deepened by recurring capital mandates and explicitly delegated
     financing scope.
  •   Existing migration and settlement-development doctrine is deepened by explicit treatment of recruitment incentives and multidimensional
     durability.
  •   Existing finance, collateral, fire and crisis doctrine is clarified so physical collateral loss cannot be interpreted as automatic debt deletion.

 CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE - REVISION XXI
 Saloon Circuit Full-Systems Playtest Integration: Objective Semantics, Person/Delegation, Provenance, Finance,
 Property & Saloon Operations

 Source baseline: Canonical Project Bible Revision XX - September 8, 2026
 Status: Active Canon integration
 PRESERVATION GUARANTEE
 Revision XXI preserves Revision XX in full except where this integration explicitly adds, deepens, clarifies or supersedes prior
 wording. The complete Revision XX document follows this integration unchanged as the preserved baseline. Where a conflict exists,
 Revision XXI controls. Exact Saloon Circuit playtest prices, wages, traffic counts, project costs, interest rates, holding periods, town
 populations, construction durations and other generated values remain calibration unless this integration explicitly identifies a design
 or scenario lock.
 PURPOSE
 Revision XXI integrates the complete SALOON CIRCUIT - THREE TOWNS systems playtest and the subsequent Master Playtest
 Integration. The campaign stress-tested scenario objectives, physical player time, labor autonomy, capability evidence, delegation,
 mixed-use property, food service, gambling, marketing, vertical integration, physical logistics, historical finance, employee succession
 and final liquidation. The principal result is not a new set of universal prices or a fixed saloon progression. It is a stronger causal
 connection among existing authorities: Persons perform real work, goods preserve provenance, agreements allocate rights, finance
 preserves obligations and scenario objectives consume authoritative state rather than narrative intent.
 REVISION XXI MASTER DOCTRINE
  Scenario objectives should be explicit economic/world predicates. Event, current-state and maintained-state objectives have
     different completion semantics.
  A legitimately completed historical event milestone remains completed unless the authored objective explicitly requires continuing
    ownership or maintenance.
  Unusual or deliberately gamey player strategies are valid when the real systems, costs, labor, time, provenance and
    consequences actually execute.
  The player and NPCs should use the same ordinary causal economic actions. Difference comes from information, resources, skill,
     authority, goals and judgment rather than exclusive mechanics.
  Employees are autonomous Persons. Assignment creates work and authority; it does not guarantee compliance, competence or
     completion.
  Delegation transfers real work and decision authority. Full Autonomy is a convenience configuration over real tasks, limits, records
    and escalation rather than magic automation.
   Vertical integration is proven by physical/economic execution - production, inventory, transport, receipt, transformation/use and
    customer sale - not by ownership labels alone.
  Debt, seller finance, guaranties, collateral and contingent exposure remain distinct. A debt-free objective must define what it
     counts.
  Marketing changes information and customer choice through causal channels; it does not create guaranteed demand.
  Known transaction facts remain exact. Forecast uncertainty, hidden capability and competitor knowledge remain information-
      limited.
 PART I - SCENARIO OBJECTIVE SEMANTICS & COMPLETION
 1.1 Event, Current-State & Maintained Predicates
 Scenario authors should define objectives from explicit authoritative facts. Three common predicate families are:
  Event predicate - a qualifying event occurred, such as a customer sale, acquisition, disposition or completed project.
   Current-state predicate - a condition is true now, such as 100 percent ownership, zero qualifying principal debt or current market
     rank.
   Maintained-state predicate - a condition remained true for an authored duration, such as profitable autonomous operation for a
     specified period.
 CANON LOCK - Do not treat these predicate families as interchangeable. Historical events persist; current-state conditions re-
 evaluate; maintained-state objectives require the authored duration/evidence.
 1.2 Historical Milestones Persist
  If the player legitimately completes a historical milestone using real underlying systems, later sale, destruction or loss of the enabling
 asset does not retroactively erase the event unless continued ownership is an explicit part of the objective. This allows build ->
 integrate -> prove -> sell strategies without rewriting history.
 1.3 Headline Objectives & Attached Criteria
 A scenario may present a readable headline objective while evaluating several attached predicates. Every mandatory criterion must
 be discoverable from the beginning through objective details, information affordances or equivalent UI. The player should not
 encounter surprise victory requirements at the deadline.





                                                        LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 114/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXI / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                       2
 1.4 Countdown Presentation
 Objective UI may show current date, deadline, status, remaining time and early-completion margin. Presentation granularity may
 become more precise as the deadline approaches, for example months -> days -> hours. Exact thresholds remain UX calibration; the
 authored deadline remains authoritative.
 1.5 Creative Completion
 A player may deliberately satisfy an objective through a minimal, odd or inefficient sequence if every underlying action is real. The
 Saloon Circuit one-chicken test is the reference example: one owned chicken can be processed, physically moved, prepared and sold
 to one customer to satisfy a distinct-product event if the authored predicate says one qualifying sale. The simulation should not add
 an unstated minimum batch merely because the designer expected a larger operation.
 CANON LOCK - Gamey player optimization is allowed. Gamey simulation shortcuts are not.
 1.6 Scenario Failure Remains Separate From Commercial Ruin
 Missing an authored objective or deadline can fail the scenario without destroying the persistent world, enterprise or save. Scenario
  failure and Commercial Ruin remain separate concepts.
 PART II - PHYSICAL PLAYER, TIME & SYSTEMIC PARITY
 2.1 Player Is a Physical Person
 The general Land & Ledgers player remains one physical commercial Person. The player may personally perform ordinary work
 where capability, tools, location and law permit. A 15-minute task consumes approximately 15 minutes of authoritative simulation
 time; travel also consumes time. Do not create a generic Owner Hours resource pool.
 Scenario-specific role restrictions may still prohibit or discourage personal labor when deliberately authored. Such restrictions do not
 become a universal rule merely because an earlier scenario used them.
 2.2 Opportunity Cost Creates the Delegation Curve
 The natural progression from hands-on work to hiring, supervision and capital allocation should emerge because owner time becomes
 scarce and economically valuable. Delegation is useful because another Person actually performs or decides the work, not because
 an owner-action-point penalty disappears.
 2.3 Systemic Player/NPC Parity
 Ordinary systemic actions available to NPC owners, managers, competitors and workers should generally be available to the player
 through the same underlying authorities. This includes hiring, bargaining, property transactions, supplier competition, credit, market
 research and - where the legal/crime systems eventually support them - deception, interference or sabotage. The consequences must
 also be shared.
 CANON LOCK - Difficulty may tune decision quality, information search, reaction speed or risk tolerance. It should not give NPCs
 hidden economic physics unavailable to the player.
 2.4 Incarceration Does Not Pause the Economy
  If the player is arrested or incarcerated, time continues. Businesses with adequate delegation may continue operating; poorly
 delegated businesses may miss decisions, consume inventory, fail obligations or deteriorate. Incarceration is not a pause screen.
 PART III - LABOR AUTONOMY, CAPABILITY & EMPLOYMENT RELATIONSHIPS
 3.1 Employees Are Autonomous Persons
 An assignment is not a guarantee. Employees may complete, delay, make mistakes, neglect, partially perform, refuse, abandon,
 complain, escalate or quit according to real circumstances. Relevant causes can include capability, workload, fatigue, task fit, safety,
  legality, pay, reliability, fairness, treatment, relationships and available alternatives.
 3.2 No Universal Refusal Threshold
 Extreme scheduling should create rising fatigue and human response rather than one global cutoff. One Person may tolerate a long
 day that another refuses. Prior treatment, current need, relationship, danger and alternatives can matter.
 3.3 Jobs Are Assignments, Not Rigid Classes
 A worker may be assigned several compatible duties and may also be assigned work outside their strongest capability when
 physically and legally possible. The result should emerge from actual capability, conditions, tools and supervision rather than a Wrong
 Class prohibition.
 3.4 Employment Rapport
 Employment and supervisory relationships retain causal history. Fair treatment, pay, scheduling and prior interactions may influence
 cooperation, disclosure, retention and tolerance for unusual requests. Rapport is not a universal Productivity multiplier.
 3.5 Capability & Confidence Presentation
 Player-facing capability bands are locked as: Abysmal / Bad / Poor / Average / Great / Excellent / Mastered.
 Confidence is Low / Moderate / High. High confidence should normally display one band, Moderate two adjacent bands and Low
 three adjacent bands. When evidence is insufficient, display Not enough information rather than false precision.
 3.6 Skill Changes Outcome Distribution
  Skill should shift the probability distribution of plausible task outcomes. Task difficulty, tools, information, fatigue, environment and
 other relevant conditions still matter. Avoid a universal +X percent Skill bonus.





                                                        LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 115/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXI / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                       3
 3.7 Evidence Creates Knowledge
 Actual capability remains hidden. Interviews, references, reputation, observed work, practical demonstrations, records and outcomes
 create evidence from which the player forms an estimate. A practical demonstration is an ordinary task/observation sequence, not a
 separate magical interview minigame.
 3.8 Family Work Is Explicit
 Household membership does not silently create free business labor. Spouses, children and relatives may work under explicit
 employment/family-work relationships where historically and economically appropriate; their time and competing household
 obligations remain real.
 3.9 Advances Do Not Create Labor Ownership
 An employee loan, wage advance, lodging benefit or other financial relationship does not automatically create forced labor authority.
 Debt and employment remain distinct relationships.
 PART IV - DELEGATION, FULL AUTONOMY & OWNER DEPENDENCY
 4.1 Granular Delegation
 Ordinary decisions and tasks may be delegated to qualified people unless ownership, law, specialist authority or the player's explicit
 reservation prevents it. Delegation can cover individual tasks, categories or standing policy such as inventory counts, reorder limits,
 receiving, cash reconciliation, scheduling, routine hiring recommendations, minor maintenance, freight coordination, routine bills,
 inspections and price changes inside limits.
 4.2 Management Is Still Labor
 A delegated inventory check still consumes the manager's time and information. Travel, conversation, paperwork, calculation and
 inspection remain real. Small actions may take minutes; accumulated workload can delay decisions.
 4.3 Full Autonomy Is a Preset
 Full Autonomy is a convenience preset that assigns broad routine authority and standing policy. It does not create a separate abstract
 manager simulation. Material debt, sale, mortgage, ownership changes or other owner-reserved acts still escalate as appropriate.
 4.4 Zero Personally Managed Businesses
 A mature portfolio can validly reach zero routinely owner-managed businesses. Crown House operating for an extended period under
 Tom Harrow without routine owner decisions is the reference playtest validation. The exact duration is calibration; the principle is
 continuity through real people and policies.
 PART V - BUSINESS CAPABILITY, PROPERTY & PHYSICAL SPACE
 5.1 Business Form Follows Actual Function
 A business's capabilities should emerge from its spaces, equipment, labor, expertise, legal authority, inventory/supply, agreements
 and market access rather than rigid labels alone. A saloon can therefore also support food service, lodging or gambling when the
 actual conditions exist.
 5.2 Parcel, Building, Functional Space & Business Use Remain Separate
 One enterprise may span multiple structures, and one building may contain several functional/economic uses. Preserve the existing
 Parcel -> Building/Improvement -> Functional Space -> occupancy/business-use separation.
 5.3 Building Condition Bands
 Use the visible condition bands Critical / Poor / Fair / Good / Excellent. Recommended shared domains are Structural, Exterior,
  Interior and Functional. More detailed hidden component state may exist where materially useful.
 5.4 Access Remodeling & Concealment
 Real improvements may create or remove exterior stairs, partitions, sealed access, controlled routes, concealed doors or concealed
 spaces when geometry and construction permit. Concealment affects discoverability and security; it does not create magical
  invisibility.
 5.5 Cosmetic Improvements Are Causal
 Painting or visible repair can change presentation, customer expectations and reputation through observation. Do not encode a direct
 CustomerDemand +X percent upgrade independent of awareness and experience.
 PART VI - MARKETING, MARKET RESEARCH & COMPETITION
 6.1 Marketing Is an Information Chain
 The core causal chain is: channel -> message -> audience -> exposure -> awareness -> consideration -> choice -> transaction.
 Newspapers, handbills, signage, workplace solicitation, relationships, promotions and word of mouth can create awareness without
 guaranteeing purchase.
 6.2 Customer Awareness Has Sources
 Where useful, customer awareness may derive from prior visits, signage, print, coworkers, employer/foreman relationships, personal
 recommendation or other real information paths. The player's attribution remains imperfect.
 6.3 Competition Is Segment & Daypart Specific
 A business can be weak at midday and strong at night, or appeal to workers but not travelers. Competitive analysis should support
 segment/daypart observation rather than reducing the market to one total customer number.




                                                        LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 116/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XXI / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                       4
 6.4 Market Research Is a Real Action
 The player may ask customers and staff what they observe, request or hear. Answers are Person-based evidence, not omniscient
 market statistics. Employees may also suggest candidates, suppliers, products, promotions or repairs when they possess a plausible
 information basis, and those suggestions may be wrong.
 6.5 Attractiveness & Persuasion Are Contextual
 Physical attractiveness or presentation may influence persuasion where a particular customer is receptive and the social context
 makes it relevant. It is not a universal sex-based sales bonus. The Saloon Circuit +15 concept remains calibration only.
 PART VII - VERTICAL INTEGRATION, INVENTORY & FREIGHT
 7.1 Integration Requires Execution
 Vertical integration should be evidenced by actual production, owned inventory, physical transfer, destination receipt,
 transformation/use and a qualifying customer transaction. Ownership of compatible enterprises alone does not prove integration.
 7.2 Provenance Matters
 When a scenario or analysis depends on origin, the underlying goods/inputs must preserve enough provenance to determine where
 they came from and how they reached the finished customer-facing product. Distinct-product objectives should count qualifying
 product definitions, not repeated lots of the same item.
 7.3 Internal Sourcing Is Optional
 Owning a supplier and customer enterprise does not force internal sourcing. Outside supply may still be cheaper, better, faster or
 more reliable. Internal transfers preserve real production, transport, spoilage, labor and other cost without manufacturing portfolio
 revenue.
 7.4 Freight Remains Physical
 Important freight preserves cargo, origin, destination, vehicle/team, driver, loading, route, time, feed, delay, unloading and cost. Useful
 operating analysis can distinguish loaded and empty mileage, labor, feed, maintenance, delay, rejected work and utilization.
 PART VIII - FINANCE, CREDIT, BUYOUTS & CONTINGENT EXPOSURE
 8.1 Historical Credit Is Information-Limited
 Avoid a universal modern consumer-credit formula for nineteenth-century business lending. Creditworthiness can depend on
 character/reputation, repayment history, cash flow, obligations, collateral/security, liquidity, purpose, maturity, lender exposure, lender
  capital/liquidity, relationships and local conditions.
 8.2 Financial Institution Type Matters
 Where legal powers differ, the institution's legal/charter type must matter. Do not assume every bank in every jurisdiction/year can
 make the same loans or hold the same security. Exact banking powers remain a dated research/data question.
 8.3 Lenders Are Not Omniscient
 A lender learns private obligations through legitimate information sources, diligence and representations. The player or NPC may
 potentially omit or misrepresent information where the interaction permits; discovery can create refusal, acceleration/default disputes,
  civil/fraud exposure, reputation damage or other consequences according to law and contract.
 8.4 Employee/Manager Buyout Financing
 A buyer may finance an acquisition through a third-party lender. The seller may receive cash at closing while separately providing a
 guaranty/surety or collateral support where historically and legally appropriate. Buyer debt, seller note, retained equity, guaranty and
 pledged collateral remain distinct structures.
 8.5 Guaranties Are Contingent Exposure
 A guaranty can remain after the seller owns zero percent of the business. It is real exposure that can affect future credit and become
 payable when triggered, but it is distinct from current principal debt until the agreement and events make it an actual liability.
 8.6 Seller Objectives Affect Deal Choice
 A seller seeking liquidity, certainty and speed may rationally accept a lower all-cash bid over a higher nominal seller-financed offer.
 Employee buyers are not entitled to artificial preference over better outside offers.
 8.7 Working Cash Remains Where Obligations Exist
 Aggressive owner debt repayment does not justify stripping operating businesses below required payroll, supplies or known
 obligations. There is no universal $150 or other fixed owner/business reserve; protected liquidity depends on real commitments and
 strategy.
 PART IX - SALOON, GAMBLING & INDEPENDENT PREMISES RELATIONSHIPS
 9.1 Saloon Capabilities Reuse Shared Systems
 Food service, lodging, poker, faro and other historically supported activities should emerge from shared Person, Premises/Space,
 Task, Inventory/Asset, Agreement, Transaction, LegalRegime and Information systems rather than isolated minigames.
 9.2 Free Poker
 A saloon may offer ordinary poker without rake or table fee. Such a game creates no direct gaming revenue; any commercial value
 arises through real customer attraction, dwell and food/drink purchases.





                                                        LAND & LEDGERS

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 117/346 ====================

 9.3 Faro Banking & Concessions
 Faro is a banking game and requires real bankroll exposure. A saloon may contract with an independent dealer/banker who supplies
 bankroll and keeps game wins/losses while the premises owner supplies space/services and receives concession rent and ordinary
 food/drink revenue. Exclusivity, licensing responsibility and duration are real agreement terms.
 9.4 Occupancy Does Not Automatically Create Employment
 An independent worker using rented business-controlled space is not automatically an employee. Premises/occupancy, employment
 and business ownership remain separate relationships. This is especially important for historically supported vice-related room
 arrangements.
 PART X - RECORDS, MONEY & INFORMATION PRESENTATION
 10.1 Known Facts Stay Exact
 When the player legitimately knows a transaction amount, cash balance or recorded payment, present the exact known fact.
 Uncertainty belongs to estimates, forecasts, hidden capability and unknown competitor information rather than recorded facts.
 10.2 Exact Cents Remain Authoritative
 Compact UI may suppress cents or use abbreviated displays, but affordability and all economic authority use exact underlying values.
 Display rounding can never make an unaffordable purchase affordable.
 10.3 Competitor Recon Uses Observable Information
 The player may observe customer counts, prices, signage, hours, public records, reputation and other legitimate evidence. Hidden
 competitor ledgers remain hidden unless a real information path reveals them.
 PART XI - LAW, ENFORCEMENT & ECONOMIC CONSEQUENCES
 11.1 Legal Rule and Enforcement Remain Separate
 An activity can be illegal yet weakly enforced or locally tolerated, or lawful/licensed yet heavily scrutinized. Preserve the chain legal
 rule -> enforcement posture/capability -> detection -> proceeding -> consequence rather than Illegal = instant arrest.
 11.2 Crime Can Propagate Into Economic State
 Where crime, sabotage or property damage systems exist, their real consequences can affect rival capacity, inventory, opening
 status, reputation, finances and customer choice. Scenario evaluators should consume the resulting authoritative economic state
 rather than special-case whether the designer intended the route. Crime still carries evidence, investigation, legal, reputation,
 restitution/insurance and retaliation consequences where applicable.
 PART XII - SALOON CIRCUIT SCENARIO LOCK
 12.1 Scenario Identity
 SALOON CIRCUIT - THREE TOWNS is a canonical scenario concept built around progression through increasingly complex saloon
 markets. This revision locks the tested completion structure but not every generated economic number, settlement population or exact
  historical start year.
 12.2 Final Completion Structure
   Historical milestone: 100 percent Ash Creek saloon ownership plus qualifying customer sale by the authored deadline.
   Historical milestone: 100 percent Prairie Crossing saloon ownership plus qualifying customer sale by the authored deadline.
   Historical milestone: qualifying sale using product/input supplied by another owned enterprise.
   Historical milestone: 100 percent Crown House ownership plus first qualifying customer sale.
   Historical milestone: three distinct internally supplied Crown customer products sold.
   Historical milestone: five distinct internally supplied Crown customer products sold.
   Final-state predicate: Crown House reaches authored #1 standardized Granite Junction saloon traffic rank.
   Final-state predicate: player owns 100 percent of Ash Creek, Prairie Crossing and Crown House.
   Final-state predicate: qualifying scenario principal debt equals $0.00.
 The final rank, ownership and debt predicates re-evaluate current state. The historical customer-sale and integration milestones
 remain completed after legitimate execution. Supporting farms, breweries, freight enterprises or other suppliers therefore need not
 remain owned after their event milestones unless a variant explicitly requires retention.
 12.3 Strategic Freedom
 The scenario should not prescribe which supporting enterprises must be owned, which managers must be hired, which customer
 segment must dominate or whether Crown wins through meals, lodging, gambling, service, marketing or another valid combination.
 Objectives constrain outcomes; the shared simulation determines routes.
 12.4 Scenario Calibration Holds
  The 1875 playtest start does not yet replace the broader project opening-date doctrine. Exact supported earlier start remains a
     design/research hold.
  Settlement population ranges, road distances, traffic thresholds and the observation window required to establish #1 rank remain
     scenario calibration.
  All exact wages, prices, sale values, loan rates, project costs, profit margins, concession terms and room rents from the playtest
    remain calibration unless separately researched and locked.
 PART XIII - AUTONOMOUS/TEXT PLAYTEST STATE DISCIPLINE
  Never invent missing cash or silently reconcile incompatible balances. Label unresolved state.
  Never silently create inventory. Physical products require legitimate source and provenance.

  After a player decision, execute the decision and advance to the next consequential date/event unless a material exception or

 PART XIV - RESEARCH & CALIBRATION HOLDS

      CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE - REVISION XX

 Autonomous Enterprise Ladder Playtest Integration: Scenario Geography, Transferability, Corporate
                                Control & Completion Presentation

                                            Revision date: September 8, 2026
                       Source baseline: Canonical Project Bible Revision XIX - September 7, 2026
                                                 Status: Active Canon integration

PRESERVATION GUARANTEE
Revision XX preserves Revision XIX in full except where this integration explicitly adds, deepens, clarifies or supersedes prior
wording. The complete Revision XIX document follows this integration unchanged as the preserved baseline. Where a conflict
exists, Revision XX controls. Exact autonomous-playtest prices, wages, traffic, project costs, interest rates, holding periods, map
shares and narration timing remain calibration unless this revision explicitly identifies a design lock.
PURPOSE
Revision XX integrates the autonomous Enterprise Ladder systems playtest and the subsequent scenario/world-scale design notes.
The autonomous campaign intentionally used a different business path from the prior full playtests and therefore tested whether the
scenario doctrine survives alternate player strategy. The result reinforces the existing economic foundation while adding stronger
rules for geographically bound objectives, very large multi-settlement maps, pre-operating major enterprises, relationship
transferability, internal segment reporting, effective control, lifetime attribution and scenario-completion presentation.
REVISION XX MASTER DOCTRINE
 • Scenario objectives may be bound to a designated on-map settlement, district, corridor or other geographic scope. Satisfying the
  same economic condition elsewhere does not qualify when geography is part of the authored objective.
 • The playable map is intended to support multiple meaningful settlements and a very large on-map economy. Off-map remains
   meaningful, but it is not a substitute economy that bypasses physical truth.
 • The Enterprise Ladder is defined by scale, transferability and ownership problems rather than by one required sequence of
   industries.
 •  Effective control, economic ownership, voting rights, board authority, management office and creditor claims remain distinct.
 • A major enterprise can become the player's controlled enterprise during development before ordinary revenue begins.
 • A relationship may fail to transfer when a business changes hands even when physical assets and legal ownership transfer
   successfully.
 • A consolidated enterprise may use internal segment reporting without manufacturing internal revenue or creating fake separate
   businesses.
 • Scenario completion should acknowledge the player's economic arc and lasting world impact without reciting a checklist or
  assuming one specific business route.
PART I - SCENARIO GEOGRAPHY & VERY LARGE WORLD DOCTRINE
1.1 Designated Scenario Settlement
A scenario may define one or more designated settlements, districts, corridors or regions as part of its objective authority. The
Enterprise Ladder may therefore require a qualifying enterprise, property, development or disposition to exist inside the named
scenario settlement rather than anywhere on the map.
Geography is an authored constraint, not a universal requirement. Open Frontier remains open-ended, and individual scenarios
decide whether location is part of qualification.
CANON LOCK - A scenario objective is not satisfied merely because its economic numbers are met somewhere else when
the objective explicitly names a geographic scope.


                                                            1

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 120/346 ====================

                           LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XX / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE

1.2 Geographic Qualification Can Combine With Economic Qualification
Scenario conditions may combine location with any other legitimate requirement: ownership of the property, debt state, operating
history, sale value, control transfer, population, infrastructure connection or other persistent fact. The geographic requirement
should be evaluated against the same authoritative world state as the economic requirement.
 • Example structure: qualifying enterprise is located in the designated town + player owns the required property + debt condition is
   satisfied + disposition condition is satisfied.
 • Do not expose geography as a cosmetic objective label if the player can actually satisfy the rule elsewhere.
1.3 Multi-Settlement Playable Map
The intended world may contain several substantial on-map towns, smaller settlements, rural clusters, industrial sites and corridors
in the same campaign. A scenario can focus attention on one primary settlement while other on-map settlements continue to trade,
migrate, compete, invest and develop under normal simulation rules.
1.4 On-Map Primacy With Off-Map Continuity
The design direction is that the overwhelming majority of ordinary business activity should occur on the playable map when
practical. Off-map remains essential for distant suppliers, regional markets, migration, correspondence, finance, travel beyond the
represented region and wider network connections.
This is a qualitative world-design priority, not a locked 95 percent or 99 percent numerical requirement. The exact balance depends
on final map scale, performance and business scope.
CANON LOCK - Off-map simulation remains part of the same causal economy. It may reduce representation detail but
must not create a second set of economic physics.
PART II - ENTERPRISE LADDER AUTONOMOUS-PLAY CLARIFICATIONS
2.1 Business Path Is Not Predetermined
The three Enterprise Ladder rungs describe increasing organizational and capital complexity, not a required bakery, freight, bank,
railway or other fixed industry sequence. A valid completion can use materially different businesses so long as the authored rung
requirements are met.
2.2 Pre-Operating Major Development Can Occupy the Enterprise Slot
A controlled major-enterprise development company can count as the player's one primary operating enterprise before ordinary
external revenue begins when the player has formed the entity, committed meaningful capital, obtained control and begun real
development toward operation.
This prevents the one-enterprise rule from being evaded by calling a railway, mine, utility or industrial project merely a pre-operating
project while simultaneously controlling an unrelated operating company.
CANON LOCK - Enterprise Ladder control restrictions follow substantive control and committed enterprise development,
not only whether the company has booked its first sale.
2.3 Control Transfer Governs Disposition
A seller note, retained receivable or other creditor claim does not by itself preserve operating control. Conversely, selling some
shares or resigning from an office does not qualify if the player retains effective governance or operating control.
Qualifying disposition occurs when the authored scenario's required control has genuinely transferred through the applicable
ownership and governance structure.
2.4 Control-Block Transactions Are Valid
A major-company disposition may be a whole-company acquisition, merger or control-block transaction rather than a sale of every
outstanding share. Minority investors may remain after the player's control ends. The player receives only the economic
consideration attached to the interest actually owned or otherwise lawfully conveyed.
2.5 Sale Readiness Is Evidence, Not Certification
Enterprise Evaluation may communicate operating history, customers, staff, management coverage, records, working capital,
relationship continuity and owner dependency. It should not become an opaque percentage that magically certifies a business as
sellable.
An actual buyer, financing structure, diligence result and control transfer remain necessary where the scenario calls for a
disposition.


                                                            2

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 121/346 ====================

                           LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XX / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE

2.6 Pre-Opening Commercial Discovery
A founder may approach prospective customers, suppliers, carriers, lenders or other counterparties before committing all startup
capital. Expressions of interest, quotes, letters, conditional commitments and negotiated preliminary agreements can provide
legitimate evidence about demand and feasibility.
Interest is not guaranteed demand. A non-binding conversation cannot become future revenue merely because the player asked
first.
CANON LOCK - Founding a business should not require either blind capital expenditure or accidental omniscience.
Legitimate pre-opening discovery is allowed, but commitment remains distinct from fulfillment.
PART III - TRANSFERABILITY, RELATIONSHIPS & OWNER
DEPENDENCY
3.1 Relationship Transferability
A change of business ownership does not automatically transfer every relationship surrounding the enterprise. Supplier terms,
customer arrangements, leases, licenses, service agreements, personal trust and informal credit can have different continuation
rules.
 •  Automatically continuing under valid terms.
 • Assignable by the current holder.
 • Requires counterparty consent.
 • Terminable or renegotiable on change of control.
 •  Likely to continue but not contractually guaranteed.
 •  Strongly personal to a departing owner, manager or worker.
 • Unknown until diligence or negotiation produces evidence.
CANON LOCK - Buying the enterprise does not teleport another person's trust or consent to the buyer.
3.2 Owner Dependency Is a Capability Map
Acquisition and sale diligence should ask what disappears if the owner leaves. Owner dependency can include physical labor,
technical expertise, purchasing judgment, management, customer relationships, supplier relationships, reputation, local knowledge,
records knowledge and informal coordination.
A replacement wage alone can understate the problem when the departing owner supplied several different capabilities or
relationships.
3.3 Technical Leadership and General Management Remain Distinct
A skilled operating lead can control a technical domain without automatically becoming the enterprise's commercial or financial
manager. Mature enterprises may legitimately divide authority among technical superintendents, commercial managers, clerks and
general management according to workload and competence.
3.4 Employee and Manager Succession
The existing management/employee buyout doctrine is reinforced. A worker can progress from employee to delegated authority to
prospective buyer to independent entrepreneur when financing, capability and personal choice support the transition. The seller is
not required to prefer an employee buyer over a stronger external offer.
3.5 Sold Enterprises Persist as Economic History
A sold enterprise remains available to become a future supplier, customer, competitor, borrower, employer or acquisition target.
Ownership change should enrich world history rather than erase prior player work.
PART IV - CONSOLIDATED ENTERPRISE REPORTING
4.1 One Enterprise Can Have Internal Segments
A genuinely consolidated enterprise may maintain diagnostic reporting by site, department, route, product family, operating function
or other meaningful segment while retaining one authoritative enterprise treasury and external ledger where the legal/economic
structure requires it.



                                                            3

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 122/346 ====================

                           LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XX / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE

4.2 Segment Reporting Does Not Create Internal Revenue
Internal segment reports may attribute cost, workload, inventory usage, margin contribution and capital consumption for diagnosis.
They must not manufacture external revenue, duplicate cash or create profit merely because value moved from one part of the
same consolidated enterprise to another.
CANON LOCK - Internal reporting is analytical attribution inside one enterprise, not permission to create a second
economic truth.
4.3 Segment Reports Should Explain Bottlenecks
The purpose of internal reporting is to answer practical ownership questions: which site consumes working capital, which function is
capacity-constrained, which product or route earns contribution, where labor is concentrated and whether integration is actually
helping. It is not a requirement for formal modern management-accounting detail.
PART V - MAJOR ENTERPRISE DEVELOPMENT, CAPITAL & STAGING
5.1 Generic Development Stage
The railway development chain from Revision XIX establishes a broader pattern for capital-intensive enterprises. Mines, utilities,
industrial plants, large property concerns and other major ventures may have meaningful investigation, promotion/formation,
development, capital assembly, construction/setup, commissioning and operation stages before mature operation.
5.2 Physical Commissioning Is Not Standalone Economic Viability
A project stage can be physically complete, legally usable and capable of serving customers while still failing to cover its operating,
maintenance and financing burden as an independent business. Revenue from an early stage may help the next stage, but the
game must not assume that it will.
CANON LOCK - Physical staging and economic staging are separate facts.
5.3 Outside Capital Must Bring Outside Rights
The player may legitimately control a major enterprise while personally funding only a minority of its total capital. That scale
transition is allowed only when outside investors and creditors have real claims, governance, covenants, repayment priority,
information rights or other period-appropriate protections. Outside capital is not free owner leverage.
5.4 Redundancy Has Contextual Economic Value
Spare or reserve equipment can look inefficient during normal operation yet become valuable during failure, peak demand or
maintenance. The value should emerge from avoided lost capacity and continuity, not from an abstract Backup Equipment bonus.
PART VI - LIFETIME LEDGER & CORPORATE ATTRIBUTION
6.1 Enterprise Activity Versus Owner Activity
As outside shareholders become important, the Lifetime Ledger must distinguish the activity of enterprises the player controls from
the economic income actually attributable to the player. Controlling a large corporation does not make its entire revenue the player's
personal income or wealth.
 •  Controlled-enterprise external revenue.
 •  Controlled-enterprise operating profit.
 • Owner distributions/dividends actually received.
 •  Interest personally received.
 • Realized disposition proceeds and gains/losses.
 • Value of the player's actual equity or creditor claim.
 •  Enterprise Value and debt remain separate from owner Net Worth.
6.2 Lifetime Ledger Is Persistent Scenario Authority
The autonomous text playtest again showed that cumulative taxes, payroll and other lifetime statistics become unreliable when
reconstructed from narrative summaries after the fact. The canonical Lifetime Ledger should be maintained continuously from
authoritative transactions and events when a scenario depends on historical accumulation.




                                                            4

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 123/346 ====================

                           LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XX / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE

6.3 Scenario Pacing Is Calibration
Outside equity and debt can allow a skilled player to reach major-enterprise scale far earlier than a personal-cash-only progression.
That is not inherently an exploit. The intended pace of a specific scenario should be calibrated deliberately through opportunity
availability, investor standards, financing, governance, risk and objective design rather than by forbidding outside capital.
PART VII - SCENARIO COMPLETION PRESENTATION
7.1 Completion Should Summarize the Arc
A completed scenario may end with a short cinematic, narration and result presentation that acknowledges what the player changed
in the world. For The Enterprise Ladder, the emotional arc is small ownership -> larger organization -> major enterprise -> lasting
economic legacy.
7.2 Narration Must Remain Route-Agnostic
Because players can satisfy the scenario through different industries and financing structures, standard completion narration should
describe the scale and meaning of the accomplishment rather than naming a bakery, freight company, railway or other path that
may not have occurred.
7.3 Do Not Read the Objective Checklist Back to the Player
Completion presentation should not sound like a report that lists every fulfilled condition. The objective UI already serves that
function. The ending should provide closure, acknowledge the persistent world and hand control back to the player or campaign
flow.
CANON LOCK - Scenario completion presentation is recognition of the player's economic story, not a narrated checklist.
PART VIII - CALIBRATION & RESEARCH HOLDS
8.1 Map Activity Share
The planning estimate that perhaps 95-99 percent of ordinary business activity should be on-map is not a locked numerical rule.
Preserve only the qualitative priority of on-map primacy until final world scale and performance are proven.
8.2 Completion Cinematic Timing and Voice
Exact narration length, camera duration, voice actor/accent, music, subtitle timing and final cinematic structure are production
calibration, not Canon. A shorter roughly half-minute target is currently favored for prototyping but remains subject to
player-attention testing.
8.3 Corporate and Railway Law
Revision XIX research holds concerning railway corporate law, control transactions, right-of-way, interchange, shareholder
procedure and related-party conduct remain active. Revision XX does not invent missing period law.
PART IX - REVISION XX LOCK SUMMARY
9.1 New Locks
 • Scenario objectives may be geographically bound to designated on-map places.
 • A very large map may contain multiple meaningful settlements; off-map remains the same causal economy at reduced
   representation.
 •  Enterprise Ladder phases are structural and do not require one fixed industry path.
 • Substantive control and committed development can occupy the one-enterprise slot before revenue begins.
 • Control transfer, not note repayment or job-title change, determines disposition.
 •  Relationship continuation after sale is not automatic.
 • Owner dependency includes capability, knowledge and relationships, not just labor hours.
 • Consolidated-enterprise segment reporting must not create fake internal revenue or cash.
 • Physical project staging and standalone economic viability remain distinct.
 •  Controlled-enterprise activity and owner-attributable income remain distinct in the Lifetime Ledger.
 • Scenario-ending narration should recognize the arc and remain compatible with alternate valid routes.

            LAND & LEDGERS
           CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE - REVISION XIX

Third Full Playtest Integration: Enterprise Ladder, Rail Capital, Retail Labor, Historical
                         Events & New Business Research

                                            Revision date: September 7, 2026
                       Source baseline: Canonical Project Bible Revision XVIII - August 30, 2026
                                                Status: Active Canon integration

PRESERVATION GUARANTEE
Revision XIX preserves Revision XVIII in full except where this integration explicitly adds, deepens, corrects, parks or
supersedes prior wording. The complete Revision XVIII document follows this integration unchanged as the preserved baseline.
Where a conflict exists, Revision XIX controls. Exact playtest dollar amounts, wages, traffic thresholds, construction costs,
interest rates and durations remain calibration unless this revision explicitly identifies a historical or design lock.

PURPOSE
Revision XIX integrates the third and longest full text systems playtest, The Enterprise Ladder. The playtest ran from Spring 1880
through June 1890 and moved through three materially different enterprises: Merritt Bakery, Dakota Union Grain Company and
Dakota Gateway Railway Company. It validated existing Canon authorities around workload, delegation, Physical Truth, working
capital, projects, logistics, records, information and business disposition while exposing major additions needed for action
discoverability, task granularity, dynamic liquidity, corporate finance, staged railway development, historical event delivery,
General Store labor, barter, early telephone use, saloon/vice systems and reward/private-detective business design.
The common rule remains causal simulation over abstract game bonuses. Complexity is welcome when the systems are
connected, discoverable and materially consequential. Complexity is not an excuse for hidden mechanics, repetitive owner clicks
or isolated novelty features.

REVISION XIX MASTER DOCTRINE
  • The player should virtually always be able to find something meaningful to do, but should not be forced to personally decide
   everything that could be done.
  • Feature breadth is desirable when features reuse shared economic, physical, legal, labor, information and management
   systems.
  • Mechanics should be discoverable through ordinary play, UI explanation, visible prerequisites, causal consequences and
   manager/contractor recommendations rather than outside guides.
  • Routine execution belongs to workers, managers, contractors and standing policy. Owner attention belongs to strategy,
   exceptions, capital allocation, negotiation and decisions deliberately reserved by the player.
  • Projects, agreements, tasks, shipments, legal rights, corporate claims and historical events remain persistent world state. A
   summary screen is never the source of truth.
  • Historical occurrence, not modern moral comfort or legality alone, determines whether an economic activity can exist in the
   simulated world. Illegal activity remains illegal and exposed to the applicable enforcement system.
  • Exact numbers from the playtest remain calibration unless independently established as a dated historical rule.

PART I - ENTERPRISE LADDER & SCENARIO DOCTRINE

1.1 Scenario identity
The Enterprise Ladder remains a canonical scenario family. Its core loop is:
Build value -> prove the enterprise works -> transfer control -> reinvest into a materially larger enterprise.
The intended learning progression is not merely bigger revenue. Each rung should introduce qualitatively different ownership
problems.

1.2 One primary operating enterprise
The standard scenario uses one primary active operating enterprise at a time. Passive investments, seller notes, property
holdings, securities and other non-operating interests may persist where the scenario allows them.



                                                   1

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 126/346 ====================

                           LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XIX / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE


A Consolidated Enterprise may contain several divisions, locations or legally distinct controlled ledgers when they are genuinely
integrated into one operating strategy. Merely placing unrelated businesses under one administrative screen does not make
them one enterprise for scenario purposes.

1.3 Value creation before disposition
A qualifying Enterprise Ladder disposition requires meaningful value creation or organizational improvement rather than passive
appreciation alone. Valid value creation can include profitable expansion, stronger customer relationships, added productive
capacity, improved records, improved property, better logistics, lower risk, improved management continuity, new market access
or other causal improvements.

1.4 Qualifying going-concern disposition
A qualifying disposition should normally demonstrate:
  • real operations and an operating history;
  • genuine outside customers or revenue where the business model requires them;
  • required employees, contractors, suppliers and service relationships;
  • adequate records for a serious buyer to understand the business;
  • no hidden owner subsidy disguising an economically broken enterprise;
  • a legitimate buyer, merger partner or other counterparty;
  • actual transfer of control;
  • a realized economic outcome for the seller after relevant costs.
A formal manager is not universally required. Transferability is the real test. A scenario may add a stricter autonomy objective,
but that objective is scenario-specific rather than a universal law of business sale.

1.5 Enterprise Evaluation presentation
A simple player-facing Enterprise Evaluation may summarize:
  • PROFIT
  • CUSTOMERS
  • OPERATIONS
  • TRANSFERABILITY
  • ESTIMATED SALE VALUE
These are read models built from real evidence. Do not replace the underlying systems with a single Business Quality score.

1.6 Scenario completion at scale
The final enterprise does not have to exhaust every future growth path. A railway does not need to reach every intended
destination merely because additional profitable expansion remains possible. The scenario can complete once the enterprise has
been materially built, proven, made transferable and legitimately transferred.

1.7 Corporate completion
If the player owns only a minority economic interest, the player cannot personally sell the entire corporation. A qualifying final
transfer can occur through a merger, whole-company acquisition, stock transaction or other valid corporate disposition requiring
the appropriate governance and creditor treatment.
