Cash flow is not profit.
Profit is not Net Worth.
Borrowing is not revenue.
Principal repayment is not ordinary expense.
Owner capital contribution is not revenue.
Owner distribution is not ordinary expense.
Asset acquisition is not ordinary operating consumption.
Internal transfer is not external portfolio revenue.
Possession is not necessarily ownership.
Current replacement cost does not rewrite historical acquisition cost.
Known transaction facts remain exact even when books are incomplete.
Audit 01 Canon status: LOCKED.

SYSTEM AUDIT 02 - PEOPLE / LABOR / SKILLS
Final verdict: KEEP + DEEPEN, with targeted SIMPLIFICATION of presentation and repetitive control.
The Canon correctly abandoned occupation-as-character-class and now separates Aptitude, Skill, Experience and
Knowledge / Domain Familiarity. Businesses generate workload rather than fixed employee slots, employees provide finite
compatible labor, schedules interact with travel and rest, compensation and poaching are real market forces, and skills grow
from actual work rather than completion-day XP bonuses.

1. System purpose
The People / Labor / Skills system answers:
Who can realistically do the work, who is available to do it, how well will they probably do it, what does employing them cost,
what happens to them through work, and why do they stay, negotiate or leave?
Employees are persistent economic people, not interchangeable production modifiers.

2. Universal labor loop
Work Need Exists -> Required capabilities/location/timing identified -> Potential workers considered -> Worker
assigned -> Travel/arrival/availability -> Task performed -> Time/quality/material/safety consequences -> Work
outcome -> Experience/knowledge/reputation generated -> Fatigue/injury/satisfaction/relationship consequences ->
Compensation -> Retention/advancement/future availability.
This same grammar applies across store service, team driving, bookkeeping, construction, repair, mining, agriculture,
management and other work.

3. Aptitude, Skill, Experience and Knowledge
KEEP the following distinctions:
Aptitude: tendency to learn or perform related capabilities well.
Skill: present capability.
Experience: what the person has actually encountered and done.
Knowledge / Domain Familiarity: understanding of a particular trade, industry, market, place, organization, procedure or
customer base.
A highly skilled generic negotiator does not automatically possess deep lumber-market knowledge. A banking veteran and an
ordinary bookkeeper may have similar numerical skill but very different domain familiarity.

4. Capability architecture and catalogue control
To prevent skill-stat explosion, use three conceptual layers:
Capability Family
Broad transferable ability, such as:
Commercial Interaction
Numerical/Clerical
Organization/Management
Construction
Mechanical/Repair



                                           REVISION XVII INTEGRATION 9

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 166/346 ====================

                         LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XVII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE


Animal Handling
Transport
Food Processing
Extraction/Industrial
Agricultural
Task Capability
What materially affects execution, such as framing, finish carpentry, loading, dispatching, diagnosis, painting or masonry.
Domain Familiarity
Contextual knowledge such as residential construction, mine timbering, railroad work, banking, livestock freight or local
customer relationships.
Player-facing presentation should usually be descriptive rather than a wall of numeric RPG attributes.

Example:

Experienced carpenter. Strong framing and layout. Adequate finish work. Limited masonry experience. Familiar with
residential construction.
Detailed numbers may exist internally where useful.

5. Occupation is descriptive, not class
Occupation summarizes current work or history. It does not restrict the person to one hard class.
A teamster may also possess animal handling, loading, repair familiarity, route knowledge and customer experience. Those
capabilities remain relevant if their job changes.

6. Attempt Rule and task types
KEEP the rule that low competence normally changes time, quality, waste, rework, supervision need, safety and customer
response rather than creating arbitrary locks.
Distinguish:

Ordinary attemptable
A novice can reasonably try.
Attemptable but dangerous/specialist-sensitive
Possible but poor competence can have serious consequences.
Actually restricted
Action is impossible without real authority, equipment, access, information or specialist capability.
Hard locks must come from reality, not progression gates.

7. Workload-based staffing
New elevated doctrine:
Businesses create work, not abstract employee requirements.
A business’s staffing need emerges from concurrent work, timing and required capabilities. A store may need one person
Tuesday morning and three Saturday afternoon without an artificial employee-slot change.

8. Work Demand grammar
Each meaningful work demand may identify:
what needs doing
where
when
expected time burden
required/relevant capabilities
urgency
whether it can wait
whether several people can collaborate
whether one worker can cover compatible work in the same period
consequence if missed
Examples include customer service, restocking, unloading, month-end reconciliation and weather-sensitive construction work.



                                           REVISION XVII INTEGRATION 10

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 167/346 ====================

                         LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XVII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE

9. Role is not capability
New lock:
Role grants responsibility and authority. Capability determines how well that responsibility is exercised.
A Manager or Foreman title does not manufacture judgment, scheduling skill, leadership or technical skill. An untitled
experienced worker can coordinate effectively.

10. Management is real labor
Managers perform finite administrative and decision work. Management overload should appear through causal symptoms:
delayed decisions
unfilled vacancies
weak scheduling
late supplier response
stale records
unresolved exceptions
weak supervision
poor hiring
excessive travel/attention burden
Avoid abstract Management Capacity bonuses where actual workload can explain the outcome.

11. Mentorship consumes time
New explicit rule:
Teaching consumes the mentor’s time and attention.
A veteran who demonstrates, checks, explains and corrects work may produce less personally while accelerating another
worker’s development. Training is therefore an investment with opportunity cost.

12. Learning
KEEP continuous learning from relevant exposure, novelty/difficulty, aptitude, instructor competence, teaching ability, time
together and feedback.
Use diminishing value:

new exposure: strong learning
developing familiarity: normal learning
routine mastery: small refinement
novel difficult situation: renewed learning opportunity
Do not add routine generic skill decay. Long absence, injury, age or specific circumstances may matter where physically
justified.

13. Experience memory
Experience should preserve meaningful career history rather than every microscopic task event.
Useful memory may include:

years/seasons in domain
major task exposure
difficult problems encountered
supervisory responsibility
businesses worked for
important projects
unusual failures/successes
market/local familiarity

14. Recruitment needs full loop
Recruitment becomes:
Vacancy / Work Pressure -> Employer defines need -> Potential candidates become discoverable -> Information
gathered -> Candidate evaluates employer -> Employer evaluates candidate -> Offer -> Negotiation / acceptance /
refusal -> Employment begins -> Actual performance reveals more information.


                                           REVISION XVII INTEGRATION 11

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 168/346 ====================

                         LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XVII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE


Candidate sources can include:

local unemployed workers
employed workers
referrals
employee networks
kin/household contacts
migrants
newspaper notices
professional contacts
other settlements
There is no omniscient global candidate list.

15. Labor supply is not population
New lock:
Effective labor supply depends on availability, compatibility, willingness, wages/conditions, housing, commute,
household responsibilities, health, season, competing employers and migration feasibility.
Town population is not the same as available labor.

16. Wage markets are capability-specific
Avoid one universal town wage multiplier. Demand for teamsters, clerks, carpenters, bookkeepers or miners can move
differently depending on overlapping alternatives and industries.
Booms should propagate through actual competition for compatible workers.

17. Employment relationship
Treat employment as a persistent simulation relationship. It can include:
employer
worker
primary responsibilities
compensation basis
board/meals/lodging where applicable
schedule expectations
bonus/commission/profit-sharing where supported
authority
start date/status
material special conditions
This does not imply every worker has a literal written contract.

18. No universal Morale bar
Do not collapse pay reliability, wage level, hours, fatigue, safety, commute, housing, manager relationship, broken promises,
promotion opportunity, reputation and outside offers into one player-facing Morale score.
Use explanations such as:

Generally satisfied. Concerned about long hours. Commute is difficult. Believes pay is below alternatives.

19. Retention and poaching
KEEP. Valuable workers can request better compensation, report competing offers or leave. Responses can include wage,
bonus, promotion, duties, hours, accommodation, stability, status and other grounded terms. Money does not have to solve
every retention problem.

20. Promotion
New lock:
Promotion changes authority and responsibility; it does not automatically increase capability.
A brilliant craft worker may be a poor manager. A moderately skilled craft worker may be an excellent foreman because of
organization and communication.




                                           REVISION XVII INTEGRATION 12

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 169/346 ====================

                         LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XVII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE

21. Cross-business labor and cost attribution
A person can temporarily work across controlled businesses without fictional firing/rehiring where authority allows. However:
legal employer/payroll payer remains real;
economic consumer of the worker’s time can differ;
internal allocation/reimbursement may be tracked;
consolidated profit must remain truthful.

22. No double-booking
New hard lock:
A person’s time and physical location are authoritative. One person cannot perform simultaneous incompatible work
in different places.
This applies to employees, managers and mentors.
Some decision/information tasks can occur remotely only when communication and authority make them physically plausible.

23. Fatigue
KEEP cumulative causal fatigue. Long shifts create slower work, errors, injury exposure, absence, irritability and turnover
rather than a generic production penalty.
Repeated overwork matters more than one unusual day.

24. Sleep
KEEP as a lightweight causal connection among work hours, commute, housing and labor performance. Do not require
player-visible minute-level sleep simulation.

25. Nutrition
KEEP the economic connection but simplify presentation heavily.
Track aggregate food adequacy/regularity such as:

well supplied
adequate
poor
severely strained
Causes remain physical: household reserves, affordability, meals, boarding and shortages. Do not build a nutrition minigame.

26. Commute
KEEP. Geography changes practical labor supply through travel time, rest, punctuality, availability and job attractiveness.
Better transport can expand the usable labor market because people can actually reach work.

27. Household responsibilities
A person’s labor availability can be affected by real household responsibilities such as dependent care, illness, domestic
work, pregnancy/recovery, elder care, childcare, seasonal household work and household enterprise.
These effects must come from actual household/person circumstances rather than gender stereotypes or fixed demographic
penalties.

28. Family labor
New lock:
Family labor is still labor.
A spouse or adult child can perform real business work without a conventional wage transaction, but their time, fatigue,
household contribution and outside earning opportunity remain economically meaningful.

29. Illness/injury
KEEP person-specific continuity effects. Reduced availability matters according to actual role coverage. The loss of the only
qualified operator is much more serious than the same injury in a redundant organization.

30. Task-specific mistakes
KEEP. Clerk errors, driving errors, construction defects, banking mistakes and other failures create domain-specific
consequences, not one generic Quality penalty.





                                           REVISION XVII INTEGRATION 13

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 170/346 ====================

                         LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XVII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE

31. Worker information doctrine
Separate:
Known facts
Current employment, wage, attendance, performed jobs, observed failures, recorded training.
Evidence
References, prior-employment claims, reputation, interview impression.
Inference
Likely aptitude, fit, retention, management potential.
Unknown
Unobserved or unsupported information.
The player does not automatically know true hidden skill values.

32. Labor pressure explanation
Labor shortages should be explainable through actual vacancies, wage offers, housing, competing employers, migration,
worker exits and capability scarcity rather than a raw Labor Pressure score.

33. Scale transformation
Owner-operator: can one worker cover the counter while I unload?
Small business: hire another clerk or work longer myself?
Growing business: who should supervise?
Multi-business owner: can a worker cover another business temporarily?
Mature portfolio: why is retention poor in this division?
Capital command: retain senior manager, promote internal candidate or recruit externally?

34. Canon locks from Audit 02
Workload is not headcount.
Role is not capability.
Occupation is not class.
Aptitude is not skill.
Training is work.
Promotion is not training.
Employment is a relationship.
Labor supply is not population.
Time is exclusive.
Family labor is still labor.
Human strain is causal.
Worker agency persists.
Capability information is imperfect.
Audit 02 Canon status: LOCKED.

SYSTEM AUDIT 03 - HOUSEHOLDS / CONSUMPTION / HOUSING / MIGRATION
Final verdict: KEEP + DEEPEN, with simplification guardrails.
The household-housing architecture is one of the strongest systems in the project. Household is not House. Kinship is distinct
from economic household membership. Residential Occupancy is distinct from Accommodation Space, Building and Parcel.
The biggest need is a common household-allocation grammar and a complete information-aware migration loop.

1. System purpose
The combined system answers:
Who lives together economically, what resources and obligations they share, what they need, how they respond when they
cannot afford everything, where they can realistically live, why they enter or leave a settlement and how those choices affect
businesses and labor markets?



                                           REVISION XVII INTEGRATION 14

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 171/346 ====================

                         LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XVII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE


Households can be consumers, labor suppliers, tenants, landlords, debtors, family-business labor sources, property owners,
care networks and migration units.

2. Universal household loop
Household composition/resources -> Income/production/reserves arrive -> Needs and obligations mature ->
Household decides what can be satisfied -> Use reserves / produce internally / purchase / use credit / substitute /
postpone / go without -> Individual member performs physical action -> Goods/services/housing obtained ->
Household state changes -> Shortfall/surplus consequences -> Work/housing/credit/migration decisions adjust ->
History persists.

3. Household identity
KEEP. A household is a persistent domestic-economic unit. It can consist of one adult or many people. Household size and
composition emerge through birth, marriage, death, adult children leaving/staying, migration, kin hosting, splitting and merger
rather than fixed templates.

4. Household / family / occupancy separation
KEEP foundational hierarchy:
Person
Household
Residential Occupancy
Accommodation Space
Building
Parcel
Household membership, kinship, property ownership and where somebody sleeps can change independently.

5. Household finance and allocation under scarcity
Needs do not create money. Households can spend actual cash, use available credit, sell labor/goods, consume reserves,
substitute, delay, reduce quantity or go without.
New Household Allocation grammar: when a household cannot satisfy everything, decisions consider:

urgency
severity
amount
substitutability
deferrability
existing reserves
credit/relationship consequences
household preference/circumstances
There is no rigid universal priority such as Food > Rent > Fuel > Debt. Different households can make different grounded
choices.

6. No household budgeting minigame
NPC households decide their ordinary consumption autonomously. The player influences them only through legitimate
authority and economic relationships: wages, prices, rents, credit, employment, housing supply, boarding, services, property
and business availability.
Player-facing household information should be diagnostic and limited by legitimate knowledge.

7. Consumption reserves
KEEP target/reserve/critical concepts. Purchasing urgency rises as household reserves fall rather than every household
shopping on a fixed weekly script.

8. Consumption category restraint
Track a category only when it creates meaningful commercial decisions. Potential categories include staple food,
meat/protein, preserved food, fuel, clothing/textiles, household consumables, tools/hardware where relevant, animal feed,
medicines/services and occasional durable purchases.
Do not simulate every fork, button, sock or bar of soap as an independent household need unless the product is economically
meaningful elsewhere.




                                           REVISION XVII INTEGRATION 15

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 172/346 ====================

                         LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XVII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE

9. Household demand remains physical and competitive
Need becomes a purchase only when:
household has reason to act;
it has cash/credit or another legitimate means;
an acceptable supplier is known/reachable;
stock/service exists;
somebody can physically shop or receive delivery;
the transaction actually occurs.
Households do not automatically buy from the player.

10. Household production
KEEP economically meaningful small production such as coops, gardens, root-cellar storage and boarder rooms where
appropriate.
Such activities use real labor, inputs, seasonality and space. Do not turn households into manually controlled homestead
minigames.

11. Domestic workload
New lock:
Domestic work consumes real household labor time even when no wage payment occurs.
Domestic workload can include cooking, cleaning, childcare, fuel handling, water hauling, laundry, animal care, garden work
and boarding labor. Who performs it depends on actual household circumstances and calibrated historical behavior, not
arbitrary stereotypes.

12. Boarding
KEEP. Boarding is not simply bed capacity. Where board includes meals/services, capacity also depends on food, fuel,
water, cooking, cleaning, laundry and labor. Boarding can convert regional labor into locally usable labor without a fake
recruitment bonus.

13. Housing ontology
KEEP exactly:
Person -> Household -> Residential Occupancy -> Accommodation Space -> Building -> Parcel.

Double Houses remain one Building with two independent accommodation units unless actual legal/property facts say
otherwise.

14. Accommodation types are arrangements, not tiers
KEEP owner-occupied, rental, room rental, boarding/lodging, employer lodging, kin hosting, doubled-up/shared, transient
lodging, temporary camp, precarious accommodation and no stable shelter as non-linear arrangements.

15. No universal Housing Quality score
Housing suitability is household-specific and may depend on:
shelter capacity
weather protection
heating
water
sanitation
cooking
storage
privacy/shared status
condition
fire exposure
yard/outbuilding access
proximity
seasonal accessibility
Summary suitability can exist but cannot replace the real factors.



                                           REVISION XVII INTEGRATION 16

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 173/346 ====================

                         LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XVII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE

16. Crowding
KEEP. Capacity creates rising strain rather than a hard occupancy wall. People can double up, host relatives, use camps or
accept cramped rooms with real consequences such as privacy loss, domestic burden, sanitation strain, wear, fire exposure
and move pressure.

17. Rental market
KEEP landlord-set asking rents and actual household choice. New construction responds with delay because it requires land,
capital, labor, materials and time. Several investors can respond simultaneously and oversupply the market.
Vacancy as information
Vacancy is evidence about rent/location/suitability/demand, not an automatic instruction to change rent.

18. Rent agreement memory
New lock:
Rent is an occupancy/tenancy agreement, not a daily spot-price reset.
Current tenant rent and current market asking rent can differ. Changes occur when the actual arrangement and applicable
law permit.

19. Housing pressure is match-specific
KEEP. A town can have empty bachelor lodging while families face severe shortage. Housing pressure compares
households with acceptable reachable accommodation, not Population - Beds.

20. Migration requires full loop
New universal migration loop:
Push / Opportunity exists -> Potential migrant becomes aware of destination -> Destination evaluated ->
Job/business/kin/property opportunity assessed -> Housing feasibility assessed -> Travel cost/difficulty assessed ->
Move/wait/reject decision -> Physical travel -> Temporary arrival state -> Employment/housing/consumption
stabilization -> Stay / onward move / return / leave.

21. Migration obeys Information Distance
People cannot respond to opportunities they have no plausible way to know about. Awareness may come through kin, former
coworkers, newspapers, recruiters, travelers, merchants, rail/transport networks, telegraph where appropriate, labor agents
where supported, project reputation or direct offers.

22. Individual vs household migration
A single worker and a household face different moving burdens. A worker may move first, board near work and bring family
later. Household migration may depend on family housing, spouse opportunities, travel, reserves, kin and job stability.

23. Relocation costs
Moving has friction:
travel
time
lost work
moving possessions
advance rent/deposits where applicable
uncertainty
separation from support networks
Small wage differences therefore do not cause constant town-to-town ping-pong.

24. Migration inertia
People accumulate real reasons to stay:
property
stable rent
employer relationship
kin
spouse employment
children/dependents
business ownership


                                           REVISION XVII INTEGRATION 17

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 174/346 ====================

                         LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XVII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE


local reputation
debt
customers
community familiarity
This is not a Loyalty stat; it is actual embeddedness.

25. Population growth decomposition
Settlement population analysis should distinguish:
natural change: births/deaths
individual labor migration
whole-household migration
household formation
household dissolution/merger
temporary/transient presence
A town gaining temporary workers is not automatically experiencing durable population growth.

26. Retention matters as much as attraction
New lock:
Arrival is not successful settlement growth.
A town can attract workers through high wages but fail to retain them because of poor housing, food costs, employment
instability, winter strain, weak family accommodation, debt or stronger alternatives elsewhere.

27. Temporary boom camps and durable conversion
Boom activity can create:
job pulse -> transient workers -> temporary lodging -> supporting merchants/services -> permanent housing
investment -> family migration -> durable settlement

or reverse:

job pulse ends -> workers leave -> boarding vacancy -> speculative housing vacancy -> merchants weaken -> town
contracts.

28. Employer lodging
KEEP. Employer housing works by creating actual acceptable accommodation and therefore changes recruitment feasibility.
It also creates real construction, maintenance, property, fuel/service and vacancy burdens.

29. Housing investment is speculative
Developers act on expectations, not future truth. High rents, boarding saturation or expected project expansion can motivate
construction. If expectations fail, vacancy and distress can follow.

30. Household hardship is causal
Do not create a Poverty meter. Household hardship should propagate through actual events:
job loss -> reduced purchases -> more credit -> rent pressure -> altered work search -> possible relocation.

31. Credit connection
Merchant credit bridges temporary income timing but does not make households wealthier. Unpaid household debt becomes
merchant receivable risk and can become merchant loss.

32. Winter/fuel pressure
KEEP. Housing economics include rent, fuel, heat retention, stove capability, reserve levels, substitution and winter strain. A
larger/draftier dwelling can be more expensive in total even if nominal rent is attractive.

33. Household information limits
The player does not automatically know exact household cash, food inventory, rent arrears, disputes or migration intention.
Knowledge depends on customer, tenant, employment, credit, landlord, reputation or other legitimate channels.

34. Household UI
Keep household panels lightweight. Show composition, broad reserves/pressure, housing and known relationships where
appropriate, not dozens of tabs.



                                           REVISION XVII INTEGRATION 18

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 175/346 ====================

                         LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XVII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE

35. Demographic lifecycle
KEEP births, deaths, marriages, household formation/split/merge, migration, displacement and guardianship as relationship
changes preserving person identity.

36. World generation
KEEP person-first generation:
generate people
establish kinship
generate prior family history
form households
assign housing
validate aggregate output
Do not generate fixed stereotypes such as Family of Five and then manufacture people to fit the template.

37. Canon locks from Audit 03
Household need is not purchasing power.
Consumption is reserve- and urgency-driven.
Household action remains physical.
Domestic work is labor.
Accommodation is a relationship.
Housing availability is match-specific.
Crowding is consequence, not prohibition.
Rent is an agreement.
Migration requires awareness.
Migration requires feasibility.
Moving has cost and inertia.
Arrival is not retention.
Transient population is economically real but analytically separate.
Housing supply responds with delay and uncertainty.
Household hardship propagates causally.
Audit 03 Canon status: LOCKED.

SYSTEM AUDIT 04 - PROPERTY / LAND / BUILDINGS / CONSTRUCTION / DEVELOPMENT
Final verdict: KEEP + DEEPEN.
Property already expresses the ownership fantasy exceptionally well: persistent parcels, real sellers, private approaches,
negotiation, diligence, flexible use, physical project execution and persistent property history. The main need is one common
Property Lifecycle authority connecting legal geography, control, acquisition, project authorization, construction, use,
redevelopment and disposition.

1. System purpose
The system answers:
What exactly do I control, what can I realistically do with it, what will it cost to change, what risks am I inheriting and why is
this land more or less valuable to me than to someone else?
Property value can arise from frontage, traffic, road/depot access, parcel depth, yard capacity, drainage, neighbors, current
improvements, title/control, occupants, taxes/debt, conversion potential and expansion potential.

2. Unified Property Lifecycle
Land/property exists -> Ownership and legal rights exist -> Opportunity becomes known -> Site/property evaluated
-> Owner approached -> Terms negotiated -> Diligence -> Financing/conditions -> Closing -> Actual
ownership/control transfers -> Carry property as-is OR authorize project -> Materials/labor/contractors committed ->
Physical work -> Building/site changes -> Productive use -> Condition/occupancy/value evolve -> Expand / convert /
refinance / sell / abandon / lose.




                                           REVISION XVII INTEGRATION 19

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 176/346 ====================

                         LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XVII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE

3. Survey/legal geography
KEEP parcel identity, parcel type, acreage, jurisdiction, ownership form, transfer status and historical provenance. Current
ownership/transferability remains separate from historical provenance.
Restricted federal, reservation, trust-allotment or other land must not become a normal Buy button merely because it is
visible.

4. Ownership vs control
New lock:
Owning land and possessing a legitimate right to use or control land are not always the same thing.
Control can arise through ownership, tenancy/lease, occupancy, contract, right-of-way, corridor rights, management authority
or another historically valid relationship.

5. Parcel / Building / Functional Space separation
KEEP:
Parcel = legal/property geography.
Building/Improvement = physical structure.
Functional Space/Residential Unit/Business Space = usable internal physical/economic space.
Occupancy/Business/Lease = relationship using that space.
Double Houses remain one Building with independent residential units unless facts establish otherwise.

6. Suitability is use-specific
New explicit lock:
Use + Site -> Fit. There is no universal parcel Commercial Potential score.
Examples:
General Store
frontage, traffic, receiving, storage, nearby households.
Livery
stable/yard depth, road access, water, feed handling, nuisance/space.
Freight Yard
loading space, major route/depot proximity, maneuvering room, stable/storage.
Boarding House
accommodation space, kitchen/service capability, employment access.
Sawmill
large site, log access, freight, fire/nuisance separation, water where relevant.

7. Flexible conversion
KEEP the rule: anything sensible into anything sensible. Buildings may be reused when their physical arrangement can
support the new use. No conversion simply because a player clicked a button.
Conversion Feasibility report
Show strengths, weaknesses and required work rather than only Valid/Invalid.
Example residence -> General Store:

strong frontage
adequate customer space
weak rear receiving
limited storage
storefront/shelving/counter modifications required

8. Deal discovery
KEEP public listings, private approaches, introductions, rumors/leads, estate situations, debt pressure, retirement, relocation,
distress and bank-held property.
Property markets are not perfect universal listing databases.





                                           REVISION XVII INTEGRATION 20

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 177/346 ====================

                         LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XVII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE

9. Negotiation
KEEP exchange-based negotiation. A seller can trade price against closing certainty, cash, financing, contingencies, earnest
money, transition, equipment inclusion and other terms. No generic Negotiation Skill discount.

10. Deal structure
KEEP headline price separate from full transaction terms:
cash at closing
financed portion
seller-carried balance
earnest money
closing date
exclusivity
contingencies
included/excluded property
inventory/equipment
tenant/account treatment
transition assistance

11. Diligence
KEEP issue-specific diligence instead of one percentage meter. Diligence can answer title, books, physical condition,
employee retention, supplier continuity, tax status and market sustainability questions. Closing with unresolved issues
remains possible.

12. Property encumbrance burden
Deepen diligence to include, where applicable:
title/ownership
mortgages/security interests
taxes due/delinquent
special assessments
occupants/tenants
leases/use arrangements
access/corridor rights
other claims
survey/boundary uncertainty
included/excluded improvements
New principle:
Closing transfers whatever was actually conveyed, not whatever the buyer assumed existed.

13. Valuation categories
New explicit separation:
Asking Price: seller’s requested terms/price.
Expected Market Value: informed estimate of likely transaction value under current market conditions.
Buyer-Specific Strategic Value: value to a particular buyer because of adjacency, integration or strategy.
Carrying/Book Value: ledger carrying concept.
Distressed/Liquidation Value: expected realizable value under time pressure.
These can diverge substantially.

14. Buyer-specific strategic value
A parcel ordinary buyers value near $300 might be worth $600 to an owner who needs it to combine two adjacent sites. The
seller may infer that value from real circumstances. This is not arbitrary player-targeted price inflation.

15. Land assembly
Elevate land assembly to a first-class strategy. Larger projects may require several parcels or rights. A player can face
holdouts, high prices, rival acquisition, title issues, occupants or access problems.


                                           REVISION XVII INTEGRATION 21

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 178/346 ====================

                         LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XVII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE


Owning most of a site does not authorize construction across land not controlled.

16. Land banking and carrying cost
Land speculation remains valid, but holding land carries real opportunity cost:
capital tied up
taxes
financing cost
maintenance/security where improved
assessments where applicable
forgone investment
There is no automatic fixed annual appreciation.

17. Geography-driven revaluation
Infrastructure changes land value through actual spatial effects. Rail/depot development changes traffic, freight, clustering,
housing and road patterns rather than applying a universal percentage increase to all land.

18. Capacity vs authorization
Hard lock:
Physical Development Capacity: what the site could plausibly support.
Authorized Projects: what an owner has actually approved.
Work in Progress: what is physically being built.
Never collapse these.

19. Project Authorization
A major project authorization may define:
scope
site
budget authority
funding route
sourcing policy
contractor/internal work policy
quality/specification target
schedule/priority
owner-reserved decisions
acceptable contingency/overrun range
After authorization, routine continuation should proceed automatically until genuine exceptions need escalation.

20. Project execution
KEEP staged physical project logic. Stages/dependencies vary by project rather than using one immutable universal stage
list. Possible work includes site work, foundation/masonry, framing, enclosure, roofing, openings, interior work, finish and final
preparation.
Overall completion percentage can exist only as a summary. Work-package state remains authoritative.

21. Project Stockpiles
KEEP. Materials allocated to a project cannot simultaneously be ordinary sale inventory. Prebuying protects against
shortages but ties capital and creates storage, theft, fire, weather and deterioration exposure.

22. Direct-to-project production
KEEP. Owned producers can manufacture directly against project requirements without fictional intermediate retail steps.
Real logs/materials, labor, machinery, freight, loading/unloading, ledger attribution and opportunity cost remain.

23. Construction project financial reporting
New four-number framework:
Estimated Cost: original/updated estimate.
Committed Cost: orders/contracts already entered into.



                                           REVISION XVII INTEGRATION 22

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 179/346 ====================

                         LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XVII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE


Spent to Date: money/resources already paid or consumed.
Forecast Cost to Complete / Forecast Final Cost: best current estimate based on known remaining burden.
Forecasts use ranges where records or estimates do not support exact precision.

24. Estimating remains uncertain
Estimating skill improves information about material quantities, freight, labor duration, difficult site work, specialists, weather
and rework. It does not directly make work cheaper.

25. Scope changes / Change Orders
Major new work or discovered conditions should create revised scope, additional authorization or changed forecast. Projects
do not silently absorb unlimited new work under the original approval.
Possible responses include:

maintain scope and accept higher cost
reduce scope
change design
pause
cancel

26. Project failure persists
A project can become paused, underfunded, abandoned, partially complete, damaged, disputed or foreclosed with the
property.
New lock:

Cancellation/failure does not reset the site or generate a magical refund.
Unfinished work, materials, salvage and deterioration remain in the world.

27. Construction quality becomes property history
Defects or weak construction can create hidden or known roof, structural, drainage, heating or other issues later. Project
history remains part of Building/Asset history and can affect future diligence.

28. Condition vs Presentation
KEEP separate:
Condition: structural/mechanical/weatherproofing/reliability state.
Presentation: cleanliness, paint, frontage, visible care and appearance.
A building can be attractive but unsafe or ugly but mechanically sound.

29. Maintenance vs improvement
Distinguish:
maintenance/repair: preserve or restore existing function
refurbishment: improve condition/presentation
expansion: add capacity
conversion: change use
new construction: create new physical capability

30. Construction & Contracting business
KEEP full business archetype based on people, tools, working capital, suppliers, subcontractors and reputation. Scale
emerges organically; no Contractor Level gates.

31. Contractor backlog
KEEP: backlog is not revenue. Awarded work still needs labor, material, time, equipment, working capital and supervision.
Overbooking can create delays, losses and reputation damage.

32. Development speculation
KEEP. Residential/commercial development responds to expected demand with construction delay and uncertainty.
Completion does not guarantee occupancy.

33. Development Feasibility report
A serious project can evaluate:


                                           REVISION XVII INTEGRATION 23

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 180/346 ====================

                         LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XVII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE


Site
owned/control status, suitability, grading/site work, access, capacity.
Project
materials, labor, contractor availability, duration.
Finance
cash requirement, funding plan, carrying burden.
Market
expected rent/revenue, current vacancy, known competing projects, household/business pressure.
Risks
estimate confidence, unresolved site/supply/labor/timing issues.
Use Unknown/ranges rather than fabricated ROI precision.

34. Vacant land carries economic state
Unimproved land still ties capital, incurs tax/financing/assessment burdens and may provide yard, storage, access, expansion
or strategic control.

35. Property disposition
Add a real selling lifecycle mirroring acquisition:
Owner decides to sell -> property prepared/information assembled -> potential buyers become aware -> offers ->
negotiation -> buyer diligence -> financing/title conditions -> closing.

Do not use a formulaic instant Sell button for serious property.

36. NPC property parity
NPCs can hold, refuse to sell, speculate, develop, rent, convert, sell, become distressed, assemble sites and compete for
property under the same rules.

37. Canon locks from Audit 04
Ownership is not universal use permission.
Parcel is not Building.
Building is not Occupancy.
Suitability is use-specific.
Asking Price is not Value.
Market Value is not Buyer-Specific Strategic Value.
Development Capacity is not Project Authorization.
Project Authorization is not Completion.
Project Estimate is not Final Cost.
Materials are consumed when work occurs.
Internal supply is not free.
Partial construction persists.
Construction quality persists into property history.
Property markets move through real geography.
Disposition requires a counterparty.
Audit 04 Canon status: LOCKED.

SYSTEM AUDIT 05 - SUPPLY / AGREEMENTS / LOGISTICS / TRANSPORT
Final verdict: KEEP + DEEPEN.
The Canon already separates standing agreements from physical shipments, prevents global inventory teleportation, uses
composite transport capacity, supports multi-leg and multi-stop routes, and now correctly distinguishes Livery from
Freight/Hauling while allowing combined businesses. The key need is one universal Logistics Execution grammar and explicit
ownership-versus-custody authority.

1. System purpose
The system answers:


                                           REVISION XVII INTEGRATION 24

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 181/346 ====================

                         LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XVII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE


What needs to move, why is it moving, who owns it, who promised to move it, what capacity is actually available, what route
will it use, what happens while it travels and when is the commercial obligation truly fulfilled?

2. Universal logistics loop
Need / Demand -> Supplier / carrier identified -> Terms agreed -> Goods/capacity committed -> Source inventory
available -> Shipment Order -> Transport capacity assembled -> Loading -> Departure -> Travel Leg ->
Transfer/Intermediate Stop -> Additional Leg(s) -> Arrival -> Unloading / Receiving -> Inventory ownership/location
update -> Commercial settlement -> Performance/relationship history.

3. Agreement vs Shipment
KEEP hard separation.
A standing agreement describes an ongoing commercial relationship. Each actual delivery is a separate physical Shipment.
An agreement can remain active while individual shipments succeed, partially fill, miss, delay or fail.

4. Agreement hierarchy
Expand commercial commitment types conceptually:
Spot Order
Recurring Supply Agreement
Requirements Agreement
Allocation/Percentage Agreement
Reserved Supply
Freight Contract
Preferred Carrier / Preferred Supplier
Project Supply Commitment
These structures differ because commitments differ, not because the game needs separate incompatible systems.

5. Inventory reserve and availability
For transport-relevant goods:
On Hand - Protected Reserve - Already Committed - Unavailable/Condition Restricted = Available to Allocate.

Priority and reserve rules remain real management policy.

6. Fulfillment Priority policy
When promises collide, managers may prioritize based on:
contract priority
internal strategic priority
due date
customer importance
margin
breach consequence
perishability
owner lock
There is no hidden universal maximize-profit rule.

7. Internal ownership does not automatically win
Owned businesses are not automatically entitled to every internal input before outside contracts. External contract
economics, breach costs, opportunity value and strategic policy matter.

8. Shipment as persistent authority
A Shipment can conceptually know:
source
destination
cargo
quantity
owner
originating agreement/order


                                           REVISION XVII INTEGRATION 25

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 182/346 ====================

                         LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XVII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE


carrier
current custodian
assigned vehicle/team
assigned labor
route/legs
current location/progress
loading state
departure
ETA/expected arrival
actual arrival
delay/failure state
freight charges
cargo condition where relevant
Shipments persist even when no related scene is loaded.

9. Ownership vs custody
New hard doctrine:
Possession, custody and ownership are separate economic facts.
A carrier may have custody of customer-owned goods. A warehouse/elevator may physically hold goods owned by someone
else. Repair providers can hold customer property. Physical control does not automatically transfer ownership.

10. Ownership transfer timing
Physical location change does not automatically imply legal ownership change. Ownership may transfer at purchase, loading,
delivery, acceptance or another agreed point according to historically appropriate terms.
Architecture must permit this variation even where exact legal calibration remains future research.

11. Loading/unloading are work
Transport does not begin or end instantaneously. Loading and unloading consume compatible labor, time, space, equipment
and access. Receiving businesses can become bottlenecks.

12. Receiving capacity
A destination may be economically willing to buy but physically unable to receive because storage is full, loading space is
blocked, workers are unavailable, arrival is outside usable hours or special handling is missing.

13. Transport capacity is composite
Usable trip capacity emerges from compatible:
vehicle
draft power
harness/equipment
driver/teamster
cargo compatibility
route feasibility
time
condition
Do not store a magical wagon-count logistics capacity.

14. Available Transport Capacity report
Player-facing report can explain owned vs ready vs in-use vs under-repair assets rather than one abstract number.

15. Operational assignment vs asset ownership
KEEP. A wagon/team can be legally owned by one ledger and operationally assigned elsewhere under authorized portfolio
policy. Asset condition, financing and ownership history remain attached to the owning ledger.





                                           REVISION XVII INTEGRATION 26

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 183/346 ====================

                         LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XVII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE

16. Transport cost attribution
When one controlled business’s transport asset serves another business, distinguish legal owner/payroll/maintenance burden
from economic consumer of the service. Internal reimbursement/transfer pricing may vary but consolidated economics remain
truthful.

17. Dispatch is policy-driven
Routine wagon dispatch should normally be handled by managers under standing policy. Player attention belongs to:
commitment conflicts
major delay
rush job
capacity shortage
repeated empty mileage
expansion request
route failure
breach risk
No requirement to manually route every ordinary shipment.

18. Route vs Shipment
New lock:
A Route is a reusable operating plan. A Shipment is actual cargo movement.
The same Monday route can carry different cargo each week.

19. Multi-stop routes / through-cargo / backhauls
KEEP. Routes can carry through-cargo, reserve capacity for later pickups, wait conditionally and use spare capacity for
eligible cargo.

20. Empty mileage
Elevate empty mileage as a central freight economic. Full outbound utilization can still produce weak economics if return
travel is unpaid. Lower-margin return cargo can be valuable because it converts otherwise empty mileage into paid work.

21. Utilization is diagnostic, not objective
KEEP. 100% utilization can still lose money; 60% utilization can be highly profitable. Reports should show loaded/empty
mileage, revenue, feed, labor, maintenance, delays, rejected work and margin.

22. Rush work
KEEP rush freight as real priority displacement. Rush premiums compensate for scarce capacity, schedule disruption and
urgency; they are not arbitrary modifiers.

23. Freight pricing
Ground quotes in:
distance
road/terrain
load/cargo
team requirements
return opportunity
urgency
loading/unloading burden
expected delays
current capacity
relationship
risk
Do not reduce all freight to distance x constant.

24. Minimum-charge/service-zone policies
KEEP legitimate carrier policies such as minimum service charge, minimum load, service zone, target margin and rush
premium. These are business policies, not designer restrictions.


                                           REVISION XVII INTEGRATION 27

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 184/346 ====================

                         LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XVII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE

25. Livery vs Freight/Hauling
New Revision XVIII lock preserving Research Item 6:
Livery core
stabling
feeding
horse/team/rig hire
possible drivers
possible sales
possible passenger/hack/bus work
Freight/Hauling core
customer cargo movement
route/contracts/loading/utilization/backhauls/teams/drivers/feed/wagon condition/scheduling
Drayage/Cartage
legitimate short/local hauling specialization, especially depot/warehouse/local transfer
Combined operations
Livery & Freight
Livery with Dray Line
Livery, Feed & Sale Stable
other evidence-supported combinations
Shared assets create coordination, not an abstract synergy bonus.

26. Feed links transport to agriculture
Transport animals consume real hay/oats/bran/feed/water. Feed shortages can raise transport costs, tighten margins, raise
freight rates, increase landed cost and affect local prices through actual resource chains.

27. Draft-animal work/recovery
Animals are not infinitely reusable motive power. Work creates fatigue, feed/water needs, injury exposure and recovery
requirements. This shares causal philosophy with human fatigue but remains a biological system.

28. Roads are infrastructure
KEEP route effects from grade, surface, drainage, bridges, crossings, weather, feed/water/stopping infrastructure. Physical
improvement changes travel economics rather than granting abstract freight bonuses.

29. Complete closure can occur
Some weather/route states should make travel practically impossible rather than merely applying speed penalties.

30. Seasonal stockpiling
Deepen working-capital/logistics interaction. Businesses may stockpile before unreliable seasons, trading resilience against
tied capital, storage burden, spoilage, fire and theft risk.

31. Logistics information and ETA
New lock:
Departure/arrival facts are facts; ETA is a forecast.
ETA confidence depends on route, weather, communication, carrier and last known information. Telegraph/telephone/rail
systems can improve information speed but do not create omniscience.

32. Exception-based logistics alerts
Surface missed departure, partial fill, blocked route, receiving constraint, team shortage, repeated empty returns,
deteriorating carrier reliability and repeatedly rejected profitable work. Do not notify every routine movement.

33. Supplier evaluation
KEEP price, freight, lead time, reliability, quality and volume limit. Add supplier flexibility dimensions such as:
minimum order
credit willingness
rush capacity



                                           REVISION XVII INTEGRATION 28

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 185/346 ====================

                         LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XVII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE


seasonal capacity
reserve-stock willingness
recurring terms
transport responsibility

34. Supplier relationship memory
Repeated successful/failed business can affect trust, reserved stock, credit, shortage priority and knowledge of requirements
through real relationship history rather than a generic Supplier Level.

35. Partial fulfillment
Agreements can result in partial shipment, accepted short delivery, backup sourcing, delay or priority allocation. Do not
reduce every shortage to Agreement Failed.

36. Backup suppliers
Maintaining a secondary supplier can trade slightly worse ordinary economics for resilience. This is a real relationship and
may have weaker terms or low use, not a free resilience stat.

37. Contracted capacity is not completed capacity
Freight companies can overbook. Contracts do not create wagons, teams or drivers. Excess commitments can lead to
failures, lost reputation, expansion requests or contract loss.

38. Overbooking remains allowed
Do not hard-block a player from accepting work simply because current capacity looks insufficient if they could add assets,
hire, subcontract or reorganize before performance is due. Consequences determine whether the choice was smart.

39. Subcontract freight
A primary carrier can subcontract excess work where appropriate, retaining customer obligation and some margin while
giving up control/profit.

40. Rail integration
KEEP depot as transfer machine, not teleport portal. Rail still requires receipt, unloading, documentation, storage and local
drayage/final delivery. Local terminal/platform/storage capacity can bottleneck traffic.
Rail transforms wagon routes rather than deleting the wagon economy:

distant railhead long haul
nearer railhead
local depot
final-mile/drayage/feeder specialization

41. Intermodal journeys
Support multi-leg chains such as supplier -> rail -> railhead -> wagon freight -> warehouse -> local dray -> customer. Each
leg can have different carrier, cost, delay and custody.

42. Storage is part of logistics
Warehousing buffers timing mismatch between arrival and consumption/onward shipment. Storage creates cost, capacity,
damage/fire/theft exposure and handling burden.

43. Pipeline inventory
Add explicit Inventory in Transit state. Distinguish:
on hand
reserved
inbound
outbound/in transit
unavailable
customer-owned/custody
Inbound stock cannot satisfy immediate local demand until physically received.

44. Opportunity & Pressure integration
Repeated logistics failures can create freight opportunity, carrier expansion pressure, depot drayage gaps, remote-camp
supply pressure or excess-carrier distress through actual evidence.

45. Canon locks from Audit 05
Agreement is not Shipment.
Shipment is not Route.
Possession is not Ownership.

SYSTEM AUDIT 06 - CONDITION / MAINTENANCE / REPAIR / FAILURE
Final verdict: KEEP + DEEPEN, with strong anti-micromanagement protection.
This is one of the strongest completed systems in the Canon. It already separates actual condition from known condition,
makes inspection an information action, allows deferred maintenance, requires physical maintenance work and uses causal
failure chains. The main addition is a separate Operating State and one universal Work Order lifecycle.

1. System purpose
The system answers:
What physical state is this asset in, what do we know, what work does it need, can we continue using it, what are we risking if
we do, and when does repair stop making sense compared with overhaul or replacement?

2. Universal asset lifecycle
Asset exists -> Use/exposure -> Component wear/damage -> Underlying condition changes -> Symptoms may
appear -> Worker/operator notices -> Inspection/diagnosis -> Defect becomes known -> Operating response ->
Continue/restrict/shut down -> Service/repair authorized -> Parts/labor/facility assembled -> Work -> Repair quality
verified -> Return to service -> History persists -> Maintain again / overhaul / replace / sell / salvage.

3. Condition domains
KEEP economically meaningful component groups, not one Health number and not microscopic part simulation.
Examples:

Wagon
wheels/running gear
axle/bearings
frame/body
harness
Steam sawmill
boiler/pressure system
engine/mechanical state
drive system
saw/cutting system
building/support condition




                                           REVISION XVII INTEGRATION 30

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 187/346 ====================

                         LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XVII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE

4. Condition vs Defect
New explicit lock:
Condition describes broader accumulated physical state. Defect describes a specific problem.
An asset can be worn without a particular acute defect, or otherwise good while suffering one serious sudden defect.

5. Operating State
Add a separate authoritative Operating State such as:
Available
Available with restriction
Monitoring
Scheduled maintenance
Out of service - planned
Out of service - failed
Temporary service
Retired/stored
Salvage/disposal
Condition, defect and operating state are separate facts.

6. Restricted operation
A damaged asset can remain usable under grounded limits such as reduced load, reduced pressure, reduced throughput or
restricted space occupancy. This creates real Continue / Restrict / Stop decisions.

7. Wear causality
KEEP wear from operating time, workload, load, terrain, heat, vibration, lubrication, material characteristics, storage, weather,
moisture, corrosion and other asset-specific exposure.
Idle assets avoid use wear but can still deteriorate environmentally.

8. Protection remains physical
Shelter, drainage, lubrication, road quality and other protective conditions affect physical exposure rather than giving abstract
lifespan bonuses.

9. Construction quality connection
Newly constructed assets are not automatically physically perfect. Weak construction can create known or latent defects that
enter asset history and may be discovered later.

10. Actual vs Known condition
KEEP as an A+ information system. The simulation knows reality; businesses know only what operation, inspection, repair,
records and observation reveal. Inspection knowledge becomes stale as additional use/exposure accumulates.

11. Inspection is not a health-bar reveal
Inspection should produce evidence and diagnosis such as wear, looseness, cracks, leaks, vibration, unsafe conditions or
recommended operating limits. Avoid magical exact failure percentages unless genuinely measurable.

12. Inspector capability
Different people notice different things. Ordinary operators may observe symptoms; specialists may identify causes and
repair scope. Better capability improves information, not physical condition.

13. Symptom vs diagnosis
New lock:
Observed symptom is not automatically the diagnosed defect.
Example: vibration may result from mounting, bearing, alignment or drive damage. Diagnosis is a separate information step.

14. Work Order authority
Add universal Work Order for repair/service. A Work Order can identify:
target asset/component
reported symptom
known/diagnosed defect


                                           REVISION XVII INTEGRATION 31

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 188/346 ====================

                         LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XVII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE


requested work
urgency
required capability
parts/material
location
assigned provider
estimated labor/time
quote/agreed price
operational restriction
status
completion
verification
payment
Use the same shared lifecycle for blacksmith work, wagon repair, building maintenance, machinery service and later rail/utility
maintenance.

15. Maintenance Backlog
Backlog is a set of real outstanding work, not a score. Reports should show actual service/repair needs, next actions,
skills/parts, downtime and status.

16. Backlog Age / Criticality
Recognized maintenance needs should consider:
severity
urgency
contextual criticality
consequence of delay
downtime opportunity cost
parts/provider availability

17. Asset Criticality
New lock:
Criticality is contextual, not inherent. It depends on what relies on the asset and what alternatives/redundancy exist.
The only mine pump is more critical than one of four redundant pumps even if physical condition is identical.

18. Dependency chains
Failure changes physical capability; dependent systems then react. A sawmill drive failure can affect lumber throughput,
customer orders, log accumulation, freight and construction without one universal failure penalty.

19. Maintenance policy
KEEP standing policies for spending limits, reserve protection, approval thresholds, shutdown rules, inspection cadence and
spare-parts targets. Player may deliberately defer maintenance.

20. Maintenance Stance
A convenient player-facing stance such as Conservative / Balanced / Run Hard may bundle real policies underneath but must
never create magic bonuses. Players may inspect/override the underlying policies.

21. Deferred maintenance is a real gamble
Cash-poor businesses can rationally postpone work. The consequence is unresolved physical state and increased exposure
where causally justified, not an arbitrary Neglect penalty.

22. Boom maintenance debt
Boom periods can create physical maintenance debt because equipment is run hard and downtime is scarce. Recessions
can provide time but little cash. This tension should emerge naturally.

23. Routine service consumables
Track economically meaningful lubricants, belts, timber, roofing material, packing, protective material or other consumables
where shortages/sourcing matter. Do not simulate trivial maintenance clutter.


                                           REVISION XVII INTEGRATION 32

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 189/346 ====================

                         LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XVII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE

24. Spare parts
KEEP resilience trade-off. Stocking parts ties cash and storage but can prevent long downtime. No universal Spare Parts
inventory that repairs any machine.

25. Cannibalization
Allow compatible failed assets to donate usable parts where physically plausible. Donor asset loses corresponding
rebuild/salvage potential.
This may be a later implementation priority but is Canon-valid.

26. Redundancy
KEEP separate from spare parts. Backup installed/usable assets can preserve operation but require capital, storage, upkeep
and may sit idle.
Backup capacity may be partial rather than identical.

27. Downtime
Treat downtime as real economic cost alongside parts/labor:
lost production
missed freight
delayed contract
displaced worker time
lost rent/occupancy
hired substitute equipment
emergency costs

28. Repair Decision report
Serious repair decisions may show:
known issue
operating state/restriction
repair estimate
expected downtime
parts/provider availability
consequence of delay
business commitments currently exposed

29. Seasonal maintenance
Schedule maintenance around actual economic/seasonal windows such as harvest, winter hauling, roofing, mine pumping,
lodging occupancy or traffic cycles. Timing matters because downtime opportunity cost changes.

30. Maintenance labor is real
Maintenance consumes finite labor time. It does not happen for free at night unless people actually perform it and scheduling
permits.

31. Proper vs Temporary/Improvised repair
Keep distinct:
Proper repair: addressed defect restored to expected service.
Temporary repair: limited/restricted service restored pending proper work.
Improvised repair: available materials/capability restore some function with limitations/follow-up need.
Temporary repair cannot become a permanent cheap exploit.

32. Repair quality
Repair work can be excellent, adequate, weak or incomplete according to actual capability/materials/supervision. Customer
may not know immediately. Later use can reveal problems.

33. Verification
Work Completed and Defect Confirmed Resolved do not always have to be identical information events. Critical work can
require test/inspection/operational verification.



                                           REVISION XVII INTEGRATION 33

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 190/346 ====================

                         LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XVII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE

34. Component replacement
Replacing one component does not reset the whole asset. The component receives new history/state while other systems
retain their age/condition.

35. Overhaul
Overhaul is a bundle of substantial real work on specified systems, not Set Condition = 90%. Different overhaul scopes are
possible and recorded.

36. Repair vs Overhaul vs Replace vs Sell vs Salvage
Late-game capital decisions should compare:
repair
overhaul
replacement
sale as-is
salvage
based on cost, downtime, remaining service, throughput needs, financing, input efficiency, parts, market outlook and
resale/salvage.

37. Replacement is not a tech-tier mandate
Newer equipment is not automatically economically superior. Old equipment may remain rational to repair; newer equipment
may be rational to buy early depending on actual economics.

38. Remaining service life is a forecast
Do not expose deterministic timers. Experts may estimate likely service horizon based on condition, history, workload and
inspection, but future failure remains uncertain.

39. Failure causality
KEEP. Failure exposure comes from design, condition, unresolved defects, load, environment and operating practice.
Probability primarily resolves timing among already plausible stressed outcomes rather than generating random healthy-asset
explosions.

40. Failure categories
Distinguish:
wear-driven failure
defect-driven failure
accident damage
catastrophic destruction
A new asset can still be destroyed by accident without violating the Condition system.

41. Secondary damage
New explicit rule:
Deferred or continued operation with a defect can cause additional physical damage where causally appropriate.
Examples: loose wheel -> hub/axle damage; leak -> moisture/structural damage; overheating bearing -> shaft damage;
chimney defect -> fire.
No universal monthly maintenance-cost escalator is required.

42. Defects do not all worsen identically
Some remain stable; some worsen only under heavy load, moisture, heat, freeze/thaw or continued use. Avoid deterministic
countdown behavior.

43. Catastrophic failure remains rare but meaningful
Routine wear should more often create repair burden/downtime than catastrophe. Serious failure requires credible physical
conditions. Maintenance is risk management, not tribute to RNG.

44. Safety-critical governance
Businesses can set safety shutdown policies and manager discretion rules where physically/legal appropriate. Player
override cannot make impossible operation physically possible.




                                           REVISION XVII INTEGRATION 34

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 191/346 ====================

                         LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XVII / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE

45. No universal Safety score
Safety exposure emerges from actual defects, affected systems, people exposed and operating conditions.

46. Fire integration
Maintenance defects can become fire-system precursors such as cracked stovepipe, damaged chimney, overheating
bearing, boiler problem or later electrical fault. No generic Poor Maintenance fire modifier.

47. Buildings
Building condition can include structure, roof/weatherproofing, chimney/heating, loading platforms and specialized systems.
Buildings simply use different time scales from machinery.

48. Condition vs Presentation
KEEP separate. Cosmetic improvement does not repair structural problems. Structural maintenance does not automatically
improve appearance.

49. Animals are not machine assets
Hard boundary lock:
Living animals use biological health/fatigue/nutrition/injury/age/recovery authority, not machinery durability.
The systems can interact but must not collapse.

50. Used equipment markets
KEEP uncertain used-asset condition, inspection, refurbishment, operation, resale and salvage. Cheap used equipment can
be a bargain or deferred-maintenance trap.

51. Maintenance records and diligence
Service/overhaul records are evidence, not guarantees. Poor or misleading records can coexist with actual condition.
Diligence combines records with inspection.

52. Condition and value
Condition affects acquisition/collateral/resale through actual repair cost, productive capability, downtime, replacement scarcity
and salvage, not a universal Poor Condition percentage.

53. Failed equipment persists
Failed assets remain physical objects that can be repaired, stored, sold, parted out, scrapped, abandoned or used as limited
backup.

54. Maintenance-service market
Growth of wagon, machinery, rail or utility assets creates real repair/service demand and can support blacksmiths,
mechanics, machinists or internal maintenance departments.

55. Specialist bottlenecks
Parts and money may exist while no qualified local provider is available. Options include wait, import specialist, send
component away, improvise temporary repair, train staff or replace equipment.

56. Internal maintenance scaling
A portfolio may rationally establish internal repair staff/shop only when actual workload supports it. Centralized maintenance
does not merge asset ownership.

57. Manager capital requests
Maintenance systems can generate grounded requests for backup assets, overhauls, spare parts, staffing or facility
investment based on actual downtime and rejected work.

58. Information doctrine
Reports distinguish known facts from forecasts:
known defect
repair quote
current unavailable state
versus
expected completion
likely progression if delayed
