false positives are valid outcomes. External delinquency can sometimes be the first evidence that a manager made an error,
diverted money or allowed cash to run short.

13. PROPERTY INVESTMENT & SMALL MULTI-HOUSEHOLD
DEVELOPMENT

13.1 Investment-analysis reporting

Where records and forecasts support it, property/project reports can show invested capital, rental income, avoided rent,
maintenance, vacancy, taxes, financing burden, simple payback, cash-on-cash style return and estimated market value.
Operational benefit and direct rental income remain separate. If evidence is insufficient, the report should say Unknown or
present a justified range rather than inventing a precise payoff period.

13.2 Double House / Two-Family House

Revision XVI supports a purpose-built two-household rental form under historically appropriate terminology such as Double
House or Two-Family House. A modern player-facing synonym such as duplex may be used if helpful, but the Canon should
not imply that the modern term or form was universal.

The mechanic supports two independent households in one structure with more privacy than boarding and some shared
structural/land economy. Direct South Dakota evidence is strongest by 1900, so this form should not be assumed as a common
spring-1880 opening-town archetype. Frequency can rise later or where authored evidence supports it.

The physical hierarchy should remain explicit: one Parcel may contain one shared Building with two Residential Units, each with
its own Occupancy relationship and potentially a different Household. The building form does not determine whether the
occupants are kin, owner plus tenant or two unrelated tenant households.

Two independent residential units do not automatically create two separately saleable deeds. The safe ordinary model is one
property/building containing two economic occupancy units unless a different title arrangement actually exists. The archetype
also does not imply poverty or luxury: quality comes from size, materials, finish, utilities, condition, location and maintenance.

Any land or construction economy arises from the actual shared structure and parcel geometry rather than a fixed Duplex ROI
or Construction Cost bonus. Exact rents, construction cost, vacancy and yield remain market/calibration data.

13.3 Staged tract development

A player may buy land capable of several future dwellings and develop it incrementally. Land acquisition and project
authorization are separate decisions. Ownership of a tract does not automatically begin every building the land might eventually
support.

14. OPPORTUNITY & PRESSURE, NPC ENTRY & PROCEDURAL NAMING

14.1 Unmet demand is not reserved for the player

When a business or service gap exists, an NPC may enter if they can plausibly assemble enough skill, knowledge,
capital/finance, property, suppliers, labor and confidence. Rival entry should not spawn solely because a hidden shortage meter
crossed a threshold. The same feasibility tests that constrain the player should constrain the NPC.

14.2 Rival intent can become information

Investigation can reveal evidence that another actor is already considering entry: a lot inquiry, lender conversation, supplier
approach, equipment purchase or recruiting effort. That creates urgency through the world rather than through an arbitrary
countdown timer.

14.3 Service and institutional gaps

Opportunity & Pressure should evaluate service and institutional gaps as well as commodity production: financial services,
printing/news, medicine/pharmacy, barber/bath, fuel supply and other historically supported services can become opportunities
when actual households and businesses create demand.

14.4 Procedural settlement names

Open Frontier settlements should normally receive generated names from curated region/period-appropriate structures rather
than gibberish syllables. Multiple grammatical forms may be used, but component pools must be structurally compatible. The
                                            REVISION XVI INTEGRATION 10

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 219/346 ====================

                          LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XVI / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE
generator should filter nearby duplicates, absurd combinations and unintended inappropriate outputs. The player may keep or
override the generated name where setup permits; authored scenarios may retain fixed names. Exact one/two/three-word
weighting remains tuning.

15. BUSINESS-FORM RESEARCH HOLDS - NOT YET SUPERSEDED

15.1 Feed & Grain classification remains under research

The playtest demonstrated that feed-and-grain commerce can matter as a distinct commercial opportunity, but Revision XVI
does not yet impose a new business classification. Research Item 6 will determine how often feed dealers, grain dealers,
warehouses, agricultural-supply merchants, mills and broader General Stores overlapped in Dakota/Black Hills settlements.
Until that pass is complete, existing Revision XV agricultural-supply and merchant authority remains in force.

15.2 Livery versus Freight classification remains under research

The playtest demonstrated that livery/stabling and freight/cartage can plausibly be operated separately or together, but the
historical prevalence and exact business-form boundary has not yet been researched in this checkpoint. Research Item 6 must
resolve that question before Revision XVI creates a new classification rule. Existing Revision XV Livery / Freight authority
remains unchanged in the meantime.

15.3 Whole-animal butcher economics is reaffirmed

The existing butcher system is reaffirmed: profitability depends on monetizing the animal across desirable cuts, lower-value
cuts, preservable product and supported byproducts such as hides or tallow while managing spoilage and true waste. Do not
evaluate livestock purchases as though every pound becomes the highest-value retail cut.

16. PRIVATE BANKING, STATE-BANK GOVERNANCE & FINANCIAL
SERVICES

16.1 Private Banking House as an earlier/smaller institutional form

Historical research strongly supports private banking houses in Dakota and South Dakota. The game should not require
national-bank-scale capitalization merely to begin legitimate local deposit/lending services. Institution type is a strategic/legal
choice, not a cosmetic upgrade ladder.

A private banking house can have a much lower formal statutory entry barrier than an incorporated state bank, but that does not
make it economically easy. The owner still needs actual capital/liquidity, records, staff, premises, depositor confidence, lending
opportunities and outside relationships. Private ownership can also expose the proprietor more directly to failure and can be
subject to a different supervision regime.

Paid-in bank capital must represent real qualifying contributed value. An owner cannot capitalize the institution by writing a
personal IOU to the bank and then treating that IOU as cash or paid capital. Exact practical capitalization for a private house
remains balance-sensitive even when no national-bank-scale statutory minimum applies.

16.2 Banking regulation changes during the campaign

The legal environment is not static. Dakota Territory recognized and regulated banking houses during the territorial era, South
Dakota created a formal state-bank framework in 1891, and the 1892 Scougal decision confirmed that private bankers were not
simply forced out of existence by the new corporate form. National banks continued under a separate federal regime. The bank
system should therefore query dated institutional authority rather than apply one timeless set of requirements to 1880 through
1905.

16.3 Incorporated state-bank requirements after 1891

For the South Dakota state-bank form, the 1891 regime supplies concrete later-campaign anchors including minimum paid
capital varying with town scale, reserve requirements, examination/reporting, a single-borrower concentration limit and a
prohibition on insolvent banks continuing to receive deposits. Exact thresholds belong to the applicable dated institution type
and should not be generalized backward to every private banking house.

Private banking did not simply disappear when the state-charter regime arrived; private banking houses and chartered banks
can coexist as different institutional forms. State-bank shareholders and national-bank shareholders can also face period-
specific liability beyond the amount initially invested, making bank ownership potentially more dangerous than a modern limited-
liability assumption.

                                            REVISION XVI INTEGRATION 11

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 220/346 ====================

                          LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XVI / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE
National banking is a separate federal form rather than Bank Level 3. In small towns the period national-bank framework
required capitalization on the order of $50,000, far above a small private banking house, along with federal supervision and
United States-bond/note-circulation requirements. National-bank status should therefore be a major strategic institutional choice
rather than a cosmetic upgrade.

16.4 Bank Ledger and reporting

A banking institution should be capable of producing a period-style balance-sheet view that separates assets such as cash,
correspondent balances, loans, supported bonds/securities, banking premises and other real estate from liabilities/equity such
as deposits, paid capital, surplus/profits and other obligations. Cash reconciliation remains especially important because
recorded books and actual cash can diverge through error or fraud.

Chartered-bank rules can require minimum reserves, qualifying correspondent balances, concentration limits and transfers of
earnings into surplus. Profit is therefore not automatically distributable owner cash. Solvency and liquidity remain separate: an
institution can have valuable assets but insufficient immediately available money, or have cash on hand while losses have
impaired its capital.

Knowingly insolvent banking institutions must not be allowed to continue accepting deposits indefinitely merely to postpone
failure. Dated law and institutional form determine when deposit-taking authority, examination or closure consequences change.

16.5 Related-party lending

A bank loan to the owner or another controlled business remains a real loan. The connected relationship is identified.
Underwriting, liquidity, concentration and solvency constraints still apply. Favorable terms may be possible when lawful, but
administrative cost, credit risk, opportunity cost and liquidity cost do not disappear because both businesses share an owner. A
delegated bank manager can refuse a connected loan that breaches policy or law.

16.6 Supported fee services and correspondents

Period evidence supports banks acting in general banking, collection and loan business; buying/selling exchange; handling
drafts/remittances and collections; providing safe-keeping services; and using outside banking relationships. Correspondent
access therefore supports ordinary settlement, remittance and collection work in addition to panic liquidity. Fee income need not
come only from loan interest.

16.7 Proprietary debt-securities portfolio

Where the institution type permits it, the bank may hold supported debt securities such as government, municipal or other lawful
bonds/evidences of debt. These are a distinct asset class from cash and loans. They can earn income while carrying issuer,
maturity, market-value and liquidation risk. Forced sale under stress can realize losses.

CANON LOCK - NO GENERIC BANK STOCK-TRADING BUSINESS

   National banks did not possess a general power to speculate in corporate stocks.
   The ordinary bank portfolio should therefore be data-driven by institution type and emphasize historically lawful debt
    instruments rather than a generic stocks menu.
    Specific instrument availability remains tied to year, legal form and market access.

16.8 Customer securities intermediation is conditional, not universal

The research does not support giving every ordinary bank a modern retail brokerage desk. Historically appropriate private
bankers, banking-and-investment houses or other financial intermediaries may arrange customer investment transactions
where their legal form, market relationships and dated authority support it. This is an optional institutional capability, not a
default Bank tab.

Whenever a financial intermediary acts for a customer, ownership remains explicit. Owner personal investments, Bank
proprietary investments and Customer-owned/agency securities are three separate property domains and must never be
merged. Specific customer-investment products remain data-driven by institution, year and market access.

16.9 Physical bank security and premises

A bank can legitimately require secure cash/record storage, controlled employee access and period safes or vaults; later and
larger institutions can use more substantial dedicated premises. Brick/stone/fire-resistant construction and prominent premises
may causally affect physical security, fire exposure and public perceptions because customers observe real evidence of
permanence. Do not implement a direct Stone Bank +10 Confidence modifier.

17. TAXATION - DAKOTA TERRITORY TO SOUTH DAKOTA, 1880-1905

17.1 Taxation follows property, jurisdiction and dated law

Land & Ledgers should not import a modern general business-income-tax model backward. The ordinary 1880-1905 tax system
relevant to the player is primarily an annual assessment of legally taxable real and personal property, combined with local
levies, specific licenses or occupation charges where applicable, road obligations, special assessments and dated enforcement
rules. The system should query the owning ledger, asset type, jurisdiction and year rather than applying one empire-wide Tax
Rate.

17.2 Real property and personal/business property are distinct

Real property covers land and improvements/buildings. Period personal-property taxation could also reach economically
important movable or financial property such as livestock, wagons, machinery, merchandise/commercial capital, money, credits
and other supported categories. The game may simplify assessment categories for usability, but it must not reduce the
historical tax base to land alone. A mortgage does not simply reduce the taxable real-property value to the owner's equity.

17.3 Annual assessment and imperfect records

Taxation should have a real annual assessment cycle rather than accruing continuously as a modern percentage skim. Dated
law determines the assessment/listing date and collection schedule. Because assessors could rely on required property
statements and estimates, poor or incomplete records can affect the information and dispute process without turning taxation
into a filing minigame. Actual State, Recorded State and Assessed State can therefore diverge for causal reasons.

17.4 Exemptions and household-scale relief

The broad taxable base coexisted with exemptions. Governmental, educational, religious, charitable and other protected
property can remain outside ordinary taxation where the dated law provides. South Dakota's original constitutional framework
also protected a limited amount of personal property for individuals. The simulation should therefore avoid absurdly taxing every
household possession while ignoring major commercial inventories and equipment.

17.5 Layered public levies without paperwork simulation

Territorial/state, county, municipal, school or other lawful local layers can contribute to a property-tax obligation. There is no
single timeless Dakota Tax Rate. The player-facing Ledger may consolidate the bill while preserving payer, taxable property,
jurisdiction and component for audit/history. Exact millages remain dated data.

17.6 Specific licenses, road obligations and special assessments

Selected businesses and activities can face period-specific municipal licenses or occupation charges, but there is no universal
annual Business License applied to every enterprise. Territorial road obligations can also involve a small money-or-labor civic
burden for eligible persons under the applicable early regime. Public improvements can create separate special assessments
against benefited or abutting property; those assessments are project-linked property obligations rather than another generic
annual tax percentage.

17.7 Delinquency, liens and tax-sale exposure

Tax obligations enter a staged collection process rather than causing instant confiscation. Unpaid taxes can become
delinquent, accrue penalties/interest, create liens, expose personal property to lawful collection and real property to tax sale,
and create redemption/title-history consequences under the dated regime. Tax status therefore belongs in acquisition/property
diligence.

17.8 Statehood changes authority, not the genre of taxation

The 1889 transition from Dakota Territory to South Dakota changes the governing legal authority but does not turn the economy
into a modern income-tax system. Property-based taxation and local levies continue under the new constitutional/statutory
framework. Bank capital and banking property remain within the taxable system subject to the institution-specific rules
researched elsewhere in Revision XVI.





                                            REVISION XVI INTEGRATION 13

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 222/346 ====================

17.9 No general retail sales tax or general South Dakota income tax during the normal
campaign

Ordinary General Store purchases should not receive a modern retail sales-tax line during 1880-1905; South Dakota's general
retail sales tax arrives decades later. Likewise the normal campaign should not impose a generic Business Profit Tax or Owner
Income Tax. Specific period excises, licenses or other lawful charges remain separate dated systems.

17.10 1905 inheritance-tax introduction

South Dakota introduces inheritance taxation in 1905. Because Land & Ledgers already simulates death, estates, succession
and ownership transfer, this can become a late-horizon dated legal event when a taxable succession actually occurs. Exact
rates, exemptions and administration belong to dated legal data rather than a generic wealth tax.

17.11 Tax information in the Lifetime Ledger

The Lifetime Ledger should preserve Taxes Paid by payer and meaningful category, including property tax, supported
licenses/occupation charges, special assessments and inheritance tax where applicable. Exact liability should come from the
dated tax authority rather than from retrospective estimation at the end of the campaign.

18. LIFETIME LEDGER, PORTFOLIO REPORTING & HISTORICAL RECORD

18.1 Persistent Lifetime Ledger

The game should accumulate career statistics from the beginning of the save. The 1905 Historical Record and scenario
completion summaries must not attempt to reconstruct twenty-five years of commerce from whatever balances happen to
remain at the end. The Lifetime Ledger is the persistent historical authority that feeds both in-play reporting and final
retrospectives.

18.2 Headline career statistics

The first layer should prioritize career-defining information rather than trivia. Supported headline categories can include current
Net Worth, peak Net Worth, Liquid Owner Cash, lifetime revenue, lifetime profit, owner capital invested, businesses
founded/acquired/sold/failed, properties acquired/built/sold, employees hired/promoted/lost, payroll paid, principal borrowed,
interest paid, principal lent/originated, interest earned, defaults/losses and taxes paid.

Exact availability depends on what the simulation legitimately tracks and how a metric is defined. A category should not be
printed merely because it sounds interesting if the underlying accounting cannot support it.

18.3 Business-specific lifetime statistics

Each industry can extend the shared historical record with meaningful statistics. A construction company can track bids, wins,
estimate variance, jobs completed and rework. A bank can track deposits, withdrawals, loan originations, interest, credit losses
and lawful securities activity. Freight can track loads, tonnage, distance and rejected work. Hospitality can track
occupancy/lodging nights. A sawmill can track production. Irrelevant categories remain hidden.

18.4 Debt, lending and business chronology

History should preserve flows, not only ending balances. A player who ends debt-free after financing twenty expansions has a
different career from one who never borrowed. Useful history includes peak debt, total principal borrowed, loans repaid,
restructurings/defaults, collateral lost, private loans made, principal recovered and lending losses.

Each business should preserve founding/acquisition date, purchase/founding cost where known, managers, major expansions,
important finance events and sale/closure/disposition. Long-serving people and major projects can become part of the Historical
Record because the underlying career data already exists.

18.5 Filters and hierarchy

The Ledger should allow the same history to be examined at useful scopes such as All Time or a selected year/period, and
Portfolio -> Division -> Business -> Property/Asset/Account where relevant. The exact UI can change, but the data should
support these questions without creating separate incompatible reporting systems.

18.6 Liquid Owner Cash, Book Equity and Net Worth

Player-facing labels must remain unambiguous as the portfolio grows. Liquid Owner Cash means immediately spendable
owner-side cash. Business cash remains on its own ledger. Bank cash belongs to the bank. Book/Ledger Equity is an
                                            REVISION XVI INTEGRATION 14

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 223/346 ====================

                          LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XVI / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE
accounting carrying-value concept; Net Worth remains the Canon's grounded portfolio economic-value metric. Illiquid valuation
can be estimated and should not pretend to false precision.

18.7 Information hierarchy and zero suppression

The main portfolio view should show the most decision-relevant information first and suppress irrelevant zero-value categories.
A one-store owner should not see a permanent wall of zero banking, securities, railway and contingent-liability rows. Detail and
historical screens can still preserve those categories when they become relevant.

18.8 Forecast discipline

Manager capital proposals, construction estimates, property payback, acquisition earnings and lending forecasts all remain
forecasts. Known facts remain exact where legitimately known. Insufficient data can produce Unknown, wide ranges or low
confidence. A sophisticated organization should become better at explaining uncertainty rather than converting estimates into
omniscient truth.

19. RESEARCH-BASED CORRECTIONS TO PLAYTEST PROPOSALS

The following playtest ideas are deliberately modified or parked because the historical research produced a stronger
interpretation.

1.  Customer securities intermediation is not a universal ordinary-bank power. Permit it only for historically appropriate
    banking/investment intermediaries whose legal form, market relationships and dated authority actually support the service.
2.  Bank proprietary investment is narrowed to institution-appropriate debt securities/bonds and other verified instruments. Do
    not create a generic bank stock-speculation menu.
3.   Private-loan early repayment is contract-specific. Do not create a generic loan toggle that automatically preserves all
    unearned future interest after prepayment.
4.  The small two-household rental archetype is canonized as Double House / Two-Family House, with duplex only an optional
    modern synonym. It should not be assumed common at the 1880 opening.
5.  Feed & Grain and Livery/Freight classification remain unresolved at this checkpoint. Research Item 6 must determine the
     historically plausible business forms, overlaps and separations before Revision XVI supersedes Revision XV on those
    boundaries.
6.   Private Banking House is positively confirmed as a valid smaller/earlier banking form; low formal statutory barrier does not
     eliminate the need for economic bankability.
7.   Brothel/prostitution content remains parked. No legal, licensing or tolerance model is Canonized in this checkpoint; if the
     project brings it into active scope, Research Item 7 must establish the territorial/state/local legal and institutional treatment
      first.

20. REMAINING HISTORICAL RESEARCH HOLDS AT THIS CHECKPOINT

Revision XVI is intentionally a checkpoint, not a claim that every playtest question has been researched. The following subjects
remain open and should be researched one at a time before a later superseding revision changes their detailed Canon
treatment.
   Research Item 6 - Feed & Grain and Livery/Freight business classification: determine the historically plausible business
    forms, overlaps and separations in Dakota/Black Hills settlements from 1880-1905.
   Research Item 7 - Brothel/prostitution legal and institutional treatment, only if the project intentionally chooses to bring this
    business/service family into active scope. Research territorial/state law, local ordinance, tolerated versus illegal operation,
     policing, property and economic treatment rather than relying on generic Western-game assumptions.
All other completed research blocks in this checkpoint are incorporated into the sections above. Numerical tuning and
implementation architecture remain separate from historical research.

   Occupation is descriptive context, not a hard character class; human capability is task-derived and transferable.

APPENDIX XVI-B - HISTORICAL RESEARCH BASIS

The Revision XVI research pass used period statutes, appellate decisions, federal/state reports, census instructions/occupation
classifications, local historical surveys and period commercial records to test the playtest assumptions. The Canon records
gameplay-relevant conclusions rather than turning these materials into a citation-heavy legal treatise. High-value anchors
include:
   Dakota and South Dakota banking law/history, including the 1891 state-bank regime, private-bank continuity,
    reserve/concentration requirements and bank reporting.
   United States Comptroller of the Currency annual reports from the 1880s-1890s for Dakota/South Dakota bank balance-
    sheet categories and institutional conditions.
   South Dakota and federal banking sources distinguishing ordinary banking powers, institution-specific securities eligibility,
    correspondent/fee services and the narrower circumstances in which customer investment intermediation is historically
    supportable.
   U.S. Supreme Court national-bank cases from the 1890s limiting general corporate-stock dealing.
   Dakota territorial and South Dakota cases involving promissory notes, mortgage acceleration, foreclosure, renewals and
    secured obligations.
   Dakota mechanic's-lien law and documented 1880s Dakota construction contracts showing contractors, subcontractors,
     material suppliers, bids, extras and progress-linked payment.
   1880 and 1900 U.S. Census occupation instructions/classifications distinguishing actual trades, clerical roles, transport
     roles, livery work, banking work, foremen and helpers.
   Dakota territorial and South Dakota constitutional/statutory material on real and personal property taxation, annual
    assessment, exemptions, local levies, road obligations, special assessments, delinquency/tax sale, statehood continuity
    and the 1905 inheritance-tax introduction.
   South Dakota/Black Hills local historical sources documenting private banks, bank buildings and the later Double House /
    Two-Family House form. Feed & Grain and Livery/Freight classification are deliberately deferred to Research Item 6.

 1.5J Scenario architecture - authored problems, systemic
 solutions
 Scenarios are not arbitrary task lists. Each scenario should begin from a believable commercial situation that explains why
 the opportunity, obligation, pressure or deadline exists. Typical drivers include contracts, tenders, financing terms, creditor
 workouts, seasonal buying windows, land options, construction schedules, railway decisions, government procurement,
 investor patience, seller retirement, settlement promotion and historically fixed events.
 CANON LOCK - The scenario states the result that must be achieved. The shared simulation determines the viable
 methods.

    • Prefer "deliver X qualifying freight by [date]" over "own five wagons."
    • Prefer "produce and sell X recoverable ore by [date]" over "own a mine, sawmill and blacksmith."
    • Prefer "grow and sustain the settlement at X residents by [date]" over direct city-builder construction quotas.
    • Supporting systems should matter because they become real bottlenecks: labor, housing, timber, tools, freight, finance,
    maintenance, processing, supplier reliability and working capital.
    • Vertical integration is an option, not a requirement. A player may own supporting businesses, contract with NPCs, finance
    them or rely on market supply if that is economically viable.
 1.5K Scenario phases, counterparties and failure
 Substantial scenarios should usually evolve through roughly three to five meaningful stages rather than exposing a giant
  static checklist. A fixed premise may generate new pressures as the economy changes. The world should reveal constraints
 through counterparties, reports, shortages, labor behavior and visible conditions rather than prescribing a build order.
    • A counterparty can renegotiate, penalize, reduce, terminate or reassign a contract when the world situation supports it.
    • Failure can be graded. Missing a contract can cause lost payment, reputation damage or loss of future business without
     necessarily ending the entire save.
    • Primary scenario failure remains distinct from Commercial Ruin.
    • Completion records should acknowledge the actual economic history even when the primary target is missed.
    • Optional Distinctions can reward speed, reliability, solvency, resilience, limited ownership, local development or other
    mastery without becoming mandatory clutter.
 1.5L Deadline language
 Player-facing deadlines should use clear inclusive language: "By December 31, 1887" means the player may complete the
 requirement through that date. When the next day begins without qualification, the deadline has been missed. Avoid
 confusing constructions such as "before January 1" when the intended final valid day can be stated directly. Exact dates
 remain scenario-specific and must be historically/economically justified.

 1.5M Scenario families and cross-system focus
 Scenarios may be grouped by a primary commercial family while carrying secondary system tags. The family identifies the
  central fantasy, not a restriction on methods. Current useful families include Commerce, Transportation, Mining, Agriculture
 & Ranching, Industry, Finance, Land & Property, Settlement Development, Infrastructure and Crisis & Recovery.
 CANON LOCK - A focused scenario should still require economic interplay.

 A mining scenario can remain unmistakably about mining while making success depend on timber, tools, labor, housing,
 processing, freight and finance. A transportation scenario can remain about moving goods while forcing decisions about
  vehicles, teams, employees, contracts, backhauls, maintenance and route capacity. The player should feel that they are
 assembling a functioning commercial pipeline, not collecting required buildings.
 1.5N Settlement-development scenarios
 Settlement-development scenarios are a signature Land & Ledgers inversion of the city-builder population challenge. The
 player does not control the town by decree. The player begins with limited private authority - often one business - and must
 create enough economic gravity that households and businesses choose to arrive, remain, invest and expand.
    • Population targets are provisional tuning values, never historical claims merely because they appear in a scenario draft.
    • Growth can require jobs, accommodation, affordable goods, construction supply, freight access, credit, services,
     infrastructure and local confidence.
    • The player can buy businesses that have second-order town effects even when those businesses are not the highest
     standalone-profit investments.
    • A weak sawmill may be strategically valuable because lumber scarcity is constraining housing. A freight company may
    unlock several NPC businesses. A bank may enable outside owners to expand without the player owning them.
    • Population alone should usually be sustained for a meaningful period or paired with economic viability so a temporary
   boom does not count as durable success.
    • Possible variants include Boomtown, Gateway Settlement, Second City, Save the Town, Railway Bypass and New Depot.
 The scenario question is not "what should the mayor build?" but "why is this town failing to attract or retain people,
 and what can an owner/investor legitimately do about it?"

 15.X Historical news, legal notices and technological
 milestones
 Major public developments should be discoverable without repeatedly interrupting play. Forced full-screen newspaper
 popups are prohibited as the default presentation. The normal surface is a small, unobtrusive notification that the player may
 open for detail.
    • Qualifying news includes major federal, territorial or state legal changes; proclamations and decrees; major financial/public
     events; and important technological or transportation milestones such as notable automobile, aviation, communication or
     infrastructure developments when historically relevant.
    • News is not instantaneous omniscience. Information must travel through historically plausible channels and delay.
    • Telegraph access, newspapers, post, rail connections, civic institutions and information networks can change how quickly
    and reliably news reaches the player or settlement.
    • A town hall, courthouse, newspaper, post office, telegraph office or similar institution can become an
     information-distribution node where appropriate.
    • Routine local business events should usually remain world evidence, correspondence, ledgers, notices or reports rather
    than "breaking news."
    • The detailed news item may use a newspaper or official-notice presentation after the player chooses to open it; the game
    should not seize the screen merely because a story exists.
 CANON LOCK - Historical news follows Information Distance. A fact may be true in Washington before the player
 legitimately knows it in Dakota.





LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XV / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                 REVISION XV INTEGRATION 4

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 231/346 ====================

 9.X Portfolio logistics - ledger ownership and operational
 assignment
 Transport assets should be legally and financially owned by a specific person or business ledger while remaining
 operationally assignable across the player-controlled portfolio when authority permits. Ownership determines whose books
 carry the asset, depreciation/condition burden, feed, maintenance and financing. Operational assignment determines what
 the asset is doing now.
 CANON LOCK - Vehicles are not permanently welded to the business that owns them.

    • A dairy farm can own a cart, horse team and employ the worker while the cart performs a route serving the General Store,
     the dairy and outside counterparties.
    • Controlled wagons/carts/teams should be visible as a portfolio-wide available transport pool while retaining ledger
    ownership.
    • The player can formally transfer an asset between Ledgers when long-term use changes. The transfer should be recorded
     rather than silently rewriting ownership.
    • NPC owners with multiple businesses use the same underlying authority and asset rules, but their scheduling quality can
    vary through actual decisions rather than hidden efficiency multipliers.
 9.XA Multi-stop routes and through-cargo
 Routes may contain multiple stops and cargo may remain aboard through intermediate stops when its destination lies later in
 the route. This permits triangular and circuit logistics, backhauls and consolidation. Route orders should be policy-like rather
 than brittle scripts.
    • Examples: load up to a quantity, reserve capacity for a later pickup, keep destination-A cargo aboard while visiting B,
    depart if cargo is unavailable, wait up to a defined time, or fill remaining capacity with eligible cargo.
    • The route planner should expose expected capacity utilization, empty mileage, timing and likely bottlenecks without
    guaranteeing uncertain future inventory.
    • Cargo remains physical. Capacity, cargo compatibility, loading time, vehicle condition, weather protection and team
     availability constrain what can be moved.
    • External cargo requires a real agreement or freight contract. The player does not obtain free rights to haul NPC property
    merely because spare capacity exists.
 9.XB Fleet composition and interruptions
  Practical transport capacity is the combination of vehicle, suitable team/animal power, driver labor, route time and condition.
 Owning eight wagons does not imply eight usable departures if only six teams or qualified drivers are available. The player
 may interrupt a scheduled route for an urgent job, but missed pickups, contract breaches, shortages and schedule disruption
 remain real consequences.





LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XV / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                 REVISION XV INTEGRATION 5

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 232/346 ====================

 6.1D Cross-business labor assignment and internal
 allocation
 Employees remain employed and paid through a specific business/person ledger, but compatible labor may be temporarily
 assigned to another controlled business when authority, skill, travel and schedule permit. The game should not require
 formal rehiring for every cross-business task.
    • A store clerk who has four hours of required store work may perform compatible hauling or warehouse work during
    remaining usable labor time.
    • The cheaper worker is not automatically the best assignment: task skill, fatigue, travel, business coverage and opportunity
     cost matter.
    • Internal labor and transport use can be allocated across Ledgers so the player can see which operation is consuming
    shared capacity.
    • Owner-facing controls can support Automatic, Preferred and Manual assignment. Automatic scheduling should seek a
     sensible plan, not guarantee the globally optimal plan.
    • The player is allowed to choose a more expensive or less efficient arrangement and bear the consequences.
 6.1E Working time, overtime and cumulative strain
 Work duration is a real causal input. Ordinary workday length, occupation, season and local practice require historical
  calibration rather than assuming a universal modern eight-hour shift. When compensation rules or agreements make
 overtime appropriate, additional work should increase payroll accordingly. Regardless of overtime pay, excessively long or
 repeated shifts create human costs.
    • Longer shifts progressively increase fatigue, mistake risk, accident risk, irritability, absence pressure and turnover risk.
    • Repeated 12-16 hour days should be materially worse than an occasional long day because recovery debt accumulates.
    • Managers and automated schedules should be capable of producing imperfect staffing choices; the player can override
    them.
    • No unexplained productivity penalty is required. Reduced performance should emerge from tired people, missed coverage,
    slower work, errors, injuries or departures.





LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XV / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                 REVISION XV INTEGRATION 6

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 233/346 ====================

 13.X Sleep, nutrition, fatigue and daily time budget
 People should have a lightweight daily human-condition model connecting work, housing, food, travel and health. The
 purpose is not life-simulation micromanagement. It is to make labor capacity and household circumstances causally
 meaningful.
    • Sleep: people have restorative sleep needs/ranges. Long workdays, long commutes, poor housing, household obligations,
     noise, illness and traits such as insomnia can reduce actual recovery.
    • Nutrition: quantity, quality and regularity of food can influence energy, recovery, illness resilience and physically demanding
    work. This links wages, household budgets, boarding/meals and local food supply to labor outcomes.
    • Fatigue: accumulates from work duration, physical intensity, inadequate sleep, travel, illness and poor nutrition and
    recovers over time rather than resetting magically at midnight.
    • Commute: travel time is part of the person's day. A worker who starts at 8:00 and needs one hour to walk should normally
    depart around 7:00. Walking, horse access, wagon transport, weather, road condition and distance alter the time budget.
    • Punctuality: arrival is not perfectly deterministic. Travel disruption, fatigue, household events and behavioral traits can
    produce lateness.
 CANON LOCK - The simulation may maintain exact numerical state underneath, but the ordinary player-facing
 experience should emphasize readable causes and consequences rather than floating "-17% fatigue" modifiers.
 13.XA Mistake severity
 Work errors should be able to resolve at multiple hidden severity bands such as minor, moderate and major. Severity and
  probability depend on the actual task and circumstances. Minor outcomes can include miscounts, wasted material or small
 delays; moderate outcomes can include damaged goods, incorrect records, missed deliveries or broken tools; major
 outcomes can include serious injury, machinery damage, lost cargo or fire-causing mistakes where physically plausible.
 Relevant causal inputs can include competence, task familiarity, attention, fatigue, sleep, nutrition, shift length, supervision,
 equipment condition and environmental difficulty. The player does not need to see the hidden probability roll.





LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XV / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE                                                 REVISION XV INTEGRATION 7

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 234/346 ====================

 13.XB Employee traits, aptitudes, interests and experience
 Workers should feel distinct without becoming full RPG characters. The preferred lightweight model uses a small number of
  visible or discoverable traits, work aptitudes/interests and experience earned through actual work.
    • Traits can include Dependable, Quick Learner, Methodical, Distractible, Witty, Patient, Habitually Late, Insomniac and
     similar grounded characteristics.
    • Avoid one deterministic "Low IQ" label as a catch-all. Where cognitive differences matter, use narrower underlying qualities
    such as reasoning, numeracy, memory, attention, learning speed or practical aptitude, and surface human-readable traits
     only when known.
    • Traits may be correlated where plausible but should not be hard-paired into stereotypes. Intelligence does not inherently
    imply punctuality; conscientiousness or disorganization is a better causal route.
    • Interests can include animals, machinery, numbers, customer-facing work, outdoor work, solitary work, mining, butchery or
    a family trade/background.
    • Interest should mainly influence job attraction, retention, satisfaction and learning, with modest performance effects
    emerging through fit and experience rather than giant buffs.
    • Experience grows from real task exposure. A retained clerk, teamster, butcher, bookkeeper or foreman can become
     materially more valuable over years.
 13.XC Compensation growth, retention and poaching
 Employees are participants in a labor market. As their experience, reputation and alternatives improve, they can request
  better compensation or accept competing offers. Valuable staff should create genuine retention decisions.
    • Compensation can include wage, meals, board/lodging, bonus, schedule, stability, status/promotion, different duties and
     historically appropriate commission/profit-sharing arrangements where supported.
    • A worker may approach the employer with a raise request or report a competing offer. The owner can match, exceed,
    bonus, promote, alter duties, refuse or allow departure.
    • NPC businesses can poach player workers and the player can approach workers employed by NPC businesses.
    • Job acceptance and retention consider compensation, work conditions, hours, commute, housing, household
    circumstances, interests, employer reputation, relationships and outside alternatives.
    • Money should not solve every retention problem. A worker can prefer another occupation, safer work, shorter travel or a
     different environment.

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 235/346 ====================

 1.7E Expertise and talent recognition
 Owner Expertise may improve the player's ability to recognize useful employee information, but it must not magically improve
 the employee. A provisional expertise concept such as Talent Judgment / Eye for People can reveal progressively better
 evidence about observed workers. Final naming remains TBD.
    • Low recognition may show only public role, tenure and obvious behavior.
    • Greater expertise may reveal likely traits, work reputation, aptitude, experience, dissatisfaction or receptiveness to an offer
    where the player has a legitimate basis to know.
    • Expertise improves observation and forecast confidence; it does not create +10% worker productivity or guarantee
     recruitment.
    • Known facts remain exact when legitimately known. Uncertain retention or acceptance remains a forecast.
 13.XD Employer reputation and organizational memory
 Workers remember how employers behave. Reliable pay, reasonable treatment, promotion, kept promises and stable work
 can improve recruiting and retention. Missed payroll, chronic overwork, broken promises and poor conditions can damage
 the employer's labor-market position. The state may be numerical underneath but should normally surface through worker
 behavior, references, requests and recruiting outcomes rather than one giant reputation meter.
 REVISION XV CROSS-SYSTEM CONSEQUENCE

 These mechanics deliberately connect previously separate systems. Distant cheap housing can create long commutes; long
 commutes reduce sleep; poor sleep and long shifts increase fatigue; fatigue increases errors and turnover; labor instability
 reduces business throughput; weak throughput can create freight or supply failures; those failures can affect contracts,
 scenario objectives and settlement growth. Conversely, better scheduling, nearby accommodation, reliable food, retained
 experienced staff and intelligently shared transport capacity create real efficiency because the underlying operation
 improved.

 APPENDIX XV-A - Scenario design reference
 The Long Haul - Transportation
 A major merchant or producer offers a preferred-carrier agreement. Move a large qualifying freight volume by an inclusive
 contract date. Success depends on route design, backhauls, teams, drivers, maintenance and customer commitments.
 Gateway to the Hills - Transportation / Settlement
 A gateway settlement wants dependable links to regional production and markets. Establish reliable freight/passenger
 service and enough commercial activity to strengthen the node before a competing route captures the traffic.
 Black Hills Gold - Mining
 An investor syndicate advances capital or grants an operating interest in exchange for a defined quantity/value of
 recoverable output by a contract date. Timber, tools, labor, housing, processing and freight become natural constraints.
 The Deep Mine - Mining / Industry
 A successful mine reaches a depth/cost threshold where water, hoisting, machinery, timber and treatment threaten viability.
 Maintain commercially sustainable production through the development agreement.
 Timber Country - Lumber / Industry
 A construction/mining boom creates a large supply agreement for lumber. Logging, hauling, mill throughput, storage, drying
 and labor must support the contract.
 A Town Worth Staying In - Settlement Development
 A land company, founder group or major owners need a weak settlement to become durable before financing or promotion
 collapses. Grow and sustain population by creating jobs, housing, services and access through private economic action.
 The Panic - Finance / Crisis
 Begin in 1893 with leverage and tightening credit. A creditor workout or maturing obligations create explicit milestones.
 Survive without magical protection, using asset sales, refinancing, collections, restructuring or distressed acquisition.
 Main Street Merchant - Commerce
 A wholesaler or merchant agreement rewards reliable regional demand coverage. Scale sales while solving supplier, credit,
  freight, staffing and storage constraints.
 Iron, Wood & Steam - Infrastructure / Industry
 A railway/mining construction tender needs timber, repair work, food, lodging and freight. The player can own, contract or
 finance the pipeline but must fulfill the real project schedule.
 Second City - Settlement / Regional Power
 A remote node has strong commercial potential. Build enough economic gravity for it to become a durable second regional
 center without receiving mayoral powers or direct population placement.

  All names, dates, volumes, population thresholds and monetary values in this appendix are design examples and remain subject to
  historical research and balance calibration unless separately locked elsewhere.

 APPENDIX XV-B - Revision XV canonical locks
    • Scenarios are a flagship play pillar, not a side mode; Open Frontier remains equally important.
    • Scenario goals are world-grounded commercial outcomes with believable reasons, counterparties and inclusive "By [date]"
     deadlines.
    • Settlement-growth scenarios rely on private investment and economic gravity rather than city-builder authority.
    • Major legal/government and technological news uses passive notifications; detail is opt-in and arrival obeys Information
     Distance.
    • Controlled transport assets remain owned on a specific Ledger but may be assigned across the controlled portfolio when
     authority permits.
    • Multi-stop routes, through-cargo, backhauls and conditional capacity planning are valid logistics mechanics.
    • Employees belong to a paying/employing Ledger but compatible labor can be allocated across controlled businesses.
    • Work duration, overtime where appropriate, fatigue, sleep, nutrition, commute and punctuality are causal labor inputs.
    • Mistakes can have hidden severity bands and arise from real conditions rather than arbitrary random punishment.
    • Workers have lightweight traits, aptitudes/interests and experience; they improve through work and may demand better
    compensation.
    • Retention and poaching are two-way labor-market mechanics. Compensation is broader than wage alone.
    • Expertise may reveal talent and improve judgment; it never creates unexplained worker bonuses.
    • NPC inefficiency must come from poorer decisions/scheduling under the same rules, not hidden production penalties.
    • Numerical state may exist underneath, but player-facing presentation should emphasize human-readable causes and
    consequences.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

 The Game in One Page

 Land & Ledgers is a realism-first frontier business empire simulation set around a commercially ambitious Dakota-style
 region beginning in spring 1880. The player starts with a useful foothold and a starter business in a genuinely
 wagon-dependent regional economy, then lives through roughly twenty-five years of overlapping modernization as
 railheads approach, communication networks deepen, electric light appears, civic infrastructure accumulates, mining
 and agriculture mechanize unevenly, institutions mature and ownership grows from owner-operator to owner-manager
 and ultimately to capital command.

 Ownership, not city painting: Growth comes through land, deals, projects, retrofits, staffing, supplier choice, finance,
 acquisition and capital allocation. The player represents one actual owner/investor in the world. Direct commands
 require real authority; settlements are shaped through ownership and economic gravity rather than god-mode
 municipal power.

 A living regional economy: Households, workers, suppliers, rivals, lenders, settlements and businesses share real
 pressures. Nodes can rise, stall, decline or surpass the opening town.

 Causal modernization: History defines the capability envelope. Rail, telegraph, telephone, electricity, water, sewer,
 mining processes and farm machinery appear when date, geography, capital, demand, legal authority and network
 economics support them.

 World first, UI second: Prosperity, strain, neglect, crowding, labor stress, freight problems, infrastructure gaps and
 district change should be visible in the world before or alongside ledger explanation.

 Two flagship play structures: Scenarios provide authored, difficulty-ranked commercial challenges with objectives and
 deadlines grounded in a specific starting situation. Open Frontier provides the large randomized 1880-1905 sandbox,
 generating a different regional economy from seed while preserving the historical capability envelope. Commercial Ruin
 remains a simulation state rather than a substitute for scenario failure or sandbox choice.

 1905 frontier-industrial horizon: The authored historical envelope remains spring 1880 through 1905. Open Frontier
 normally begins in 1880 and can run through that full span; Scenarios may begin later or use shorter slices inside it.
 The strongest nodes can have rail, telephones, electric light, waterworks, banks and sophisticated mines while
 secondary towns and rural properties remain wagon-, horse-, well- and privy-dependent. Rare automobiles do not
 replace the core transport economy.

 REVISION XIV DEPTH-BALANCE DOCTRINE

  A system is not deep merely because it contains many variables, and the game is not broad merely because the Canon
  can name many businesses. Depth means the player can face meaningfully different situations inside the same system
  because demand, inputs, labor, property, information, capital, condition, timing and counterparties interact. Width
  means a genuinely different economic role has entered the simulation. Revision XIV therefore favors deepening existing
   high-value roles over adding another shallow storefront. New width should usually be promoted only when it creates a
  new economic relationship that existing systems cannot express.

 REVISION XIV SYSTEMIC SPINE

 Scarcity creates choices. Information makes those choices intelligible but imperfect. Counterparty agency makes
 external choices negotiated. Commitment gives decisions memory. Physical Truth determines whether promises can
 actually be fulfilled. Delegation determines how far the player's authority can reach. Alternatives determine bargaining
 power and resilience. Records and retained people allow organizations to persist. Failure removes options and
 recombines assets. Historical time makes delay irreversible. The design lock that follows from this is simple: progress
 should give the player control over more of the economy without ever giving them freedom from the economy.

PART I


 Product Vision & Design Doctrine What the player is becoming, what the world must feel like, and how a campaign can
 end.

  READING RULE This part is the authoritative home for the systems listed here. Related appendices compress the same
   rules for

 routing and summary; they do not override the body.

 CORE IDENTITY

 1.1 Core fantasy

 Land & Ledgers is a realism-first frontier business empire sim. The player rises from owner-operator toward
 owner-manager and then toward broader local and regional influence through business operation, land deals, repair,
 staffing, financing, supplier choice, strategic acquisition, and capital allocation. The town is not decorative; it is the
 main stage on which economic opportunity, labor strain, family burden, and regional usefulness become readable and
 playable. The player is not manually painting a town into existence. The fantasy is becoming the person who
 understands how this place works and profits by shaping it better than anyone else. Growth comes through ownership,
 deals, projects, retrofits, staffing, and capital allocation rather than click-to-place construction. The long arc moves from
 personal handling to delegation without turning businesses into passive-income abstractions. NPCs should increasingly
 feel like people living under the same economic gravity as the player rather than decorative extras.

1.1A Starting foothold, regional freedom, and settlement plurality

 The starting frontier town remains the player's first proving ground, but it is no longer treated as a permanent
 dominant-town lock. The stronger canon direction is that the player begins with one useful foothold and one starter
 business, then gradually earns the freedom to buy, shape, and test land anywhere on the regional map. Some runs may
 remain centered on the original town for decades. Other runs may see a mine camp, freight stop, farm-service cluster,
 or rail-side settlement surpass the original town in gravity, capital, and regional importance. This does not turn Land &
 Ledgers into a freeform city-builder from minute one. The player is still not painting towns into existence by decree. The
 player creates or redirects settlement by buying land, adding services, supporting housing and boarding, creating jobs,
 improving freight access, and solving real local pressures. If the underlying conditions are weak, the experiment stalls
 or fails. If the conditions are strong and the player commits enough capital and operational support, a new node can
 become a hamlet, a town, or in exceptional cases the portfolio center of the whole run.

 1.1B Player identity, authority truth, and economic power

 The player is not an abstract government and does not receive command authority merely for being the player. The
 fiction treats the player as one actual business owner, investor and contracting person, even though the interface is
 camera-led rather than dependent on a third- person avatar. Every direct action should pass an Authority Test: what
 ownership, employment, contract, tenancy, lending, investment, management, legal right or other relationship permits
 this person to make the decision? If no legitimate authority exists, the player must influence the outcome indirectly
 through purchase, negotiation, finance, market behavior, petition, franchise, right-of-way assembly, hiring, contracting
 or another historically plausible channel. Late-game power should emerge because the player genuinely controls
 capital, jobs, land, credit, freight, utilities or communication - not because a hidden player-authority level grants
 city-builder powers. Other owners, workers, households, governments and corporations retain agency and can refuse,
 compete or choose differently.

 1.2 Prestige-frontier presentation layer

 The game should present itself as practical, weathered, ambitious, and commercially young. It should feel premium and
 serious, but not theatrical. World first, UI second: a thriving business should feel busy, cared for, and confident before
 the panel tells the player why. Big actions should feel substantial without becoming tedious. Weight comes from
 presentation, staging, visible state change, restrained pacing, and clarity of consequence. Details should communicate
 use, wear, prosperity, neglect, seasonality, and pressure rather than acting as random clutter. A store with healthy
 trade should feel distinct from a weak store before any ledger tooltip is read. A prosperous boarding house, crowded
 freight yard, or overworked sawmill should communicate strain through the world itself. The UI should feel like a
 premium frontier business ledger: clean, serious, practical, and readable.

1.2A World evidence doctrine





                                                                                                     CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE 4

==================== CAN-XXXI ORIGINAL PDF PAGE 241/346 ====================

LAND & LEDGERS / REVISION XIV / CANONICAL PROJECT BIBLE



  • Important economic conditions should preferably have a readable world expression before or alongside pure UI
    explanation.

  • Prosperity, strain, neglect, crowding, labor stress, settlement instability, and district rise should appear through
    physical state, repeated behavior, and local perception.

  • UI should clarify and compress; it should not carry the whole burden of truth.

  • Physical Truth is part of world evidence: a local customer purchase, work shift, delivery or service call should
    correspond to the relevant person or transport asset actually being present and able to perform it before the
    transaction resolves.

  • Do not turn dedicated merchandise capacity into manual shelf-by-shelf furniture placement; normalized allocation
    should capture the economic decision without store-layout busywork.

  • Do not turn workload-based staffing into minute-by-minute employee micromanagement. The long-term model should
    calculate task pressure and usable labor while letting owners/managers set policy and schedules.

  • Do not mistake detailed planning for automatic implementation scope. Preserve causal design depth, then classify it
    as owner-facing, delegated execution, background abstraction or parked detail.

 1.3 Realism framework

 Every system should be checked against five realism filters. Historical plausibility asks whether the thing could happen
 in this place and time. Economic plausibility asks whether the incentives, costs, and outcomes make sense. Social
 plausibility asks whether people in this setting would behave this way. Lifecycle plausibility asks whether the rule fits
 how a household or person changes across life. Gameplay tolerance asks what the smallest bend is when pure realism
 becomes too slow, too opaque, or too punishing for strong play. That final filter matters. Land & Ledgers should be
 realism first, not realism without judgment. The goal is not museum simulation. The goal is a grounded commercial
 historical sim that remains readable, playable, and worth mastering. Growth is not automatically prosperity. More
 people, more businesses, or more building frontage can also create overextension, speculation, freight strain, labor
 distortion, and fragility. The town should be allowed to boom badly, stall awkwardly, and recover unevenly.

1.3A Three-filter design standard and freedom doctrine

 Every mechanic should also pass three standing production filters. First, historical accuracy: model what could plausibly
 happen in this place and period, and research uncertain details before inventing confidence. Second, player freedom: if
 an action is physically, legally and economically possible, prefer allowing it and letting consequences determine
 whether it was wise. The game should not forbid a store from opening at 1:00 a.m. merely because the choice is usually
 irrational; labor, lighting, customer schedules, safety and demand should decide whether it works. Third, premium
 systemic quality: aim for the depth and interconnection of a serious systems-driven strategy game with the
 presentation, world feedback and interface clarity expected from a high-end production. The player should feel free,
 informed and grounded rather than boxed into designer-approved answers. Depth-before-simplification rule: planning
 should understand the real process at high causal resolution before deciding what to abstract. A feature can later be
 cut or simplified for scope, but its surviving design should preserve the important physical and economic
 cause-and-effect rather than replacing reality with arbitrary bonuses.

 1.4 Anti-drift rules

 Do not reduce households to decorative customers or population filler. Do not reduce women to static domestic tags;
 treat wage work, boarding, teaching, widow ownership, and household labor as real mechanics. Do not treat
 professions as permanent immutable classes; age, injury, literacy, marriage, opportunity, and migration should matter.
 Do not make property automatically market-available just because the player wants it. Do not let acquisition bypass
 seriousness, seller motive, financing credibility, inherited problems, or rival pressure. Do not impose modern
 zoning-style restrictions when suitability, nuisance, frontage, adjacency, and conversion cost are the better answer. Do
 not let seasons become cosmetic reskins of the same loop. Do not let notices, Opportunity & Pressure, or recurring local
 orders feel detached from the underlying town simulation. Do not make ordinary actions slow for the sake of slowness.
 Favor grounded presentation over friction tax. Do not let rivals act without believable economic cause. Do not let
 off-map actors feel magical; outside finance, supply, and competition should still leave readable local effects. Do not let
 takeovers erase inherited weakness. Do not let notices surface raw abstract scores without human-readable causes. Do
 not assume all growth is healthy simply because counts went up. Do not use artificial prohibitions to keep the player
 inside an intended strategy when the action is historically and physically possible; let bad hours, bad allocation, bad
 credit policy, overstaffing, underpricing and other poor choices fail through their consequences. Do not grant
 city-builder god powers that the owner character has no legal or economic authority to exercise.

1.4A Design derivation rule

  • Do not begin new mechanics from abstract feature brainstorming.
